**5.4 Waiver of Unknown Claims.** Each Party acknowledges and agrees that it or he may discover facts, claims, or legal theories in addition to or different from those that it or he now knows or believes to be true with respect to the Released Claims, and each Party expressly agrees that this release shall be and remain effective in all respects notwithstanding the subsequent discovery of such additional or different facts, claims, or legal theories. Each Party hereby waives, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, any and all rights it or he may have under any statute, regulation, or common-law principle that would otherwise limit a release to those claims actually known or suspected to exist at the time of execution of the release. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, each Party expressly acknowledges that this waiver is knowingly and voluntarily made and is an essential term of this Agreement.
**[ARTICLE VI --- NON-SOLICITATION COVENANT]{.underline}**

**6.1 Non-Solicitation.** For a period of five (5) years commencing on the Effective Date and ending on September 12, 2029 (the \"**Non-Solicitation Period**\"), the Harlow Parties and each of their respective Affiliates, agents, officers, directors, employees, representatives, contractors, successors, and assigns shall not, directly or indirectly, whether on their own behalf or on behalf of any other person or entity, solicit, contact, call upon, market to, sell to, supply to, bid for the business of, or otherwise attempt to transact business with any CPS Current Customer (as defined in Section 1.7 and as identified and listed on Exhibit A attached hereto) with respect to any barrier coating, laminate, packaging substrate, or any product that is the same as, substantially similar to, or competitive with any product manufactured, formulated, marketed, or sold by CPS as of the Effective Date, without the prior written consent of CPS.

**6.2 Scope of Covenant.** The non-solicitation covenant set forth in Section 6.1 applies to all CPS Current Customers as of the Effective Date, as identified on Exhibit A. CPS shall deliver Exhibit A (the list of CPS Current Customers) to the Harlow Parties concurrently with the execution of this Agreement. The Parties acknowledge that the list of CPS Current Customers set forth on Exhibit A is not intended to be exhaustive and that CPS reserves the right to supplement Exhibit A within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date to include any additional customers inadvertently omitted, provided that any such supplement shall be subject to the reasonable good-faith objection of the Harlow Parties. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Article VI shall restrict the Harlow Parties from selling products that are not barrier coatings, laminates, or packaging substrates (or products substantially similar thereto) to any CPS Current Customer, or from responding to unsolicited inquiries from CPS Current Customers with respect to products other than barrier coatings, laminates, and packaging substrates.

**6.3 Reasonableness.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that the duration, geographic scope, and subject matter scope of the non-solicitation covenant set forth in this Article VI are reasonable and necessary to protect CPS\'s legitimate business interests, including its trade secrets, proprietary formulations, customer relationships, and goodwill. The Harlow Parties acknowledge that they have received independent legal advice regarding the enforceability and reasonableness of this covenant.

**6.4 Remedies.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that any breach or threatened breach of this Article VI would cause irreparable harm to CPS for which monetary damages alone would not provide an adequate remedy. Accordingly, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity, in the event of any actual or threatened breach of this Article VI, CPS shall be entitled to seek and obtain temporary, preliminary, and permanent injunctive relief, specific performance, and an equitable accounting of all profits earned by the Harlow Parties in connection with any such breach, as well as recovery of its reasonable attorneys\' fees, costs, and expenses incurred in enforcing the provisions of this Article VI. The Harlow Parties agree that CPS shall not be required to post a bond or other security as a condition to obtaining any such injunctive relief, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.
**[ARTICLE VII --- NO ADMISSION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**

**7.1 No Admission.** This Agreement represents a compromise and settlement of disputed claims. The Parties have entered into this Agreement to avoid the burden, expense, distraction, and uncertainty of continued litigation, and for no other reason. Nothing in this Agreement, including without limitation the payment of the Settlement Payment, the agreement to injunctive relief, the return and destruction of materials, or any other term or provision hereof, shall be deemed, construed, or interpreted as an admission of liability, wrongdoing, fault, or the merit or lack of merit of any claim or defense by any Party, and specifically not by the Harlow Parties. The Harlow Parties expressly deny all allegations of wrongdoing and liability asserted by CPS in the Action and otherwise, and enter into this Agreement solely to resolve the disputes between the Parties and to avoid the continued costs and burdens of litigation.

**7.2 Inadmissibility.** This Agreement and the Settlement Payment shall not be offered or received in evidence in any legal, administrative, regulatory, or other proceeding as an admission, concession, or evidence of liability, wrongdoing, or fault on the part of any Party, except as may be necessary to enforce the terms of this Agreement or to support a defense of res judicata, collateral estoppel, release, or other similar defense. The provisions of Federal Rule of Evidence 408 and any analogous state evidentiary rule shall apply to this Agreement and all negotiations and communications leading to its execution.
**[ARTICLE VIII --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**8.1 Confidentiality of Settlement Terms.** The Parties agree that the existence and terms of this Agreement, including without limitation the Payment Amount, the specific injunctive relief provisions, the non-solicitation covenant, and all other specific terms, conditions, and provisions hereof, shall be kept strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed, revealed, or communicated to any third party, except as expressly permitted by Section 8.2 of this Agreement. Each Party shall instruct its respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives who become aware of the terms of this Agreement to maintain the confidentiality of such terms in accordance with this Article VIII.
**8.2 Permitted Disclosures.** Notwithstanding Section 8.1, a Party may disclose the existence and/or terms of this Agreement under the following circumstances:

> \(a\) **Financial and Tax Advisors.** To its auditors, accountants, financial advisors, and tax advisors, to the extent reasonably necessary for financial reporting, audit, and tax compliance purposes, provided that such recipients are informed of the confidential nature of the information and agree to maintain its confidentiality;

> \(b\) **Legal Compulsion.** As required by applicable law, regulation, governmental order, court order, or subpoena, provided that the disclosing Party gives the other Parties prompt written notice (to the extent legally permissible and practicable) of such requirement prior to making any such disclosure and cooperates reasonably with the other Parties in seeking a protective order, confidentiality agreement, or other appropriate remedy to limit the scope and dissemination of any such disclosure;

> \(c\) **Legal Counsel.** To its legal counsel in connection with the enforcement, interpretation, or defense of this Agreement, or in connection with legal proceedings arising out of or relating to this Agreement;

> \(d\) **Insurance Carriers.** To its insurance carriers and their agents and representatives, to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with any applicable insurance policy, coverage determination, or claim for coverage, provided that such recipients are informed of the confidential nature of the information;

> \(e\) **CPS\'s Equity Sponsor and Lender.** In the case of CPS, to Ridgepoint Capital Partners LP (CPS\'s equity sponsor), its officers, directors, partners, members, employees, and advisors, and to Keystone Commerce Bank (CPS\'s senior secured lender) and its officers, employees, agents, and representatives, in each case to the extent reasonably necessary for business, financial reporting, and compliance purposes, and in each case subject to obligations of confidentiality at least as restrictive as those set forth in this Article VIII; and

> \(f\) **Successors and Acquirors.** In the case of Harlow, to any bona fide successor-in-interest or prospective acquiror of Harlow or substantially all of its assets, in connection with a potential acquisition, merger, or similar transaction, provided that any such disclosure is made subject to a written confidentiality agreement containing restrictions no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article VIII and that Harlow provides CPS with prior written notice (which may be general in nature and need not identify the prospective acquiror) of its intent to make such disclosure at least ten (10) business days before any such disclosure is made.

**8.3 Breach of Confidentiality.** Any breach of this Article VIII shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement and shall entitle the non-breaching Party or Parties to all available remedies, including without limitation injunctive relief, specific performance, and damages (including consequential damages to the extent proximately caused by such breach). The Parties acknowledge and agree that any unauthorized disclosure of the terms of this Agreement would cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages alone would not provide an adequate remedy.

**8.4 Public Statements.** In the event that any Party receives an inquiry from a member of the media, an industry publication, or any other third party regarding the Action or its resolution, such Party shall limit its response to a statement substantially as follows: \"The matter has been resolved to the satisfaction of all parties.\" No Party shall make any public statement that is inconsistent with the foregoing or that disparages any other Party in connection with the Action, the TMA, or the subject matter of this Agreement.
**[ARTICLE IX --- DISMISSAL OF THE ACTION]{.underline}**

**9.1 Stipulation of Dismissal.** Within five (5) business days following receipt by CPS of the full Payment Amount in immediately available funds, the Parties shall jointly execute and cause to be filed with the Clerk of the Court a Stipulation and Order of Dismissal with Prejudice in the Action (Case No. 2:24-cv-00891) before the Honorable Judge Patricia Langford, United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio, Eastern Division, stipulating to the dismissal with prejudice of all claims, counterclaims, and cross-claims asserted in the Action, each Party to bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement. Counsel for CPS shall be responsible for filing the executed Stipulation and Order of Dismissal with the Court.

2: ===== documents/matters/1005-00005/Settlement/letter-ridgecrest-settlement-notice.docx =====
3: **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Attorneys at Law*
4: 
5: 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 4400 Chicago, Illinois 60606 Telephone: (312) 555-7800 Facsimile: (312) 555-7801 www.calderwoodharkness.com
6: 
7: August 21, 2023
8: 
9: Ms. Karen Whitmore Relationship Manager Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. 120 North LaSalle Street Chicago, Illinois 60602
10: 
11: **Re: Notice Pursuant to Section 6.03(b) of Credit Agreement --- Settlement of Litigation by Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.**
12: 
13: > Credit Agreement: \$45,000,000 Revolving Credit Facility, dated as of March 12, 2021, by and between Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. (as Borrower) and Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. (as Administrative Agent and Lender) (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"Credit Agreement\")
14: >
15: > Calderwood & Harkness Matter No. 1005-00005
16: 
17: Dear Ms. Whitmore:
18: 
19: **[I. Purpose of This Letter and Legal Basis for Notice]{.underline}**
20: 
21: Calderwood & Harkness LLP writes on behalf of its client, Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. (\"Nexford\" or the \"Borrower\"), a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal executive offices located at 4200 West Lakeshore Industrial Parkway, Suite 300, Waukegan, Illinois 60085 (Employer Identification Number: 36-4821097; Delaware Charter No. 7284159). This firm serves as outside litigation counsel to Nexford in connection with the matter described herein and has been authorized by the Borrower to deliver this notice on its behalf.
22: 
23: The purpose of this letter is to provide formal written notice to Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A., in its capacity as Administrative Agent under the Credit Agreement (the \"Administrative Agent\"), pursuant to Section 6.03(b) of that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of March 12, 2021, by and between the Borrower and Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"Credit Agreement\"), governing the \$45,000,000 revolving credit facility made available to the Borrower thereunder. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Credit Agreement.
24: 
25: As you are aware, Section 6.03(b) of the Credit Agreement requires the Borrower to promptly notify the Administrative Agent in writing of any settlement of litigation, arbitration, or other legal proceedings involving the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries where the aggregate settlement amount, including any amounts payable by or on behalf of the Borrower in connection therewith, exceeds One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000). The settlement described in detail below meets and exceeds that threshold, and accordingly this letter is being delivered to satisfy the Borrower\'s notice obligation under Section 6.03(b). The Borrower believes that this notice is being provided promptly following the execution of the definitive settlement documentation and well within the time period contemplated by the Credit Agreement.
26: 
27: **[II. Description of the Underlying Litigation]{.underline}**
28: 
29: **A. Case Caption and Parties**
30: 
31: The litigation that is the subject of this notice was captioned as follows:
32: 
33: **Cardinal Peak Industries v. Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.** Case No. 2022-L-008471 Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois County Department, Law Division
34: 
35: The plaintiff in the action was Cardinal Peak Industries (\"Cardinal Peak\" or \"CPI\"), a Colorado limited liability company with its principal place of business at 1580 Ridgeline Boulevard, Pueblo, Colorado 81001. Cardinal Peak is a domestic producer and distributor of flat-rolled steel products, including hot-rolled coil and cold-rolled coil products used in industrial manufacturing applications.
36: 
37: The defendant in the action was Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc., the Borrower under the Credit Agreement.
38: 
39: **B. Counsel of Record**
40: 
41: Cardinal Peak was represented by the law firm of Blackwood Stein & Associates LLP, located at 717 Seventeenth Street, Suite 2200, Denver, Colorado 80202. The lead partner responsible for the prosecution of the matter on behalf of Cardinal Peak was Garrett Blackwood.
42: 
43: Nexford was represented in its defense by this firm, Calderwood & Harkness LLP. The responsible partner for the matter was Priya Anand, and the billing partner was Douglas Carmichael, both of the firm\'s Chicago office.
44: 
45: **C. Nature of the Dispute**
46: 
47: The dispute arose from a pricing disagreement between the parties under a Master Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2020 (MSA Reference No. MSA-NIH-CPI-2020-001) (the \"MSA\"), pursuant to which Nexford, in its capacity as buyer, purchased hot-rolled coil (\"HRC\") and cold-rolled coil (\"CRC\") steel products from Cardinal Peak, in its capacity as seller. Specifically, the dispute centered on contested raw-material surcharge pass-throughs that Cardinal Peak sought to impose on Nexford during a period of significant volatility in raw-material input costs, particularly in the pricing of iron ore, metallurgical coal, and zinc used in the production of flat-rolled steel products.
48: 
49: Cardinal Peak contended that it was contractually entitled, under Section 7.4 of the MSA, to pass through to Nexford certain increases in its raw-material input costs in the form of surcharges applied to the base price of HRC and CRC products. Nexford disputed both the methodology employed by Cardinal Peak in calculating those surcharges and the procedural manner in which the surcharges were communicated and invoiced.
50: 
51: **D. Claims Asserted by Cardinal Peak**
52: 
53: Cardinal Peak\'s complaint, filed on August 8, 2022, asserted three causes of action against Nexford:
54: 
55: > 1\. **Breach of Contract** --- Cardinal Peak alleged that Nexford breached its obligations under the MSA by failing and refusing to pay invoiced surcharges on shipments of HRC and CRC products delivered during the period from March 2021 through May 2022, and that such refusal constituted a material breach of Sections 7.4 and 8.1 of the MSA.
56: >
57: > 2\. **Unjust Enrichment** --- Cardinal Peak alleged, in the alternative, that Nexford was unjustly enriched by receiving steel products at prices that did not reflect the true cost of raw-material inputs borne by Cardinal Peak, and that equity and good conscience required Nexford to compensate Cardinal Peak for the difference.
58: >
59: > 3\. **Account Stated** --- Cardinal Peak alleged that the invoices it issued to Nexford for the disputed surcharges were received, retained, and not objected to within a commercially reasonable time, and therefore constituted an account stated binding upon Nexford.
60: 
61: **E. Claimed Damages**
62: 
63: Cardinal Peak\'s complaint sought recovery of the following amounts:
64: 
65: > • Unpaid surcharges for the period March 2021 through May 2022: **\$4,730,000**
66: >
67: > • Prejudgment interest on unpaid surcharges: **\$380,000**
68: >
69: > • **Total claimed damages: \$5,110,000**
70: 
71: Cardinal Peak also sought recovery of its reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs of litigation pursuant to the fee-shifting provision in Section 14.6 of the MSA, as well as such other and further relief as the Court deemed just and proper.
72: 
73: **F. Nexford\'s Defenses and Counterclaim**
74: 
75: Nexford filed its Answer and Affirmative Defenses on September 19, 2022, denying the material allegations of the complaint and asserting several affirmative defenses, including the following:
76: 
77: > • **Failure to Comply with Contractual Notice Requirements.** Nexford asserted that Cardinal Peak failed to comply with the mandatory written notice requirements set forth in Section 7.4(a) of the MSA, which required Cardinal Peak to provide Nexford with no less than forty-five (45) days\' prior written notice of any proposed surcharge adjustment, accompanied by supporting documentation demonstrating the basis for the adjustment and the methodology used to calculate it. Nexford contended that Cardinal Peak\'s notices were untimely, incomplete, and did not include the requisite supporting documentation.
78: >
79: > • **Deviation from Agreed Surcharge Methodology.** Nexford asserted that Cardinal Peak deviated from the Surcharge Methodology set forth in Exhibit C to the MSA, which established a specific formula for calculating permissible surcharges based on published index prices for raw-material inputs. Nexford contended that Cardinal Peak unilaterally substituted its own internal cost data for the agreed-upon published index references, resulting in surcharges that were materially inflated and inconsistent with the parties\' bargained-for pricing structure.
80: >
81: > • **Exceeded Surcharge Cap Without Written Consent.** Nexford asserted that numerous surcharges invoiced by Cardinal Peak exceeded the twelve percent (12%) cap on aggregate surcharge increases established by Section 7.4(c) of the MSA, and that Cardinal Peak failed to obtain Nexford\'s prior written consent before imposing surcharges in excess of that cap, as expressly required by the MSA.
82: 
83: In addition, on October 3, 2022, Nexford filed a counterclaim against Cardinal Peak seeking: (i) a declaratory judgment that Cardinal Peak\'s surcharges were not properly imposed under the terms of the MSA; and (ii) recovery of approximately \$210,000 in alleged overpayments that Nexford had made to Cardinal Peak on invoices that included improperly calculated surcharges during the early months of the disputed period, before Nexford commenced its practice of withholding payment on the disputed surcharge amounts.
84: 
85: **[III. Procedural History Leading to Settlement]{.underline}**
86: 
87: Following the close of pleadings in November 2022, the litigation proceeded through several phases of discovery and motion practice.
88: 
89: **Written discovery and Depositions (December 2022 -- April 2023).** The parties engaged in extensive written discovery, exchanging document productions relating to the MSA, the surcharge invoices, the Exhibit C Surcharge Methodology, internal pricing analyses, and correspondence between the parties\' respective procurement and commercial departments. The combined document production exceeded 48,000 pages. The parties also conducted a total of six fact-witness depositions, including depositions of key commercial personnel from both Nexford and Cardinal Peak who were directly involved in the administration of the MSA and the surcharge disputes.
90: 
91: **Expert Reports (March -- April 2023).** Each party retained damages experts. Cardinal Peak\'s expert, a forensic accountant, submitted a report quantifying the claimed unpaid surcharges and prejudgment interest. Nexford\'s expert, an industry pricing consultant with specific expertise in flat-rolled steel surcharge methodologies, submitted a rebuttal report concluding that Cardinal Peak\'s surcharges deviated materially from the Exhibit C Surcharge Methodology and that, had the correct methodology been applied, the aggregate surcharges for the relevant period would have been approximately \$1.6 million less than the amount invoiced by Cardinal Peak.
92: 
93: **Mandatory Mediation.** Section 14.3 of the MSA contained a mandatory mediation provision requiring the parties to submit any unresolved dispute to non-binding mediation prior to proceeding to trial. On May 22, 2023, the parties filed a joint motion to stay litigation pending completion of mandatory mediation pursuant to MSA Section 14.3. The Court entered an order granting the joint motion on June 5, 2023, staying all proceedings and deadlines pending the conclusion of the mediation process.
94: 
95: **Mediation Proceedings.** A full-day mediation session was conducted on August 2, 2023, before the Honorable Catherine Lindström (Ret.) at the Great Lakes Dispute Resolution Center, located at 150 North Riverside Plaza, Suite 2700, Chicago, Illinois 60606. Judge Lindström, a former Justice of the Illinois Appellate Court with extensive experience mediating complex commercial disputes, conducted separate caucuses with the parties and their counsel throughout the day. After extensive arm\'s-length negotiations, the parties reached a settlement in principle at the conclusion of the mediation session. A term sheet memorializing the essential terms of the settlement was signed by authorized representatives of both Nexford and Cardinal Peak on August 2, 2023.
96: 
97: **[IV. Terms of the Settlement]{.underline}**
98: 
99: **A. Definitive Settlement Documentation**
100: 
101: Following execution of the term sheet, the parties and their respective counsel negotiated the terms of a formal Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (the \"Settlement Agreement\"), which was fully executed by both parties on August 18, 2023. A copy of the executed Settlement Agreement is enclosed herewith for the Administrative Agent\'s records, subject to the confidentiality restrictions described below in Section IV.F.
102: 
103: **B. Settlement Amount**
104: 
105: The total settlement amount payable by Nexford to Cardinal Peak under the Settlement Agreement is **One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000)**. This amount represents approximately forty percent (40%) of Cardinal Peak\'s claimed \$4,730,000 in allegedly unpaid surcharges, and reflects a substantial discount from the total claimed damages of \$5,110,000 (inclusive of prejudgment interest). 363: 
364: > *\"A general release does not extend to claims that the creditor or releasing party does not know or suspect to exist in his or her favor at the time of executing the release and that, if known by him or her, would have materially affected his or her settlement with the debtor or released party.\"*
365: 
366: Each Party understands the significance of this waiver of unknown claims and acknowledges that it has been advised by its legal counsel with respect thereto and assumes the risk that facts additional to or different from those that it now knows or believes to be true may later be discovered, and agrees that this Agreement shall be and remain effective in all respects regardless of the discovery of any such additional or different facts.
367: 
368: **3.4 No Admission of Liability.** This Agreement, and the settlement and releases reflected herein, do not constitute and shall not be construed as an admission of liability, wrongdoing, fault, or responsibility by either Party or any of their respective Released Parties. Neither Party admits that any of the claims, counterclaims, defenses, or affirmative defenses asserted in the Litigation have merit or lack merit. This Agreement is entered into solely for the purpose of settling disputed claims and avoiding the uncertainty, expense, and burden of continued litigation. This Agreement, and any statements made or acts performed in connection with the negotiation or execution hereof, shall not be offered or received in evidence in any action or proceeding of any kind as an admission or concession of liability or wrongdoing of any nature, and shall not be admissible for any purpose other than to enforce the terms of this Agreement.
369: 
370: **[ARTICLE 4 --- DISMISSAL OF LITIGATION]{.underline}**
371: 
372: **4.1 Stipulation of Dismissal.** Within five (5) business days following the Effective Date, counsel for the Parties shall jointly prepare, execute, and file with the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, a Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice of all claims and counterclaims pending in the Litigation, Case No. 2022-L-008471, in a form substantially consistent with the requirements of the Illinois Code of Civil Procedure and the local rules of the Circuit Court of Cook County. The Stipulation of Dismissal shall provide that each Party shall bear its own attorneys\' fees, costs, and expenses incurred in connection with the Litigation.

374: **4.2 Cooperation.** Each Party shall cooperate fully with the other Party, and shall execute and deliver such further documents and instruments as may be reasonably necessary or appropriate, to effectuate the dismissal of the Litigation in accordance with Section 4.1, including without limitation any agreed orders, stipulations, or other filings required by the Court.
375: 
376: **4.3 Court Retention of Jurisdiction.** Notwithstanding the dismissal of the Litigation with prejudice, the Parties agree that the Stipulation of Dismissal shall expressly provide that the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, shall retain jurisdiction solely for the purpose of enforcing the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including but not limited to the payment obligations set forth in Article 2 and the confidentiality obligations set forth in Article 6. Either Party may apply to the Court for enforcement of this Agreement without the necessity of filing a new action or proceeding.

379:

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Attorneys at Law*
200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 4400 Chicago, Illinois 60606 Telephone: (312) 555-7800 Facsimile: (312) 555-7801 www.calderwoodharkness.com
August 21, 2023
Ms. Karen Whitmore Relationship Manager Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. 120 North LaSalle Street Chicago, Illinois 60602
**Re: Notice Pursuant to Section 6.03(b) of Credit Agreement --- Settlement of Litigation by Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.**

> Credit Agreement: \$45,000,000 Revolving Credit Facility, dated as of March 12, 2021, by and between Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. (as Borrower) and Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. (as Administrative Agent and Lender) (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"Credit Agreement\")
> Calderwood & Harkness Matter No. 1005-00005
Dear Ms. Whitmore:
**[I. Purpose of This Letter and Legal Basis for Notice]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP writes on behalf of its client, Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. (\"Nexford\" or the \"Borrower\"), a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal executive offices located at 4200 West Lakeshore Industrial Parkway, Suite 300, Waukegan, Illinois 60085 (Employer Identification Number: 36-4821097; Delaware Charter No. 7284159). This firm serves as outside litigation counsel to Nexford in connection with the matter described herein and has been authorized by the Borrower to deliver this notice on its behalf.

The purpose of this letter is to provide formal written notice to Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A., in its capacity as Administrative Agent under the Credit Agreement (the \"Administrative Agent\"), pursuant to Section 6.03(b) of that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of March 12, 2021, by and between the Borrower and Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"Credit Agreement\"), governing the \$45,000,000 revolving credit facility made available to the Borrower thereunder. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Credit Agreement.

As you are aware, Section 6.03(b) of the Credit Agreement requires the Borrower to promptly notify the Administrative Agent in writing of any settlement of litigation, arbitration, or other legal proceedings involving the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries where the aggregate settlement amount, including any amounts payable by or on behalf of the Borrower in connection therewith, exceeds One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000). The settlement described in detail below meets and exceeds that threshold, and accordingly this letter is being delivered to satisfy the Borrower\'s notice obligation under Section 6.03(b). The Borrower believes that this notice is being provided promptly following the execution of the definitive settlement documentation and well within the time period contemplated by the Credit Agreement.
**[II. Description of the Underlying Litigation]{.underline}**
**A. Case Caption and Parties**
The litigation that is the subject of this notice was captioned as follows:
**Cardinal Peak Industries v. Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.** Case No. 2022-L-008471 Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois County Department, Law Division

The plaintiff in the action was Cardinal Peak Industries (\"Cardinal Peak\" or \"CPI\"), a Colorado limited liability company with its principal place of business at 1580 Ridgeline Boulevard, Pueblo, Colorado 81001. Cardinal Peak is a domestic producer and distributor of flat-rolled steel products, including hot-rolled coil and cold-rolled coil products used in industrial manufacturing applications.
The defendant in the action was Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc., the Borrower under the Credit Agreement.
**B. Counsel of Record**

Cardinal Peak was represented by the law firm of Blackwood Stein & Associates LLP, located at 717 Seventeenth Street, Suite 2200, Denver, Colorado 80202. The lead partner responsible for the prosecution of the matter on behalf of Cardinal Peak was Garrett Blackwood.

Nexford was represented in its defense by this firm, Calderwood & Harkness LLP. The responsible partner for the matter was Priya Anand, and the billing partner was Douglas Carmichael, both of the firm\'s Chicago office.
**C. Nature of the Dispute**

The dispute arose from a pricing disagreement between the parties under a Master Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2020 (MSA Reference No. MSA-NIH-CPI-2020-001) (the \"MSA\"), pursuant to which Nexford, in its capacity as buyer, purchased hot-rolled coil (\"HRC\") and cold-rolled coil (\"CRC\") steel products from Cardinal Peak, in its capacity as seller. Specifically, the dispute centered on contested raw-material surcharge pass-throughs that Cardinal Peak sought to impose on Nexford during a period of significant volatility in raw-material input costs, particularly in the pricing of iron ore, metallurgical coal, and zinc used in the production of flat-rolled steel products.

Cardinal Peak contended that it was contractually entitled, under Section 7.4 of the MSA, to pass through to Nexford certain increases in its raw-material input costs in the form of surcharges applied to the base price of HRC and CRC products. Nexford disputed both the methodology employed by Cardinal Peak in calculating those surcharges and the procedural manner in which the surcharges were communicated and invoiced.
**D. Claims Asserted by Cardinal Peak**
Cardinal Peak\'s complaint, filed on August 8, 2022, asserted three causes of action against Nexford:

> 1\. **Breach of Contract** --- Cardinal Peak alleged that Nexford breached its obligations under the MSA by failing and refusing to pay invoiced surcharges on shipments of HRC and CRC products delivered during the period from March 2021 through May 2022, and that such refusal constituted a material breach of Sections 7.4 and 8.1 of the MSA.

> 2\. **Unjust Enrichment** --- Cardinal Peak alleged, in the alternative, that Nexford was unjustly enriched by receiving steel products at prices that did not reflect the true cost of raw-material inputs borne by Cardinal Peak, and that equity and good conscience required Nexford to compensate Cardinal Peak for the difference.

> 3\. **Account Stated** --- Cardinal Peak alleged that the invoices it issued to Nexford for the disputed surcharges were received, retained, and not objected to within a commercially reasonable time, and therefore constituted an account stated binding upon Nexford.
**E. Claimed Damages**
Cardinal Peak\'s complaint sought recovery of the following amounts:
> • Unpaid surcharges for the period March 2021 through May 2022: **\$4,730,000**
> • Prejudgment interest on unpaid surcharges: **\$380,000**
> • **Total claimed damages: \$5,110,000**

Cardinal Peak also sought recovery of its reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs of litigation pursuant to the fee-shifting provision in Section 14.6 of the MSA, as well as such other and further relief as the Court deemed just and proper.
**F. Nexford\'s Defenses and Counterclaim**
Nexford filed its Answer and Affirmative Defenses on September 19, 2022, denying the material allegations of the complaint and asserting several affirmative defenses, including the following:

> • **Failure to Comply with Contractual Notice Requirements.** Nexford asserted that Cardinal Peak failed to comply with the mandatory written notice requirements set forth in Section 7.4(a) of the MSA, which required Cardinal Peak to provide Nexford with no less than forty-five (45) days\' prior written notice of any proposed surcharge adjustment, accompanied by supporting documentation demonstrating the basis for the adjustment and the methodology used to calculate it. Nexford contended that Cardinal Peak\'s notices were untimely, incomplete, and did not include the requisite supporting documentation.

> • **Deviation from Agreed Surcharge Methodology.** Nexford asserted that Cardinal Peak deviated from the Surcharge Methodology set forth in Exhibit C to the MSA, which established a specific formula for calculating permissible surcharges based on published index prices for raw-material inputs. Nexford contended that Cardinal Peak unilaterally substituted its own internal cost data for the agreed-upon published index references, resulting in surcharges that were materially inflated and inconsistent with the parties\' bargained-for pricing structure.

> • **Exceeded Surcharge Cap Without Written Consent.** Nexford asserted that numerous surcharges invoiced by Cardinal Peak exceeded the twelve percent (12%) cap on aggregate surcharge increases established by Section 7.4(c) of the MSA, and that Cardinal Peak failed to obtain Nexford\'s prior written consent before imposing surcharges in excess of that cap, as expressly required by the MSA.

In addition, on October 3, 2022, Nexford filed a counterclaim against Cardinal Peak seeking: (i) a declaratory judgment that Cardinal Peak\'s surcharges were not properly imposed under the terms of the MSA; and (ii) recovery of approximately \$210,000 in alleged overpayments that Nexford had made to Cardinal Peak on invoices that included improperly calculated surcharges during the early months of the disputed period, before Nexford commenced its practice of withholding payment on the disputed surcharge amounts.
**[III. Procedural History Leading to Settlement]{.underline}**
Following the close of pleadings in November 2022, the litigation proceeded through several phases of discovery and motion practice.

**Written discovery and Depositions (December 2022 -- April 2023).** The parties engaged in extensive written discovery, exchanging document productions relating to the MSA, the surcharge invoices, the Exhibit C Surcharge Methodology, internal pricing analyses, and correspondence between the parties\' respective procurement and commercial departments. The combined document production exceeded 48,000 pages. The parties also conducted a total of six fact-witness depositions, including depositions of key commercial personnel from both Nexford and Cardinal Peak who were directly involved in the administration of the MSA and the surcharge disputes.

**Expert Reports (March -- April 2023).** Each party retained damages experts. Cardinal Peak\'s expert, a forensic accountant, submitted a report quantifying the claimed unpaid surcharges and prejudgment interest. Nexford\'s expert, an industry pricing consultant with specific expertise in flat-rolled steel surcharge methodologies, submitted a rebuttal report concluding that Cardinal Peak\'s surcharges deviated materially from the Exhibit C Surcharge Methodology and that, had the correct methodology been applied, the aggregate surcharges for the relevant period would have been approximately \$1.6 million less than the amount invoiced by Cardinal Peak.

**Mandatory Mediation.** Section 14.3 of the MSA contained a mandatory mediation provision requiring the parties to submit any unresolved dispute to non-binding mediation prior to proceeding to trial. On May 22, 2023, the parties filed a joint motion to stay litigation pending completion of mandatory mediation pursuant to MSA Section 14.3. The Court entered an order granting the joint motion on June 5, 2023, staying all proceedings and deadlines pending the conclusion of the mediation process.

**Mediation Proceedings.** A full-day mediation session was conducted on August 2, 2023, before the Honorable Catherine Lindström (Ret.) at the Great Lakes Dispute Resolution Center, located at 150 North Riverside Plaza, Suite 2700, Chicago, Illinois 60606. Judge Lindström, a former Justice of the Illinois Appellate Court with extensive experience mediating complex commercial disputes, conducted separate caucuses with the parties and their counsel throughout the day. After extensive arm\'s-length negotiations, the parties reached a settlement in principle at the conclusion of the mediation session. A term sheet memorializing the essential terms of the settlement was signed by authorized representatives of both Nexford and Cardinal Peak on August 2, 2023.
**[IV. Terms of the Settlement]{.underline}**
**A. Definitive Settlement Documentation**

Following execution of the term sheet, the parties and their respective counsel negotiated the terms of a formal Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (the \"Settlement Agreement\"), which was fully executed by both parties on August 18, 2023. A copy of the executed Settlement Agreement is enclosed herewith for the Administrative Agent\'s records, subject to the confidentiality restrictions described below in Section IV.F.
**B. Settlement Amount**

The total settlement amount payable by Nexford to Cardinal Peak under the Settlement Agreement is **One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000)**. This amount represents approximately forty percent (40%) of Cardinal Peak\'s claimed \$4,730,000 in allegedly unpaid surcharges, and reflects a substantial discount from the total claimed damages of \$5,110,000 (inclusive of prejudgment interest). Nexford\'s litigation counsel and management believe this result represents a favorable outcome for the Borrower, particularly in light of the inherent risks and costs of continued litigation and trial.
**C. Payment Structure**
The settlement amount is payable in two installments, as follows:
**Installment**   **Amount**        **Percentage of Total**   **Due Date**
Installment 1     \$1,134,000       60%                       September 17, 2023 (30 days after execution)
Installment 2     \$756,000         40%                       November 16, 2023 (90 days after execution)

The Settlement Agreement provides that failure by Nexford to make either installment payment when due (subject to a five-business-day cure period following written notice from Cardinal Peak) would constitute a breach of the Settlement Agreement, potentially entitling Cardinal Peak to pursue enforcement of the settlement and to seek entry of a consent judgment in the amount of the unpaid balance, plus interest at the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum from the date of default.
**D. Notice Threshold**

The Administrative Agent will note that the aggregate settlement amount of \$1,890,000 exceeds the \$1,000,000 notice threshold set forth in Section 6.03(b) of the Credit Agreement. Accordingly, this notice is being provided in satisfaction of the Borrower\'s obligation under that section.
**E. Mutual Release and No Admission of Liability**

Under the terms of the Settlement Agreement, Nexford and Cardinal Peak have exchanged full and mutual general releases, releasing each other and their respective affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from any and all claims, counterclaims, demands, causes of action, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses of whatever kind or nature, whether known or unknown, arising out of or relating to the MSA, the surcharge dispute, or the litigation, from the beginning of time through the date of execution of the Settlement Agreement.

Importantly, the Settlement Agreement contains an express provision confirming that neither party admits any liability, fault, or wrongdoing in connection with the underlying dispute. The settlement was entered into solely for the purpose of resolving the litigation and avoiding the expense, burden, and uncertainty of continued proceedings.
**F. Confidentiality Provisions**

The Settlement Agreement contains mutual confidentiality provisions pursuant to which both parties have agreed to maintain the terms of the settlement, including the settlement amount and payment schedule, in strict confidence. Disclosure is permitted only: (i) to the parties\' respective legal, financial, and tax advisors; (ii) as required by applicable law or regulation; (iii) in connection with the enforcement of the Settlement Agreement; and (iv) as required by any contractual reporting obligation, including without limitation loan agreement covenants.

This notice is being provided to Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. in reliance upon the exception described in clause (iv) above. **We respectfully request that the Administrative Agent and Ridgecrest National Bank, N.A. maintain the confidentiality of the settlement terms disclosed herein, consistent with the bank\'s own confidentiality obligations under Section 11.08 of the Credit Agreement, and that the enclosed copy of the Settlement Agreement not be further distributed, copied, or disclosed to any third party without the prior written consent of the Borrower.**
**G. Termination of the MSA**

As a component of the overall settlement, the parties have agreed to terminate the MSA by mutual consent, effective August 31, 2023. The parties have further agreed to a transition period extending through October 31, 2023, during which Cardinal Peak will fulfill all outstanding purchase orders issued by Nexford prior to the effective date of termination at the prices set forth in such purchase orders (exclusive of any disputed surcharges). No new purchase orders will be issued under the MSA following August 31, 2023. Nexford has already identified and is in the process of onboarding alternative suppliers for HRC and CRC products.
**H. Dismissal of Litigation**

The Settlement Agreement provides for the filing of a Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice of all claims and counterclaims in the litigation. As of the date of this letter, the Stipulation of Dismissal had not yet been filed but was expected to be filed imminently upon completion of certain administrative formalities. We note for the Administrative Agent\'s records that the Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice was subsequently filed with the Circuit Court of Cook County on September 14, 2023, and the case has been closed.
**[V. Financial Impact and Borrower\'s Compliance]{.underline}**
**A. Source of Settlement Funds**

The aggregate settlement payment of \$1,890,000 will be funded from Nexford\'s operating cash flow and, to the extent necessary, from available capacity under the \$45,000,000 revolving credit facility governed by the Credit Agreement. Nexford\'s Chief Financial Officer has confirmed that the Borrower maintains sufficient liquidity to satisfy both installment payments when due without material impact on the Borrower\'s working capital position or its ability to meet its other financial obligations.
**B. Materiality Assessment**
To provide the Administrative Agent with appropriate context for assessing the financial significance of the settlement, we note the following:
> • Nexford\'s consolidated annual revenue for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022 was approximately **\$287,000,000**.
> • The aggregate settlement amount of \$1,890,000 represents approximately **0.66%** of Nexford\'s annual revenue --- well below one percent.

> • The settlement, while material for purposes of the Section 6.03(b) notice threshold, does not, in the Borrower\'s assessment, constitute a Material Adverse Effect as defined in Section 1.01 of the Credit Agreement.
**C. Total Legal Costs**
The total legal costs incurred by Nexford in connection with the defense of the Cardinal Peak litigation and the negotiation of the settlement are approximately **\$272,085**, broken down as follows:
**Category**                                                                        **Amount**
Legal fees (Calderwood & Harkness LLP)                                              \$243,670
Costs advanced (filing fees, deposition costs, expert fees, mediation fees, etc.)   \$28,415
**Total legal costs**                                                               **\$272,085**
**D. Savings Analysis**
The settlement achieved significant savings for the Borrower relative to the amounts originally claimed by Cardinal Peak:
> • **Gross savings:** \$4,730,000 (claimed unpaid surcharges) minus \$1,890,000 (settlement amount) = **\$2,840,000**
> • **Net savings after legal costs:** \$2,840,000 minus \$272,085 = approximately **\$2,567,915**

These figures do not account for the additional prejudgment interest of \$380,000 claimed by Cardinal Peak, or the potential exposure to Cardinal Peak\'s attorneys\' fees under the MSA\'s fee-shifting provision, which would have further increased Nexford\'s potential liability had the case proceeded to an adverse judgment at trial.
**E. Compliance Representations**
The Borrower hereby represents to the Administrative Agent as follows:

> 1\. The execution, delivery, and performance of the Settlement Agreement, and the payment of the settlement amount contemplated thereby, do not result in a Default or an Event of Default under the Credit Agreement, as those terms are defined in Article VIII thereof.

> 2\. After giving effect to the settlement and the anticipated settlement payments, the Borrower remains in compliance with all financial covenants set forth in Section 7.01 of the Credit Agreement, including without limitation the Maximum Leverage Ratio, the Minimum Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio, and the Minimum Consolidated Tangible Net Worth requirements.
> 3\. The Borrower is in compliance with all other material terms, conditions, covenants, and obligations under the Credit Agreement as of the date of this letter.

> 4\. No other litigation, arbitration, or proceedings are pending or, to the knowledge of the Borrower, threatened against the Borrower that would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect.
**[VI. Awareness and Approval by Nexford\'s Equity Sponsor]{.underline}**

For the Administrative Agent\'s information, Nexford\'s majority equity owner, **Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Partners, LP** (the \"Sponsor\"), a Delaware limited partnership (general partner: Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Management LLC; managing partner: Conrad Yeung), has been kept fully apprised of the Cardinal Peak litigation from its inception, including all material developments in the proceedings and the terms of the proposed settlement. The Sponsor\'s designated board observer, Diana Calloway, Principal at Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Partners, LP, has participated in all relevant board discussions concerning the litigation and the settlement.

The Borrower\'s Board of Directors, with the knowledge and concurrence of the Sponsor, authorized the settlement at the amounts and on the terms described in this letter prior to the execution of the Settlement Agreement. Accordingly, the settlement has received all necessary corporate and sponsor-level approvals.
**[VII. Contact Information and Availability for Questions]{.underline}**

Should the Administrative Agent have any questions regarding this notice, the underlying litigation, or the terms of the settlement, or should the Administrative Agent require any additional information or documentation, please do not hesitate to contact any of the following individuals:
**For questions regarding the litigation and settlement terms:**
> Priya Anand, Partner Calderwood & Harkness LLP 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 4400 Chicago, Illinois 60606 Telephone: (312) 555-7842
> Email: panand@calderwoodharkness.com
**For questions regarding legal and corporate governance matters:**
> Deborah Whitfield, General Counsel Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. 4200 West Lakeshore Industrial Parkway, Suite 300 Waukegan, Illinois 60085 Telephone: (847) 555-3100
> Email: dwhitfield@nexfordindustrial.com
**For financial inquiries regarding the settlement payment schedule:**
> Lydia Tran, Chief Financial Officer Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. 4200 West Lakeshore Industrial Parkway, Suite 300 Waukegan, Illinois 60085 Telephone: (847) 555-3115
> Email: ltran@nexfordindustrial.com
We are available at your convenience to discuss this matter further or to arrange a call among the relevant parties should that be helpful.
**[VIII. Reservation of Rights]{.underline}**

This notice is provided solely for informational purposes, in satisfaction of the Borrower\'s notice obligation under Section 6.03(b) of the Credit Agreement. Nothing in this letter shall be construed as, or deemed to constitute, a waiver, modification, or amendment of any rights, remedies, defenses, or obligations of the Borrower, the Administrative Agent, or any other party under the Credit Agreement or under applicable law. The Borrower expressly reserves all of its rights and remedies under the Credit Agreement, the other Loan Documents, and applicable law, all of which are hereby preserved in full.

This letter and the obligations described herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles, consistent with the governing law provision set forth in Section 11.05 of the Credit Agreement.

We trust that this notice provides the Administrative Agent with the information required under Section 6.03(b) of the Credit Agreement. We appreciate the Administrative Agent\'s continued cooperation and attention to this matter.
Very truly yours,
**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**
Priya Anand Partner
Date: August 21, 2023
**cc:** (via email and first-class mail)

> Deborah Whitfield, General Counsel, Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. Martin Schaeffer, Chief Executive Officer, Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. Lydia Tran, Chief Financial Officer, Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. Diana Calloway, Principal, Marlowe Asset Management Bluff Capital Partners, LP Douglas Carmichael, Partner, Calderwood & Harkness LLP
**Enclosure:**

> Copy of executed Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, dated August 18, 2023, by and between Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. and Cardinal Peak Industries *(subject to confidentiality restrictions --- provided for the Administrative Agent\'s records only; not for further distribution without the prior written consent of the Borrower)*

CONFIDENTIAL --- This letter and its enclosure contain information that is confidential and subject to the confidentiality provisions of the Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release and Section 11.08 of the Credit Agreement. This communication is intended solely for the use of the addressee and other authorized recipients identified herein. Any unauthorized review, use, disclosure, or distribution is prohibited.

**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**
**Execution Date: August 18, 2023**

This Agreement resolves all disputes between the Parties in connection with *Cardinal Peak Industries v. Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.*, Case No. 2022-L-008471, Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division
This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of August 18, 2023 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and between:

**Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 4200 West Lakeshore Industrial Parkway, Suite 300, Waukegan, Illinois 60085 (EIN: 36-4821097; Delaware Charter No. 7284159) (hereinafter \"**Nexford**\" or \"**NIH**\");
and

**Cardinal Peak Industries**, a Colorado limited liability company with its principal place of business at 1580 Ridgeline Boulevard, Pueblo, Colorado 81001 (EIN: 84-3295618) (hereinafter \"**Cardinal Peak**\" or \"**CPI**\").
Nexford and Cardinal Peak are each referred to individually herein as a \"**Party**\" and collectively as the \"**Parties**.\"
**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Nexford and Cardinal Peak are parties to that certain Master Supply Agreement dated January 15, 2020, designated MSA-NIH-CPI-2020-001 (the \"**MSA**\"), pursuant to which Cardinal Peak manufactures and supplies hot-rolled coil (\"**HRC**\") and cold-rolled coil (\"**CRC**\") steel products to Nexford for use in Nexford\'s downstream fabrication and distribution operations;

**WHEREAS**, the MSA provides for the pass-through of certain raw-material surcharges, including scrap surcharges, energy surcharges, and alloy surcharges, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in Section 7.4 of the MSA and the methodology prescribed in Exhibit C thereto (the \"**Surcharge Methodology**\"), which methodology specifies, among other things, the applicable indices, baseline reference points, calculation periods, and cap-and-collar mechanisms governing the determination of such surcharges;

**WHEREAS**, a dispute arose between the Parties concerning surcharge invoices issued by Cardinal Peak for the period from March 2021 through May 2022 (the \"**Disputed Period**\"), during which Cardinal Peak invoiced total surcharges of approximately Six Million Four Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$6,410,000.00), of which Nexford paid One Million Six Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars (\$1,680,000.00), and Cardinal Peak claims an unpaid balance of approximately Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00) (the \"**Surcharge Dispute**\");

**WHEREAS**, at the core of the Surcharge Dispute, Nexford contends that Cardinal Peak deviated from the Surcharge Methodology by, among other things, utilizing incorrect index reference dates, applying surcharges to product categories excluded from the surcharge pass-through framework, and failing to apply the cap-and-collar limitations set forth in Exhibit C, while Cardinal Peak contends that its surcharge calculations were proper and in accordance with the MSA as reasonably interpreted;

**WHEREAS**, on June 10, 2022, Cardinal Peak, through its counsel Blackwood Stein & Associates LLP, issued a formal demand to Nexford for payment of Four Million Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$4,730,000.00), which demand included a detailed reconciliation of surcharge invoices for the Disputed Period, and Nexford, through its General Counsel Deborah Whitfield, rejected such demand by letter dated July 5, 2022, setting forth Nexford\'s position that a substantial portion of the surcharges had been improperly calculated;

**WHEREAS**, on August 8, 2022, Cardinal Peak filed a Complaint against Nexford in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, County Department, Law Division, docketed as Case No. 2022-L-008471 (the \"**Litigation**\"), asserting claims for breach of contract (Count I), unjust enrichment (Count II), and account stated (Count III), and seeking damages in the amount of \$4,730,000.00, plus pre-judgment interest, costs, and attorneys\' fees;

**WHEREAS**, on September 19, 2022, Nexford, through its counsel Calderwood & Harkness LLP, filed an Answer and Affirmative Defenses to the Complaint, raising, among other defenses, failure to comply with contractual conditions precedent, failure to mitigate, estoppel, and the contractual cap-and-collar limitations, and on October 3, 2022, Nexford filed a Counterclaim (the \"**Counterclaim**\") asserting breach of contract by Cardinal Peak and seeking declaratory judgment that Cardinal Peak\'s surcharge calculations were inconsistent with the Surcharge Methodology, as well as recovery of alleged overpayments in the approximate amount of Two Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$210,000.00);

**WHEREAS**, the Parties have engaged in extensive discovery in the Litigation, including the exchange of thousands of pages of documents, interrogatory responses, and requests for admission, as well as depositions of fact witnesses and the exchange of expert reports addressing the proper interpretation and application of the Surcharge Methodology, and have thereby fully informed themselves of the facts and law relating to the Surcharge Dispute;

**WHEREAS**, the MSA, at Section 14.3, provides for mandatory mediation in Chicago, Illinois, administered by a mutually agreed-upon neutral mediator, as a prerequisite to the continuation of litigation, and on May 22, 2023, the Parties jointly moved to stay the Litigation pending mediation, which motion was granted by the Honorable Judge Raymond P. Callahan on June 5, 2023;

**1.9 \"Settlement Amount\"** means the aggregate sum of One Million Eight Hundred Ninety Thousand Dollars (\$1,890,000.00), as further described in Article 2 hereof.

Upon execution of this Agreement, the Term Sheet is superseded in its entirety by this Agreement and shall have no further force or effect.
**[ARTICLE 2 --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

Line 5250: **Bottom-Line Recommendation.** Based on the analysis set forth below, MCB should enter mediation seeking a monetary settlement in the range of **\$1.2 million to \$1.75 million**, combined with a comprehensive trademark coexistence agreement providing ongoing, enforceable brand protection. A coexistence framework is preferable to pursuing complete cessation of Brindoval\'s use of MERIDIAN FRESH for two principal reasons. First, complete cessation is unlikely achievable given the Court\'s refusal to enjoin the word mark at the preliminary injunction stage and Brindoval\'s significant revenue investment in the MERIDIAN FRESH product line. Second, a well-drafted coexistence agreement can provide structured, enforceable restrictions on Brindoval\'s use of any MERIDIAN-incorporating mark --- including channel limitations, product-category restrictions, trade-dress modifications, and liquidated-damages provisions --- that would deliver meaningful, long-term brand protection exceeding what MCB might obtain through a contested trial. This memorandum recommends an opening monetary demand of \$2.5 million at mediation, with authority to settle within the recommended range, and a walk-away floor of \$1.0 million on the monetary component alone (which must be coupled with meaningful coexistence terms).
Line 5320: The commercial strength of the MERIDIAN brand is substantial. The purpose of this memorandum is to set forth Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s (\"C&H\") recommendation that Vantage Mobility Systems Corp. (\"VMS\") accept a nuisance-value settlement in the amount of **\$385,000** to resolve all claims and counterclaims in *Pinnacle Innovations LLC v. Vantage Mobility Systems Corp.*, No. 2:24-cv-00187-JRG (E.D. Tex.) (the \"Action\"). We have conducted a thorough assessment of the merits of the defense positions, the cost of continued litigation, the insurance coverage available to VMS, and the business considerations implicated by a trial scheduled for October 6, 2025. This memorandum presents the results of that assessment and our recommendation in full.

The core rationale for the settlement recommendation is straightforward: the proposed settlement amount of \$385,000 represents a small fraction of the estimated **\$2.8 million to \$3.4 million** in additional legal fees, expert fees, and other litigation expenses that VMS would be required to incur to take the case through trial. Rodney Gilstrap on December 19, 2024, while generally favorable, left the critical \"network congestion metric\" claim term ambiguously construed, preserving a meaningful path for the plaintiff to argue infringement at trial. In our judgment, the settlement is economically rational even under the most optimistic view of the defense.

Importantly, insurance coverage under VMS\'s Commercial General Liability policy with Northbridge Specialty Insurance Company (Policy No. NSI-CGL-2024-08821) will fund **\$310,000** of the \$385,000 settlement amount. **Bottom-Line Recommendation.** Based on the analysis set forth below, MCB should enter mediation seeking a monetary settlement in the range of **\$1.2 million to \$1.75 million**, combined with a comprehensive trademark coexistence agreement providing ongoing, enforceable brand protection. A coexistence framework is preferable to pursuing complete cessation of Brindoval\'s use of MERIDIAN FRESH for two principal reasons. First, complete cessation is unlikely achievable given the Court\'s refusal to enjoin the word mark at the preliminary injunction stage and Brindoval\'s significant revenue investment in the MERIDIAN FRESH product line. Second, a well-drafted coexistence agreement can provide structured, enforceable restrictions on Brindoval\'s use of any MERIDIAN-incorporating mark --- including channel limitations, product-category restrictions, trade-dress modifications, and liquidated-damages provisions --- that would deliver meaningful, long-term brand protection exceeding what MCB might obtain through a contested trial. This memorandum recommends an opening monetary demand of \$2.5 million at mediation, with authority to settle within the recommended range, and a walk-away floor of \$1.0 million on the monetary component alone (which must be coupled with meaningful coexistence terms).

The commercial strength of the MERIDIAN brand is substantial. In fiscal year 2022, MCB\'s MERIDIAN cleaning product line generated **\$94.5 million in revenue**, representing approximately 24.4% of MCB\'s total fiscal year 2022 revenue of \$387 million. The MERIDIAN cleaning line is the single largest revenue-generating brand in MCB\'s portfolio and is the cornerstone of the company\'s market positioning in the household cleaning segment.

MCB has invested heavily in building consumer awareness and brand equity for the MERIDIAN marks. Cumulative advertising and promotional expenditures from 2011 through 2022 total approximately **\$47.2 million**, representing an average annual investment of approximately \$3.93 million per year over the twelve-year period. These expenditures encompass television advertising, digital marketing, social media campaigns, in-store promotional displays, trade show participation, and co-marketing partnerships with major retailers.

It is important to note the broader corporate context. MCB is a portfolio company of **Waypoint Capital Partners LLC**, a private equity firm whose Managing Partner is James Alderton. Waypoint acquired MCB in 2019 for approximately **\$625 million**, and the value of MCB\'s brand portfolio --- with the MERIDIAN brand as its most valuable asset --- was a significant component of the acquisition price and the investment thesis. MCB is led by CEO Sandra Kwan, with Thomas R. Hennessy serving as General Counsel. The protection of the MERIDIAN brand is therefore not only a matter of MCB\'s ongoing commercial operations but also directly relevant to the preservation of Waypoint\'s substantial investment.

Taken together, these facts support the conclusion that MCB\'s MERIDIAN marks are strong, commercially distinctive marks with significant consumer recognition. The marks have achieved strong secondary meaning through over a decade of continuous use, tens of millions of dollars in advertising investment, nearly \$100 million in annual brand revenue, and nationwide distribution. This strength is a critical factor both in assessing MCB\'s likelihood of success on its trademark infringement claims and in valuing the settlement.

Based on information obtained during the PI proceedings, Brindoval\'s MERIDIAN FRESH line generated **gross revenue of \$6.8 million** during the initial five-month period from July through November 2022. Annualized, this equates to projected revenue of approximately **\$16.32 million** (\$6.8 million ÷ 5 months × 12 months). The actual annualized figure may vary based on seasonal purchasing patterns and the impact of the Court\'s PI Order on Brindoval\'s trade dress, but \$16.32 million represents a reasonable working estimate.

As a rough approximation, applying the 31.4% confusion rate to Brindoval\'s \$6.8 million in actual revenue over the five-month launch period yields an estimated diverted-sales figure of approximately **\$2.14 million** (31.4% × \$6.8M). On an annualized basis, this figure would be approximately **\$5.12 million** (31.4% × \$16.32M).

Accounting for these discounts, the realistic range for lost-profits damages is **\$1.0 million to \$2.5 million** for the period from Brindoval\'s July 2022 launch through the projected trial date (estimated Q4 2023 or Q1 2024). This range assumes that a properly qualified economic expert can credibly establish that approximately 15% to 35% of consumers who experienced confusion would have purchased MCB\'s products instead, after applying appropriate discounts to the raw confusion-rate calculation.

**Calculation.** Applying a 5% midpoint royalty rate to Brindoval\'s actual gross revenue of \$6.8 million for the five-month period yields a reasonable royalty of approximately **\$340,000**. On an annualized basis, a 5% royalty applied to the projected \$16.32 million in annual revenue yields approximately **\$816,000**.

**Brindoval\'s Revenue.** As noted, Brindoval\'s MERIDIAN FRESH line generated gross revenue of **\$6.8 million** from July through November 2022. Full discovery of Brindoval\'s financial records will be necessary to determine Brindoval\'s cost of goods sold, marketing and distribution costs, and net profit margin for the MERIDIAN FRESH line. In the absence of complete financial data, we rely on industry benchmarks: private-label or store-brand products in the household cleaning category typically carry **net profit margins of 25% to 40%**, which are generally higher than national-brand margins due to lower marketing costs and direct-to-consumer distribution.

**Estimated Profits.** Applying these margin assumptions to Brindoval\'s \$6.8 million in gross revenue yields estimated Brindoval net profits of **\$1.7 million to \$2.72 million** for the actual five-month period. Jury Optics.** Although this factor is secondary to the legal merits, it is worth noting that jury sympathies in the Southern District of New York may be marginally influenced by the parties\' relative profiles. Brindoval is a regional retailer based in the Midwest, while MCB is a private equity-backed consumer products company acquired by Waypoint Capital Partners LLC for \$625 million. The comparison demonstrates that **settlement eliminates risk and transaction costs while delivering a comparable or superior net economic outcome**. A settlement at the target of \$1.35 million, coupled with a strong coexistence agreement, would yield a net gain of approximately \$700,000--\$800,000 after deducting total matter costs, with certainty. By contrast, proceeding to trial offers a range of outcomes from a net loss of over \$1 million (in the adverse scenario) to a net gain of approximately \$1.3 million (in the favorable scenario), with the most likely outcome falling somewhere in between. Risk-adjusted, the settlement path is clearly preferable.

**Floor: \$1.0 million.** This figure represents the approximate lower bound of MCB\'s reasonable-royalty damages calculation extrapolated through the projected trial date, and roughly recoups MCB\'s total litigation investment to date plus projected settlement costs (\$550,000--\$650,000) with a modest premium. A settlement below \$1.0 million would not adequately compensate MCB for the demonstrated infringement or provide a credible return on the litigation investment. Importantly, a \$1.0 million monetary settlement must be coupled with meaningful coexistence terms to be acceptable; the monetary floor alone is insufficient without strong non-monetary protections.

**Target: \$1.35 million.** This figure represents a credible compromise between MCB\'s moderate damages estimate (lost profits of \$1.0M--\$2.5M) and the range we anticipate Brindoval would find acceptable (\$800,000--\$1.35M, as discussed in Section IX below). A settlement at \$1.35 million coupled with the coexistence framework would represent a strong outcome for MCB, delivering meaningful monetary recovery while securing the long-term brand protections that are of critical strategic importance.

**Ceiling: \$1.75 million.** This represents the upper bound of what MCB could reasonably expect to achieve in a negotiated settlement, given the litigation risk factors and Brindoval\'s likely negotiation positions. A settlement above \$1.75 million is possible but would likely require Brindoval to accept a figure approaching its risk-adjusted expected litigation cost (damages plus legal fees), which may not be achievable without additional leverage.

**Recommended Opening Demand: \$2.5 million.** Consistent with standard mediation practice, MCB should open with a demand that provides adequate negotiation room to reach the target range. An opening demand of \$2.5 million is aggressive but credible --- it falls within the range of MCB\'s damages theories (between the moderate lost-profits estimate and the aggressive disgorgement estimate) and signals the seriousness of MCB\'s position without being so extreme as to undermine credibility with the mediator.

**Recommended Walk-Away Floor: \$1.0 million.** MCB should not accept a monetary settlement below \$1.0 million under any circumstances without further authorization from the client. This floor applies to the monetary component alone and assumes that the settlement includes meaningful coexistence terms as described in Section VIII.

1538:
