**Background. WHEREAS**, VHG owns and operates three resort properties in the State of Florida, specifically: (i) Verimark Grand Key Resort, located at Mile Marker 48, Marathon, Florida 33050; (ii) Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, located at 1400 Estero Boulevard, Fort Myers Beach, Florida 33931; and (iii) Verimark Sunset Shores, located at 7200 Gulf Boulevard, St. Pete Beach, Florida 33706;

**WHEREAS**, Hurricane Callista, classified as a Category 4 hurricane by the National Hurricane Center, made landfall on September 18, 2022, in the Lower Florida Keys, causing catastrophic property damage and prolonged business interruption at all three of VHG\'s resort properties;

**WHEREAS**, at the time of Hurricane Callista, VHG maintained a property and business-interruption insurance program with a total tower limit of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) above a Five Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$500,000) per-occurrence deductible, structured as follows:

**WHEREAS**, VHG submitted a sworn statement in proof of loss on November 15, 2022, claiming approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) in aggregate business-interruption losses arising from Hurricane Callista across all three resort properties;

**WHEREAS**, VHG filed suit on March 1, 2023, in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, Miami-Dade County, under Case No. 2022-CA-031547, asserting claims for breach of contract, declaratory judgment, and bad faith against all four Insurer Defendants;

**WHEREAS**, cross-motions for partial summary judgment regarding the named-windstorm sub-limit were pending at the time of mediation, with VHG\'s motion for partial summary judgment having been filed on November 1, 2023, and the Insurer Defendants\' cross-motion for partial summary judgment having been filed on November 15, 2023, and no ruling having been issued on either motion;

This Term Sheet memorializes the principal terms of the settlement reached at the conclusion of mediation on December 5, 2023, and shall be binding on all Parties upon execution, subject to the preparation and execution of a definitive Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release as contemplated in Section 7 below.

The Insurer Defendants shall collectively pay to VHG a total aggregate settlement amount of **Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$47,300,000)** (the \"Settlement Amount\"). The Settlement Amount represents approximately 78.83% of VHG\'s total claimed loss of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) under the insurance program referenced herein. The Settlement Amount is inclusive of all claims for property damage, business-interruption loss, extra expense, debris removal, and any and all other coverages or benefits under the referenced policies, and is further inclusive of any and all claims for interest, penalties, attorneys\' fees, and costs asserted or assertable in the above-captioned litigation.
The aggregate Settlement Amount of \$47,300,000 shall be allocated among the Insurer Defendants as follows:

Each Insurer Defendant\'s obligation under this Term Sheet and the contemplated Settlement Agreement is several and not joint. Each Insurer Defendant shall be responsible solely for its individual allocated share of the Settlement Amount as set forth in Section 1.2 above. No Insurer Defendant shall have any obligation or liability for the payment of any other Insurer Defendant\'s allocated share. VHG acknowledges and agrees that it shall look only to each individual Insurer Defendant for that Insurer Defendant\'s allocated share and shall have no right to seek recovery from any Insurer Defendant for any shortfall in payment by another Insurer Defendant.

All payments to be made by each Insurer Defendant under this Term Sheet and the definitive Settlement Agreement shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States dollars to the trust account designated by Calderwood & Harkness LLP, as counsel for VHG.

Each Insurer Defendant shall remit its allocated share of the Settlement Amount, as set forth in Section 1.2 above, within forty-five (45) calendar days following the date of execution of the definitive Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release by all Parties. Based on the anticipated execution of the definitive Settlement Agreement on or before December 19, 2023, the resulting payment deadline is anticipated to be on or before February 2, 2024. In the event the definitive Settlement Agreement is executed on a date other than December 19, 2023, the forty-five (45) calendar day payment deadline shall be calculated from the actual date of full execution by all Parties.

All settlement payments shall be directed to the Interest on Trust Account (\"IOTA\") or other designated trust account of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, as counsel for VHG. Calderwood & Harkness LLP shall provide written wire transfer instructions to counsel for each Insurer Defendant promptly following the execution of the definitive Settlement Agreement. No payment shall be made directly to VHG or to any person or entity other than the designated trust account of Calderwood & Harkness LLP unless otherwise agreed in writing by VHG and its counsel.

Upon receipt by Calderwood & Harkness LLP, on behalf of VHG, of the full aggregate Settlement Amount of \$47,300,000 (i.e., upon receipt of all four Insurer Defendants\' respective allocated shares), the Parties shall exchange mutual general releases of all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, causes of action, demands, obligations, damages, losses, costs, expenses, and liabilities of every kind and nature, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, accrued or unaccrued, contingent or absolute, arising from, relating to, or in any way connected with the losses sustained by VHG as a result of Hurricane Callista (September 18, 2022) under the following insurance policies:

> \(b\) The mutual release shall not affect, impair, or otherwise modify coverage under the referenced policies (IIC-PRP-2022-07541, PSL-XS1-2022-3390, MAC-XS2-2022-09817, and SRL-XS3-2022-5102) for any loss, claim, or occurrence other than Hurricane Callista (September 18, 2022). To the extent VHG has or may assert any claim under any of the referenced policies arising from any event or occurrence other than Hurricane Callista, such claims are expressly preserved and are not affected by this Term Sheet or the contemplated Settlement Agreement.

27193: 
27194: **Section 4.3** *Scope of Release.* The releases set forth in Sections 4.1 and 4.2 of this Agreement are intended to be as broad and comprehensive as permitted by law and extend to all Claims, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, disclosed or undisclosed, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, that exist as of the Effective Date and that arise from, relate to, or are in any way connected with the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies. Each Party expressly, knowingly, and voluntarily waives any and all rights it may have under any statute, regulation, or common-law principle of any jurisdiction---including, but not limited to, Section 1542 of the California Civil Code and any analogous provision of Florida law or the law of any other jurisdiction---that would otherwise limit the scope of this release to claims known or suspected at the time of execution of this Agreement. Each Party acknowledges and understands that it may discover facts different from or in addition to those it now knows or believes to be true with respect to the Released Claims, and that the releases set forth herein shall remain in full force and effect notwithstanding such discovery.

27196: **Section 4.4** *Carve-Out --- Enforcement of This Agreement.* Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Article IV, nothing in this Agreement shall release any Party from its obligations, covenants, representations, or warranties set forth in this Agreement. Each Party expressly retains the right to enforce the terms and conditions of this Agreement, to seek specific performance of any obligation hereunder, and to pursue any available remedies for breach of this Agreement.
27197: 
27198: **Section 4.5** *No Release of Third-Party Claims.* The releases set forth in this Article IV do not extend to, and shall not be construed to release or affect, any claims VHG may have against third parties that are not signatories to this Agreement, including but not limited to Tidewater Risk Advisors LLC, or any other broker, agent, or consultant. Similarly, the releases set forth in this Article IV do not extend to, and shall not be construed to release or affect, any claims by any Insurer Party against third parties that are not signatories to this Agreement, including but not limited to any claims for contribution, indemnification, or subrogation against non-party third parties.
27199: 
27200: **[ARTICLE V --- NO ADMISSION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**
27201: 
27202: **Section 5.1** *No Admission.* This Agreement and the settlement reflected herein are the result of a compromise of disputed claims and shall not be construed as an admission of liability, fault, wrongdoing, or the validity or invalidity of any claim or defense by any Party. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing:
27203: 
27204: > \(a\) No Insurer Party admits or concedes that any coverage was owed to VHG under any of the Policies with respect to the Hurricane Callista Losses, that any denial or reservation of rights was improper, unfounded, or made in bad faith, or that any Policy provision, including the named-windstorm sub-limit, the flood exclusion, the concurrent-causation provision, or any other provision, was inapplicable to VHG\'s claim.
27205: >
27206: > \(b\) VHG does not admit or concede that its claim for business-interruption losses was overstated, exaggerated, or otherwise unsupported, that it failed to mitigate its losses, or that any amount less than its full claimed losses was the proper measure of recovery under the Policies.
27207: >
27208: > \(c\) This Agreement, and any of its terms, provisions, or the fact of settlement, may not be offered, received, or admitted in evidence in any action, suit, or other proceeding of any kind or nature as an admission, concession, or evidence of liability, fault, wrongdoing, or the invalidity of any claim or defense by any Party, except in an action to enforce the terms of this Agreement.
27209: 
27210: **[ARTICLE VI --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
27211: 
27212: **Section 6.1** *Confidential Settlement Amount.* The Parties agree that the specific dollar amount of the Settlement Amount and the allocation of the Settlement Amount among the Insurer Parties as set forth in Section 2.2 and Exhibit A hereto shall be treated as strictly confidential information. The Parties may state publicly that the Litigation has been settled on terms agreeable to all Parties without disclosing the specific financial terms of the settlement.
27215: 
27216: **Section 6.3** *Permitted Disclosures.* Notwithstanding Section 6.1, the Parties may disclose the financial terms and other confidential provisions of this Agreement:

27218: > \(a\) To their respective legal counsel, accountants, auditors, and tax advisors, on a need-to-know basis, as reasonably necessary for the purpose of obtaining legal, accounting, auditing, or tax advice, provided that such recipients are advised of the confidential nature of the information and are bound by obligations of confidentiality at least as restrictive as those set forth herein;

**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**
**Effective Date: December 19, 2023**
This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of December 19, 2023 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:
**VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation (\"VHG\" or \"Plaintiff\"), with its principal offices at 1900 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200, Miami, Florida 33129;
**IRONCLAD INDEMNITY CORPORATION**, a Connecticut-domiciled stock insurance company (\"Ironclad\"), with its principal offices at 55 Constitution Boulevard, Hartford, Connecticut 06103;
**PINNACLE SURPLUS LINES INC.**, a Texas-domiciled surplus-lines insurer (\"Pinnacle\"), with its principal offices at 200 Congress Avenue, Suite 1400, Austin, Texas 78701;
**MONTCLAIR ASSURANCE COMPANY**, a New York-domiciled admitted insurance carrier (\"Montclair\"), with its principal offices at 1 Liberty Plaza, 38th Floor, New York, New York 10006; and
**SOVEREIGN RE LTD.**, a Bermuda-domiciled excess carrier (\"Sovereign Re\"), with its principal offices at 14 Front Street, Hamilton HM 11, Bermuda.
VHG, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re are referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**
**WHEREAS:**

**A.** VHG is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, whose common stock is publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VMRK,\" and which maintains its principal executive offices at 1900 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200, Miami, Florida 33129. VHG is engaged in the business of owning, operating, and managing luxury resort hotel properties in the State of Florida. As of the Effective Date, VHG\'s portfolio of properties includes, among others, the following three resort hotel properties (collectively, the \"Insured Properties\"):
> \(i\) the Verimark Grand Key Resort, located at Mile Marker 48, Marathon, Florida 33050, a 287-room full-service luxury resort and marina situated in the Florida Keys;

> \(ii\) the Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, located at 1400 Estero Boulevard, Fort Myers Beach, Florida 33931, a 412-room beachfront hotel and conference center situated on the Gulf Coast of Florida; and

> \(iii\) the Verimark Sunset Shores, located at 7200 Gulf Boulevard, St. Pete Beach, Florida 33706, a 194-room boutique luxury hotel and spa situated on the barrier island of St. Pete Beach on the Gulf of Mexico.

**B.** In connection with VHG\'s ownership and operation of the Insured Properties, VHG procured and maintained a layered insurance program consisting of property and business-interruption coverage as follows:

> \(i\) Ironclad is a stock insurance company domiciled in the State of Connecticut and licensed to transact insurance business in the State of Florida. Ironclad issued to VHG an all-risk property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number IIC-PRP-2022-07541, for the policy period commencing July 1, 2022 and ending July 1, 2023, providing primary coverage with a per-occurrence limit of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) for property damage and business-interruption losses, subject to a deductible of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per occurrence (the \"Primary Policy\").

> \(ii\) Pinnacle is a surplus-lines insurer domiciled in the State of Texas and authorized to transact surplus-lines insurance business in the State of Florida. Pinnacle issued to VHG a first excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number PSL-XS1-2022-3390, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Fifteen Million Dollars (\$15,000,000) in coverage in excess of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the Primary Policy (the \"First Excess Policy\").

> \(iii\) Montclair is an admitted insurance carrier domiciled in the State of New York and licensed to transact insurance business in the State of Florida. Montclair issued to VHG a second excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number MAC-XS2-2022-09817, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in coverage in excess of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the combined limits of the Primary Policy and the First Excess Policy (the \"Second Excess Policy\").

> \(iv\) Sovereign Re is an excess carrier domiciled in Bermuda and authorized to transact excess insurance business relating to risks situated in the State of Florida. Sovereign Re issued to VHG a third excess layer property and business-interruption insurance policy, bearing Policy Number SRL-XS3-2022-5102, for the same policy period of July 1, 2022 through July 1, 2023, providing Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in coverage in excess of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), i.e., attaching at the exhaustion of the combined limits of the Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, and the Second Excess Policy (the \"Third Excess Policy\").

The Primary Policy, the First Excess Policy, the Second Excess Policy, and the Third Excess Policy are referred to herein collectively as the \"Policies.\" The Policies provide aggregate tower limits of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) above the Five Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$500,000) deductible applicable under the Primary Policy.

**C.** On September 18, 2022, Hurricane Callista, classified by the National Hurricane Center as a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Veltason Hurricane Wind Scale, made landfall in the Lower Florida Keys with maximum sustained winds of approximately 145 miles per hour and produced storm surge inundation of approximately eight (8) to fourteen (14) feet above normal tide levels in Monroe County and approximately six (6) to ten (10) feet above normal tide levels in Lee County. Hurricane Callista caused catastrophic and widespread damage throughout southern Florida, including significant damage to coastal structures, resort properties, marinas, and critical infrastructure along the Florida Keys and the Gulf Coast of southwestern Florida. As a direct and proximate result of Hurricane Callista, the Insured Properties sustained catastrophic property damage and experienced prolonged and severe business interruption, including complete closure of the Grand Key Resort and the Harborview Hotel & Conference Center for extended periods, and partial closure of Sunset Shores (collectively, the \"Hurricane Callista Losses\"). VHG submitted an initial notice of loss to Ironclad, as primary carrier, on September 22, 2022, four days following the landfall of Hurricane Callista. Thereafter, VHG submitted a sworn statement in proof of loss to Ironclad on November 15, 2022, pursuant to the requirements of the Primary Policy, asserting total business-interruption losses of approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) across the Insured Properties.

**D.** On October 12, 2022, Ironclad, through its designated third-party claims administrator, Arbor Claims Services LLC, and its coverage counsel, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP, issued a reservation of rights letter to VHG with respect to VHG\'s claim for business-interruption losses. On February 3, 2023, Ironclad issued a formal denial of coverage for VHG\'s business-interruption claim, asserting, among other grounds, that: (i) the Primary Policy contained a named-windstorm sub-limit that capped business-interruption recovery at an amount substantially below VHG\'s claimed losses; (ii) the period of restoration was subject to dispute, and VHG had failed to establish the proper period of restoration for business-interruption coverage; (iii) certain claimed losses were attributable to flood and storm surge, which were subject to a concurrent causation analysis and the flood exclusion in the Primary Policy; and (iv) VHG had failed to adequately mitigate its losses in breach of its duties under the Primary Policy. On February 10, 2023, Pinnacle, through its coverage counsel, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP, followed Ironclad\'s denial on a follow-form basis and denied coverage for VHG\'s business-interruption claim to the extent it fell within Pinnacle\'s layer. Montclair and Sovereign Re, through their joint coverage counsel, Delvecchio & Kraus LLP, did not issue formal denials of coverage but reserved all rights under their respective policies, asserting that their excess layers would not be reached based on the application of the named-windstorm sub-limit asserted by Ironclad and Pinnacle.

**E.** On March 1, 2023, VHG filed a multi-count complaint in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, captioned *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corp., Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, assigned to the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge (the \"Litigation\"). In the Litigation, VHG asserted claims for: (i) breach of contract against all four Insurer Parties; (ii) declaratory judgment seeking a judicial determination of coverage rights under the Policies; and (iii) bad faith, including both statutory bad faith under Section 624.155 of the Florida Statutes and common-law bad faith, against all four Insurer Parties. VHG\'s complaint alleged total business-interruption losses of approximately Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000), comprised of approximately Thirty-One Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$31,400,000) attributable to the Verimark Grand Key Resort, approximately Eighteen Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,700,000) attributable to the Verimark Harborview Hotel & Conference Center, and approximately Nine Million Nine Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$9,900,000) attributable to the Verimark Sunset Shores. On April 15, 2023, Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re, through their respective counsel, filed answers and affirmative defenses denying liability and raising numerous defenses to VHG\'s claims. Thereafter, the Parties conducted extensive fact discovery, including the exchange of voluminous documents, written discovery, and depositions of party representatives, including depositions of VHG\'s Chief Executive Officer Marcus Ellsworth, VHG\'s Chief Financial Officer Diane Calder, VHG\'s General Counsel Nathaniel Driscoll, Ironclad\'s Senior Vice President of Claims Victor Haddon, and Arbor Claims Services LLC\'s lead adjuster Denise Whitford. **F.** On December 4 and December 5, 2023, the Parties participated in a two-day mediation session before the Honorable Richard Mendelson (Ret.) of Keystone Dispute Resolution Inc. in Miami, Florida. **NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

> \(a\) \"Agreement\" means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, together with all Exhibits attached hereto, as the same may be amended or modified from time to time in accordance with Section 9.4.

> \(c\) \"Effective Date\" means the date on which this Agreement is fully executed by all Parties, which the Parties agree is December 19, 2023.

> \(d\) \"Hurricane Callista Losses\" means any and all property damage, business-interruption losses, loss of rents, extra expenses, debris removal costs, increased cost of construction, loss of business income, and all related losses, costs, and expenses sustained or incurred by VHG at or in connection with the Insured Properties arising out of or relating to Hurricane Callista, which made landfall on September 18, 2022, and the aftermath thereof.

**Section 2.1** *Total Settlement Amount.* In consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, releases, and obligations set forth in this Agreement, and in full and final settlement and resolution of all Claims among the Parties arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies, the Insurer Parties shall pay to VHG the aggregate sum of Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$47,300,000.00) (the \"Settlement Amount\"). The Parties acknowledge that the Settlement Amount represents approximately 78.83% of VHG\'s total claimed business-interruption losses of Sixty Million Dollars (\$60,000,000) and reflects a negotiated compromise of disputed claims among all Parties. The Settlement Amount shall be allocated among the Insurer Parties as set forth in the Payment Allocation Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A and in accordance with Section 2.2 of this Agreement.
**Section 2.2** *Allocation of Settlement Amount.* The Settlement Amount shall be allocated among the Insurer Parties as follows:
> \(a\) Ironclad Indemnity Corporation shall pay Twenty-Four Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$24,500,000.00);
> \(b\) Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. shall pay Twelve Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$12,200,000.00);
> \(c\) Montclair Assurance Company shall pay Six Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$6,800,000.00); and
> \(d\) Sovereign Re Ltd. shall pay Three Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$3,800,000.00).

The foregoing allocation represents the Parties\' agreed-upon allocation and shall not be construed as a determination or admission of the amount of coverage owed by any individual Insurer Party under its respective Policy.

**Section 2.3** *Payment Terms.* Each Insurer Party\'s share of the Settlement Amount, as set forth in Section 2.2, shall be paid in a single lump-sum payment by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars within forty-five (45) calendar days of the Effective Date. Given that the Effective Date is December 19, 2023, the payment deadline shall be February 2, 2024 (the \"Payment Deadline\"). All payments shall be made to the Interest on Lawyers\' Trust Account (IOLTA) of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, counsel for VHG, in accordance with wire transfer instructions to be provided separately and in writing by Calderwood & Harkness LLP to counsel for each respective Insurer Party within five (5) business days of the Effective Date. Each Insurer Party shall provide written confirmation to Calderwood & Harkness LLP of the initiation of its wire transfer no later than two (2) business days prior to the Payment Deadline. Each Insurer Party shall be severally, and not jointly, liable for its respective share of the Settlement Amount as set forth in Section 2.2. The payment by each Insurer Party of its respective share shall fully discharge that Insurer Party\'s financial obligations under this Agreement regardless of whether any other Insurer Party pays or fails to pay its respective share.

**Section 2.4** *Late Payment.* In the event that any Insurer Party fails to remit its respective share of the Settlement Amount on or before the Payment Deadline, the unpaid amount shall bear interest at the rate of twelve percent (12%) per annum, or the maximum rate permitted under applicable Florida law, whichever is less, computed from the day immediately following the Payment Deadline until the date upon which such payment is received in full. VHG acknowledges and agrees that no Insurer Party, nor any agent, employee, or counsel of any Insurer Party, has provided or is providing any tax advice to VHG with respect to the Settlement Amount or any portion thereof. The Parties agree that VHG will report the Settlement Amount as proceeds from an insurance recovery for business-interruption losses for applicable tax purposes. **Section 3.1** *Stipulation of Dismissal.* Within ten (10) business days following receipt by VHG (through the trust account of Calderwood & Harkness LLP) of the full Settlement Amount from all Insurer Parties, the Parties shall jointly execute and file a Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice of all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and affirmative defenses in the Litigation, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, before the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge. **Section 3.3** *Withdrawal of Pending Motions.* Upon the filing of the Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice in the Litigation, all pending motions in the Litigation shall be deemed withdrawn and rendered moot, including without limitation: (a) VHG\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment Regarding the Applicability of the Named-Windstorm Sub-Limit to Business-Interruption Losses, filed on November 1, 2023; and (b) the Cross-Motion for Partial Summary Judgment filed by Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re on November 15, 2023. **Section 4.3** *Scope of Release.* The releases set forth in Sections 4.1 and 4.2 of this Agreement are intended to be as broad and comprehensive as permitted by law and extend to all Claims, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, disclosed or undisclosed, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, that exist as of the Effective Date and that arise from, relate to, or are in any way connected with the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies. Each Party acknowledges and understands that it may discover facts different from or in addition to those it now knows or believes to be true with respect to the Released Claims, and that the releases set forth herein shall remain in full force and effect notwithstanding such discovery.

**Section 4.4** *Carve-Out --- Enforcement of This Agreement.* Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Article IV, nothing in this Agreement shall release any Party from its obligations, covenants, representations, or warranties set forth in this Agreement. Each Party expressly retains the right to enforce the terms and conditions of this Agreement, to seek specific performance of any obligation hereunder, and to pursue any available remedies for breach of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE V --- NO ADMISSION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1** *No Admission.* This Agreement and the settlement reflected herein are the result of a compromise of disputed claims and shall not be construed as an admission of liability, fault, wrongdoing, or the validity or invalidity of any claim or defense by any Party. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing:

> \(a\) No Insurer Party admits or concedes that any coverage was owed to VHG under any of the Policies with respect to the Hurricane Callista Losses, that any denial or reservation of rights was improper, unfounded, or made in bad faith, or that any Policy provision, including the named-windstorm sub-limit, the flood exclusion, the concurrent-causation provision, or any other provision, was inapplicable to VHG\'s claim.

The memorandum is intended to provide a comprehensive framework for the internal allocation of settlement funds and to serve as a reference document for AMA\'s legal, finance, and accounting teams as the settlement proceeds through the court approval process.

On September 8, 2023, following two full-day mediation sessions before the Honorable Patricia Okoro (Ret.) of Westpark Dispute Resolution Inc. in Los Angeles, the parties to the consolidated *Fuentes* class action reached a tentative class-wide settlement with a Gross Settlement Amount of \$14,750,000. The first mediation session was held on August 14, 2023, and resulted in a mediator\'s proposal that was conditionally accepted by both sides subject to further negotiation of settlement terms. The second session on September 8, 2023, resolved all remaining disputes regarding settlement structure, class definition, allocation methodology, and release scope, resulting in the parties\' agreement in principle to the \$14,750,000 GSA.

The settlement includes a PAGA component of \$750,000, which is allocated as required under California Labor Code § 2699(i): seventy-five percent (\$562,500) to the California Labor and Workforce Development Agency (\"LWDA\"), and twenty-five percent (\$187,500) to the aggrieved employees. The PAGA payment is included within --- not in addition to --- the \$14,750,000 GSA. This structure was negotiated to ensure that the total settlement exposure remained fixed and that the PAGA component did not create incremental funding obligations beyond the GSA.

The full abatement of the proposed IRC § 6662(e) substantial valuation misstatement penalty represents a significant and independently valuable component of the settlement outcome. The proposed penalty of \$15,977,000 would have been assessed at the 20% rate on any tax attributable to a net IRC § 482 transfer pricing adjustment, regardless of the ultimate settlement amount of the underlying income adjustment. That is, even at the settlement-level adjustment of \$47,600,000, a penalty could theoretically have been imposed on the tax attributable to that adjustment (approximately \$2,000,000 in penalties on the settlement adjustment amount) had PPC not established a defense to penalties. The full abatement therefore eliminates penalty exposure entirely.

The \$47,600,000 U.S. income adjustment has the potential to create a corresponding adjustment on PBI\'s Irish tax return. Under the U.S.-Ireland Income Tax Treaty, Article 9 (Associated Enterprises), where one Contracting State (the United States) makes an adjustment to the profits of an enterprise of that State in respect of transactions with an associated enterprise of the other Contracting State (Ireland), the other State is generally required to make a corresponding adjustment to the amount of tax charged on the associated enterprise, to the extent necessary to eliminate double taxation.

If PBI\'s Irish taxable income is not correspondingly reduced to reflect the \$47,600,000 U.S. adjustment, PPC and PBI would effectively be subject to double taxation on the same income. To avoid this result, PPC has the option of requesting relief through the **Mutual Agreement Procedure (\"MAP\")** provided under Article 25 of the U.S.-Ireland Income Tax Treaty. A MAP request would invoke the competent authorities of the United States (the IRS) and Ireland (the Revenue Commissioners) to consult with one another to resolve the double taxation issue.

However, the decision to pursue a MAP request involves a cost-benefit analysis. MAP proceedings can be time-consuming (often requiring 18 to 36 months to resolve) and involve additional professional fees. Given the relatively modest settlement amount of \$47,600,000 and the resulting Irish tax implications (which would be computed at Ireland\'s 12.5% corporate tax rate or, for qualifying income, the 6.25% Knowledge Development box rate), the potential Irish tax relief may be in the range of approximately \$3,000,000 to \$6,000,000. PPC should evaluate whether the magnitude of potential relief justifies the cost and administrative burden of pursuing MAP.

The \$47,600,000 federal income adjustment resulting from the settlement will flow through to PPC\'s state income tax returns in PPC\'s filing jurisdictions. PPC files income tax returns in multiple states, including its state of incorporation and principal place of business, New Jersey, as well as other states in which PPC has nexus.

Based on the comprehensive analysis set forth in this memorandum, **Calderwood & Harkness recommends that PPC accept the settlement offer** of \$47,600,000 in total income adjustments for Tax Years 2017 through 2020, together with full abatement of the proposed IRC § 6662(e) penalty.

> **1. Favorable Economics.** The total estimated cash cost to PPC of approximately \$12,840,000 (tax plus estimated interest) compares extremely favorably to the potential exposure of \$95,861,000 or more (tax plus penalty on the full proposed adjustment, before interest). The settlement represents approximately 86.6% savings on a tax-plus-penalty basis, and approximately 89.6% savings when the penalty abatement is separately weighted.

> **2. Full Penalty Abatement.** The settlement eliminates the \$15,977,000 proposed IRC § 6662(e) penalty in its entirety, as well as the reserved IRC § 6662(h) gross valuation misstatement penalty. This outcome provides complete certainty that no penalty exposure exists for the 2017--2020 examination period.

> **4. Within Target Range.** The settlement amount of \$47,600,000 (12.51% of proposed adjustments) falls squarely within Calderwood & Harkness\'s recommended target range of 10--15%, and well below the 20% hard ceiling authorized by PPC management. The result validates the negotiation strategy employed throughout the Appeals process.

> **5. Favorable FIN 48 Impact.** The settlement enables PPC to reduce its ASC 740-10 uncertain tax position reserve from \$62,400,000 to approximately \$14,800,000 --- a reserve release that will benefit PPC\'s effective tax rate and improve the Company\'s reported financial results in Q1 2024.

The settlement offer of \$47,600,000 represents an exceptional outcome for Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. in light of the \$380,400,000 in proposed adjustments set forth in the IRS\'s Notice of Proposed Adjustment. The settlement concedes only 12.51% of the proposed adjustments and achieves full abatement of the proposed \$15,977,000 IRC § 6662(e) penalty.

The total cost of the examination to PPC --- approximately \$21,165,420, including all professional fees, federal income tax, and estimated interest --- compares very favorably to the potential tax-plus-penalty exposure of \$95,861,000 (before interest) and reflects the strength of PPC\'s factual and legal positions on each of the issues under examination. The result was achieved through the combination of PPC\'s well-maintained contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, the rigorous and persuasive economic analyses prepared by Whitmore Valuation Group, the comprehensive economic substance evidence documenting PBI\'s independent operations, and the effective advocacy by the Calderwood & Harkness team throughout the examination and Appeals process.

On October 12, 2023, the IRS examination team issued a Notice of Proposed Adjustment (\"NOPA\") proposing net adjustments totaling \$380,400,000 across all four tax years. PPC received the corresponding 30-Day Letter on November 8, 2023. Pursuant to a written extension of time granted by the examination team, PPC timely filed its formal Protest on December 22, 2023. The Protest set forth PPC\'s detailed factual, legal, and economic objections to each of the proposed adjustments and requested a conference with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals.

The examination team allowed a correlative offset of (\$42,650,000) to avoid double-counting of income that would otherwise be attributed to PPC under both the CSA cost-sharing ratio adjustment and the legacy IP royalty rate adjustment.

Specifically, the examination team contended that PBI\'s share of reasonably anticipated benefits --- and therefore its required cost-sharing contribution --- was understated by the taxpayer. The proposed adjustments were as follows:

**(b) Royalty Rate Adjustments.** The examination team also proposed an increase in the royalty rate applicable to the intercompany license of legacy intellectual property from the taxpayer to PBI, from the reported rate of 4.5% of non-Americas net sales to a proposed rate of 11.0% of non-Americas net sales. The examination team asserted that comparable uncontrolled transactions and other transfer pricing methods supported a higher arm\'s-length royalty rate. The proposed adjustments were as follows:

**(c) Correlative Offset.** The IRS allowed a correlative offset in the amount of (\$42,650,000) across all four taxable years to prevent double-counting of income attributable to the overlap between the CSA cost-sharing adjustments and the royalty rate adjustments.
**(d) Net Proposed Adjustment.** The net proposed adjustment across all four taxable years, after application of the correlative offset, was as follows:

**(e) Penalty.** In addition to the proposed income adjustments, the IRS proposed a substantial valuation misstatement penalty under IRC § 6662(e) at a rate of twenty percent (20%) of the underpayment of tax attributable to the IRC § 482 allocation. The proposed penalty was calculated as follows:

The taxpayer, through its authorized legal representatives at Calderwood & Harkness LLP, filed a timely Formal Protest on December 22, 2023. The Formal Protest contested all proposed adjustments to taxable income under IRC § 482, as well as the proposed IRC § 6662(e) substantial valuation misstatement penalty. The Formal Protest set forth detailed legal and factual arguments, supported by economic analyses and expert reports, challenging the examination team\'s proposed transfer pricing adjustments on multiple grounds, including the appropriate selection and application of the best method under Treasury Regulations § 1.482-1(c), the proper measurement of reasonably anticipated benefits under the CSA, and the identification and analysis of comparable uncontrolled transactions for purposes of the royalty rate determination.
**Section 2.5 --- Appeals Conference and Settlement**

During the Appeals conference, the parties discussed the merits of each proposed adjustment and the associated penalty in detail. The taxpayer\'s representatives presented economic analyses and expert testimony from Dr. Helena Vasquez of Whitmore Valuation Group LLC, addressing the comparability analyses, the application of the residual profit split method to the CSA cost-sharing ratios, and the application of the comparable uncontrolled transaction method to the legacy IP royalty rate.
This Closing Agreement memorializes the terms of the settlement agreed upon by the parties.

The parties agree that the taxable income of Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. (EIN: 22-3741856), as reported on its Forms 1120 for the taxable years specified below, shall be increased by the following amounts. These amounts represent the agreed adjustments under IRC § 482 to the intercompany transfer pricing between Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. and Penterra Biopharma International DAC with respect to both the Qualified Cost-Sharing Arrangement and the intercompany license agreement for legacy compounds:

The total agreed adjustment of Forty-Seven Million Six Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$47,600,000) represents approximately 12.51% of the originally proposed net adjustment of Three Hundred Eighty Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$380,400,000).

These agreed adjustments reflect a compromise of the positions of the Commissioner and the taxpayer with respect to both the CSA cost-sharing ratio issue and the legacy intellectual property royalty rate issue. The agreed adjustments incorporate and include the effect of any applicable correlative offsets to prevent double-counting of income between the two categories of proposed adjustments. The parties agree that no further allocation, segregation, or attribution of the agreed adjustments to one category or the other is necessary or intended for purposes of this agreement.
The agreed adjustments to taxable income result in the following additional federal income tax liabilities for each taxable year:

The total additional federal income tax due under this agreement is Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000). This amount is computed as the sum of the additional tax for each taxable year. For the taxable year ending December 31, 2017, the applicable corporate tax rate reflects the blended rate resulting from the enactment of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (Pub. L. No. 115-97), which reduced the corporate income tax rate from 35% to 21% effective January 1, 2018. Because Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. is a calendar-year taxpayer, the 2017 taxable year is subject to the pre-Tax Cuts and Jobs Act rate of 35%. For the taxable years ending December 31, 2018, December 31, 2019, and December 31, 2020, the applicable corporate income tax rate is 21%. The total additional tax of \$10,000,000 reflects the aggregate of the year-by-year computations as shown above, with such minor rounding adjustments as are reflected in the total.

The taxpayer shall pay the total additional tax of Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) to the Internal Revenue Service within sixty (60) days of the date of execution of this Closing Agreement, or upon assessment, whichever is earlier. Payment shall be made by electronic funds transfer to the United States Treasury, referencing EIN 22-3741856 and the applicable taxable years.

Interest on the additional tax determined under this Closing Agreement shall be computed at the applicable federal underpayment rate as prescribed by IRC § 6621(a)(2), compounded daily pursuant to IRC § 6622, from the respective original due date of each taxable year\'s federal income tax return (without regard to extensions) through the date on which payment of the additional tax is received by the Internal Revenue Service.

Based upon current interest rate projections and the anticipated date of payment, the estimated total interest liability across all four taxable years is approximately Two Million Eight Hundred Forty Thousand Dollars (\$2,840,000). This estimate is subject to final computation by the Internal Revenue Service upon receipt of payment and may vary depending on the actual date of payment. The taxpayer acknowledges its obligation to pay interest as finally computed by the IRS, and the IRS will provide the taxpayer with a final computation of interest due upon processing of this Closing Agreement.

No other penalties are asserted or agreed to by the parties under this Closing Agreement. The Commissioner will not assert any accuracy-related penalty under IRC § 6662(a), any negligence penalty under IRC § 6662(b)(1), any substantial understatement penalty under IRC § 6662(b)(2), or any other penalty provision of the Code with respect to the agreed adjustments for the taxable years covered by this agreement.
The total cash liability of the taxpayer under this Closing Agreement is summarized as follows:

The total estimated liability of approximately Twelve Million Eight Hundred Forty Thousand Dollars (\$12,840,000) is subject to adjustment based upon the final computation of interest by the Internal Revenue Service.

This Closing Agreement covers, and is final and conclusive with respect to, the following specific matters for the taxable years ending December 31, 2017, December 31, 2018, December 31, 2019, and December 31, 2020:
> \(d\) The correlative adjustments applicable to prevent double-counting of income between the CSA cost-sharing adjustments and the legacy intellectual property royalty rate adjustments.
This Closing Agreement does not cover, and is not final or conclusive with respect to, the following matters:

> \(c\) **State and Local Tax Consequences.** This agreement does not address, determine, or affect any state or local income tax, franchise tax, or other tax consequences that may arise from or be related to the federal income tax adjustments agreed to herein. The taxpayer acknowledges that the agreed federal adjustments may have state and local tax implications and that this agreement does not limit or preclude any state or local taxing authority from making adjustments based upon the federal adjustments reflected herein.

> \(d\) **Competent Authority Relief.** This agreement does not preclude the taxpayer from initiating a request for competent authority assistance under Article 25 (Mutual Agreement Procedure) of the Convention between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of Ireland for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital Gains (the \"U.S.-Ireland Income Tax Treaty\"), with respect to any double taxation of income that may result from the adjustments agreed to herein. The taxpayer retains the right to seek relief from double taxation through the competent authority process, and the Commissioner agrees to cooperate in any such process in accordance with applicable law and treaty obligations.

This Closing Agreement is entered into solely to resolve the specific matters covered herein for the taxable years specified. The terms and adjustments agreed to herein do not constitute a concession by either party of any legal position or factual determination, and this agreement shall not be cited, referenced, or relied upon by either party as precedent or authority in any other proceeding, examination, or matter, whether involving the taxpayer, any related entity, or any other taxpayer.

> \(b\) Marcus Whitfield, Vice President, Global Tax, is a duly authorized officer of Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. and has been authorized by the Board of Directors of Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. to execute this Closing Agreement on behalf of the taxpayer. A copy of the Board resolution authorizing Mr. Whitfield to execute this agreement has been made available to the Commissioner upon request.

> \(d\) The taxpayer has not engaged in any fraud, malfeasance, or misrepresentation of a material fact in connection with the examination, Appeals proceedings, or the negotiation and execution of this Closing Agreement.

> \(a\) The settlement reflected in this Closing Agreement is based upon Appeals Officer Castañeda\'s independent consideration of the hazards of litigation and the relative merits of the respective positions of the Commissioner and the taxpayer with respect to each of the issues resolved herein.

> \(b\) Appeals Officer Castañeda is duly authorized to execute this Closing Agreement on behalf of the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, pursuant to Delegation Order 8-3 (or its successor) and applicable IRS procedures.
> \(c\) The terms of this Closing Agreement are consistent with applicable law and with the policies and procedures of the IRS Independent Office of Appeals.

> \(a\) Consents to extend the period of limitations on assessment of federal income tax (IRS Forms 872 --- Consent to Extend the Time to Assess Tax) were executed by the taxpayer and the Commissioner for the taxable years ending December 31, 2017 and December 31, 2018. These consents extend the period within which the Commissioner may assess additional tax for those taxable years through December 31, 2024.

> \(b\) For the taxable years ending December 31, 2019 and December 31, 2020, the original three-year period of limitations under IRC § 6501(a) had not expired at the time the NOPA was issued and remains open as of the date of execution of this Closing Agreement.

> \(c\) The assessment of additional federal income tax and interest as determined under this Closing Agreement shall be made within the periods prescribed by law, as extended by agreement of the parties, and in accordance with IRC § 7121(b).
The taxpayer agrees to cooperate with the Internal Revenue Service in effecting the timely assessment of additional tax and interest in accordance with the terms of this Closing Agreement.

This Closing Agreement, upon execution by both the taxpayer and the duly authorized representative of the Commissioner, is final and conclusive as to the specific matters covered herein, and is binding upon the taxpayer, the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, and their respective successors, in accordance with IRC § 7121.

Except upon a showing of fraud or malfeasance, or misrepresentation of a material fact, neither the taxpayer nor the Commissioner may reopen, modify, set aside, or otherwise disturb the specific matters determined under this Closing Agreement. This agreement shall remain in full force and effect regardless of any subsequent change in law, regulation, or administrative interpretation, to the extent that such change applies to the taxable years covered herein.

This Closing Agreement is entered into in reliance upon the representations and warranties set forth in Part V above and upon the completeness and accuracy of the information provided by the taxpayer during the examination and Appeals proceedings.

Upon execution of this Closing Agreement by both parties, the examination of Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. (EIN: 22-3741856) for the taxable years ending December 31, 2017, December 31, 2018, December 31, 2019, and December 31, 2020, conducted under Exam Team ID LB&I-NE-TP-2022-00641, is hereby closed with respect to all matters covered by this agreement.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned have executed this Closing Agreement as of the date set forth below, each representing that he or she has the full power and authority to bind the party on whose behalf he or she signs.

The following schedule sets forth, for each taxable year covered by the Closing Agreement, the agreed adjustments to taxable income, the corrected taxable income, the additional federal income tax, the penalty determination, and the interest computation methodology:
3\. The IRC § 6662(e) substantial valuation misstatement penalty has been fully abated for all taxable years, as set forth in Section 3.4 of the Closing Agreement.
The following entities are related to the taxpayer and are relevant to the intercompany transactions covered by this Closing Agreement:
The following intercompany transactions between Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. and Penterra Biopharma International DAC are covered by this Closing Agreement:

**[MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**

**[PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT]{.underline}**

**TO:** Elaine Forsythe, Responsible Partner Howard Bellamy, Billing Partner

**FROM:** Tiffany Rosenthal, Lead Associate

**DATE:** January 3, 2024

**RE:** Confirmation of Receipt of Settlement Funds --- *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corporation, Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547 (Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, Miami-Dade County)

**MATTER/ENGAGEMENT NO.:** 1021-00003

**CLIENT:** Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. (Nasdaq: VMRK)

**[I. Purpose of Memorandum]{.underline}**

The purpose of this memorandum is to confirm that all settlement payments due under the Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release dated December 19, 2023 (the \"Settlement Agreement\") have been received in full and have cleared into the Calderwood & Harkness LLP client trust account maintained at our Miami office. This memorandum is intended to serve as the firm\'s contemporaneous internal record documenting receipt of the settlement proceeds and to outline the remaining steps necessary to conclude this engagement.

As background, the Settlement Agreement resolved all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and potential claims asserted in *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corporation, Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc., Montclair Assurance Company, and Sovereign Re Ltd.*, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, pending before the Honorable Catherine Embry in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County. The underlying dispute concerned the defendants\' denial and underpayment of a substantial business-interruption insurance claim submitted by Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. (\"VHG\" or the \"Client\") arising from hurricane damage sustained at multiple hotel and resort properties during the 2022 hurricane season.

The total aggregate settlement amount is **\$47,300,000.00** (Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars and 00/100). All four insurer defendants --- Ironclad Indemnity Corporation (\"Ironclad\"), Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. (\"Pinnacle\"), Montclair Assurance Company (\"Montclair\"), and Sovereign Re Ltd. (\"Sovereign Re\") --- have funded their respective shares of the settlement in accordance with the Payment Allocation Schedule set forth in Exhibit A to the Settlement Agreement. Each wire transfer has been received and has fully cleared through the firm\'s trust account, and no amounts remain outstanding from any settling party. As detailed below, all payments were received well in advance of the contractual payment deadline.

**[II. Settlement Agreement Reference]{.underline}**

The definitive Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release was executed on December 19, 2023, by all parties to the litigation --- VHG as plaintiff, and Ironclad, Pinnacle, Montclair, and Sovereign Re as defendants --- as well as by their respective counsel of record. The Settlement Agreement memorialized the terms previously agreed upon in the Term Sheet executed on December 5, 2023, during a two-day mediation session conducted before the Honorable Richard Mendelson (Ret.) at Keystone Dispute Resolution Inc. in Miami, Florida.

Section 3.1 of the Settlement Agreement obligated the four insurer defendants to make lump-sum payment of their respective settlement shares within forty-five (45) calendar days following execution of the Settlement Agreement, establishing a contractual payment deadline of **February 2, 2024**. As described more fully below, all four payments were received and cleared no later than January 2, 2024 --- a full thirty-one (31) days in advance of the contractual deadline.

The specific allocation of the aggregate settlement amount among the four insurer defendants was governed by Exhibit A to the Settlement Agreement (the \"Payment Allocation Schedule\"), which set forth each insurer\'s pro rata share based on the applicable insurance tower layer. The Payment Allocation Schedule was negotiated during the mediation and reflected a layered allocation roughly proportional to each insurer\'s exposure within the insurance program, with the primary carrier bearing the largest share and the upper-layer excess carriers bearing progressively smaller shares. The precise allocation is detailed in Section III below.

The Settlement Agreement also contains a mutual release of all claims (Section 4), a confidentiality provision governing the settlement amount (Section 7), representations and warranties of authority (Section 5), and a provision requiring the parties to file a Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice within thirty (30) days of receipt of all settlement payments (Section 6). The status of the stipulation of dismissal is addressed in Section VI.B below.

**[III. Summary of Funds Received]{.underline}**

**A. Table of Wire Receipts**

The following table sets forth the details of the four wire transfers received from the settling defendants, including the paying party, applicable policy number, layer position, settlement amount, wire initiation date, date funds cleared, and the identity of sending counsel:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Paying Party**                 **Policy No.**       **Layer**                                                 **Settlement Amount**   **Date Wire Initiated**   **Date Funds Cleared**   **Sending Counsel / Entity**
  -------------------------------- -------------------- --------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------- ------------------------- ------------------------ --------------------------------------------------
  Ironclad Indemnity Corporation   IIC-PRP-2022-07541   Primary (\$25M limit, \$500K per-occurrence deductible)   \$24,500,000.00         December 28, 2023         December 29, 2023        Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP (Gregory Stanton)

  Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc.      PSL-XS1-2022-3390    1st Excess (\$15M xs \$25M)                               \$12,200,000.00         December 28, 2023         December 29, 2023        Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP (Gregory Stanton)

  Montclair Assurance Company      MAC-XS2-2022-09817   2nd Excess (\$10M xs \$40M)                               \$6,800,000.00          December 29, 2023         January 2, 2024          Delvecchio & Kraus LLP (Patricia Kraus)

  Sovereign Re Ltd.                SRL-XS3-2022-5102    3rd Excess (\$10M xs \$50M)                               \$3,800,000.00          December 29, 2023         January 2, 2024          Delvecchio & Kraus LLP (Patricia Kraus)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Copies of the bank wire confirmation receipts for each of the above transfers are included as **Attachment 1** to this memorandum.

**B. Aggregate Confirmation**

The total funds received across all four wire transfers are calculated as follows:

> \$24,500,000.00 (Ironclad Indemnity Corporation) + \$12,200,000.00 (Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc.) + \$6,800,000.00 (Montclair Assurance Company) + \$3,800,000.00 (Sovereign Re Ltd.) = **\$47,300,000.00 (Total)**

The total of **\$47,300,000.00** matches, to the penny, the aggregate settlement amount set forth in (i) the Term Sheet executed on December 5, 2023, at the mediation before the Honorable Richard Mendelson (Ret.) at Keystone Dispute Resolution Inc., and (ii) the definitive Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release dated December 19, 2023. There is no discrepancy, and no additional amounts remain due from any of the insurer defendants.

All funds are currently held in Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s Interest on Lawyers\' Trust Account (\"IOLTA\") / client trust account, maintained at Stonefield Trust Bank, at the firm\'s Miami office located at 333 SE 2nd Avenue, Suite 4400, Miami, Florida 33131. The funds remain in the trust account pending disbursement to the Client in accordance with the procedures described in Section VI.A below and in compliance with Rule 5-1.1 of the Rules Regulating The Florida Bar (Trust Accounts).

**[IV. Wire Transfer Details]{.underline}**

**A. Ironclad and Pinnacle Payments**

Wire instructions for the Calderwood & Harkness LLP client trust account were transmitted to Gregory Stanton of Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP via letter dated December 20, 2023. That letter was prepared by the undersigned and included the firm\'s full wire routing information, ABA routing number, beneficiary account details, and reference information identifying the matter and applicable Settlement Agreement section. A copy of the wire instruction letter is included as part of **Attachment 3** to this memorandum.

Ironclad Indemnity Corporation\'s payment of **\$24,500,000.00** and Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc.\'s payment of **\$12,200,000.00** were each wired separately on **December 28, 2023**. Both wires were initiated through the same sending institution, which is consistent with the fact that Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP served as joint defense counsel for both Ironclad and Pinnacle in this matter. Both transfers were confirmed as fully cleared and available in the Calderwood & Harkness client trust account on **December 29, 2023**, the next business day.

The combined payment received from Ironclad and Pinnacle totals **\$36,700,000.00**, representing approximately 77.6% of the total aggregate settlement.

It bears noting that Ironclad\'s settlement payment of \$24,500,000.00 represents its full primary policy layer limit of \$25,000,000.00 less the \$500,000.00 per-occurrence deductible that is retained by VHG under the terms of Policy No. IIC-PRP-2022-07541. The deductible was not at issue in the litigation and was not a component of the settlement, as VHG had already absorbed the deductible amount. Accordingly, Ironclad\'s payment of \$24,500,000.00 effectively constitutes a settlement at 100% of its net exposure under the primary layer, exclusive of the deductible.

**B. Montclair and Sovereign Re Payments**

Wire instructions for the Calderwood & Harkness LLP client trust account were separately transmitted to Patricia Kraus of Delvecchio & Kraus LLP via letter also dated December 20, 2023, prepared by the undersigned. The wire instruction letter to Delvecchio & Kraus contained the same trust account routing and beneficiary information as the letter to Fendowell Rourke & Stanton, with appropriate reference information for the Montclair and Sovereign Re policy layers. A copy of this letter is also included as part of **Attachment 3** to this memorandum.

Montclair Assurance Company\'s payment of **\$6,800,000.00** and Sovereign Re Ltd.\'s payment of **\$3,800,000.00** were each wired separately on **December 29, 2023**. Although the wires were initiated on December 29, the funds did not clear and become available in the Calderwood & Harkness client trust account until **January 2, 2024**. The three-business-day clearing delay was attributable to the intervening New Year\'s holiday weekend; December 30 and 31, 2023, fell on Saturday and Sunday, respectively, and January 1, 2024, was a federal bank holiday. No portion of the delay was attributable to any funding deficiency, hold, or issue with the wire transfers themselves.

The combined payment received from Montclair and Sovereign Re totals **\$10,600,000.00**, representing approximately 22.4% of the total aggregate settlement.

I confirmed receipt of all four wires directly with our firm\'s trust account administrator, Daniel Carrillo, on the morning of January 2, 2024, and obtained copies of the bank wire confirmation receipts at that time. Mr. Carrillo confirmed that all four wires were received without incident and that the full aggregate balance of \$47,300,000.00 is reflected in the trust account ledger for Matter No. 1021-00003.

**[V. Reconciliation Against Settlement Terms]{.underline}**

For purposes of evaluating the settlement outcome in the context of VHG\'s total claimed losses, the following reconciliation sets forth each insurer\'s settlement share as a percentage of its respective policy layer limit:

> **Ironclad Indemnity Corporation (Primary Layer)** Settlement Amount: \$24,500,000.00 Policy Layer Limit: \$25,000,000.00 (subject to \$500,000 per-occurrence deductible) Net Layer Exposure (after deductible): \$24,500,000.00 Recovery as Percentage of Net Layer: **100.0%**
>
> **Pinnacle Surplus Lines Inc. (1st Excess Layer)** Settlement Amount: \$12,200,000.00 Policy Layer Limit: \$15,000,000.00 excess of \$25,000,000 Recovery as Percentage of Layer Limit: **81.33%**
>
> **Montclair Assurance Company (2nd Excess Layer)** Settlement Amount: \$6,800,000.00 Policy Layer Limit: \$10,000,000.00 excess of \$40,000,000 Recovery as Percentage of Layer Limit: **68.0%**
>
> **Sovereign Re Ltd. (3rd Excess Layer)** Settlement Amount: \$3,800,000.00 Policy Layer Limit: \$10,000,000.00 excess of \$50,000,000 Recovery as Percentage of Layer Limit: **38.0%**

The descending recovery percentages across the insurance tower are consistent with the settlement dynamics observed during the mediation. Ironclad, as the primary carrier, faced the greatest exposure and the weakest coverage defenses at the lower layer, and accordingly settled at the effective maximum of its net liability. The upper-layer excess carriers obtained progressively steeper discounts commensurate with the increasing uncertainty as to whether VHG\'s total provable loss would fully penetrate each successive layer. In particular, Sovereign Re\'s position at the \$50 million excess attachment point afforded it significant leverage given the disputed quantum of VHG\'s business-interruption losses in the range above \$50 million.

In aggregate, the total settlement of **\$47,300,000.00** represents recovery of approximately **78.83%** of VHG\'s total asserted business-interruption claim of \$60,000,000.00, as quantified in the expert report of Dr. Lawrence Pemberton of Meridian Forensic Economics dated June 14, 2023. While VHG did not recover 100% of its claimed loss, the settlement amount represents an excellent result in light of the contested coverage issues --- particularly the defendants\' period-of-restoration arguments and the anti-concurrent-causation defenses raised by Pinnacle and Montclair --- and avoids the inherent risk, delay, and expense of a trial that was scheduled to commence on February 26, 2024.

All amounts set forth in the Settlement Agreement and received via wire transfer match the Payment Allocation Schedule set forth in Exhibit A to the Settlement Agreement. A copy of Exhibit A is included as **Attachment 2** to this memorandum.

**[VI. Next Steps]{.underline}**

**A. Client Disbursement**

Now that all settlement funds have been received and confirmed, the next step is the preparation and transmission of a Disbursement Letter to VHG\'s General Counsel, Nathaniel Driscoll, setting forth the calculation of net settlement proceeds to be disbursed to the Client after deduction of Calderwood & Harkness\'s legal fees and reimbursement of expenses advanced by the firm during the course of the engagement.

Howard Bellamy, as Billing Partner, should prepare and transmit this Disbursement Letter calculating the net settlement proceeds. The anticipated fee and expense deductions are summarized as follows:

> **Legal Fees**
>
> • *Total Hourly Fees:* Approximately **\$2,684,700.00**, representing approximately 3,420 hours of professional time billed at a blended rate of approximately \$785.00 per hour. This figure encompasses all partner, associate, and paralegal time recorded to Matter No. 1021-00003 from inception of the engagement through the date of settlement. A final time audit is being conducted by the billing department and is expected to be completed by January 4, 2024.
>
> • *Contingency Enhancement:* **\$865,000.00**, calculated as 5% of the net recovery above \$30,000,000.00 (i.e., 5% × \$17,300,000.00 = \$865,000.00). The contingency enhancement was provided for in Section 4(c) of the Amended Engagement Letter dated September 12, 2022, which was approved by Nathaniel Driscoll on behalf of VHG\'s Board of Directors and provides for a success fee of 5% on any recovery exceeding the \$30 million threshold.
>
> • *Total Fees (Hourly + Contingency Enhancement):* Approximately **\$3,549,700.00**.
>
> **Expenses Advanced**
>
> • *Total Expenses Advanced:* Approximately **\$412,000.00**, encompassing the following principal categories:
>
> • Expert witness fees for Meridian Forensic Economics (Dr. Lawrence Pemberton, forensic accounting and damages quantification): approximately \$218,000.00
>
> • Expert witness fees for Caldwell Engineering Associates (structural engineering and causation analysis): approximately \$104,000.00
>
> • Court filing fees and service of process costs: approximately \$3,800.00
>
> • Deposition transcription and videography costs (32 depositions): approximately \$47,500.00
>
> • Mediation fees (Keystone Dispute Resolution Inc., two sessions): approximately \$22,000.00
>
> • Travel and related costs (depositions, site inspections, mediation): approximately \$11,200.00
>
> • Document hosting and e-discovery platform costs (Relativity): approximately \$5,500.00
>
> **Net Settlement Proceeds to Client**
>
> • Gross Settlement Proceeds: \$47,300,000.00
>
> • Less Total Fees: (\$3,549,700.00)
>
> • Less Expenses Advanced: (\$412,000.00)
>
> • **Estimated Net Proceeds to VHG: \$43,338,300.00** (subject to final time audit and expense reconciliation)

The target date for preparation and transmission of the Disbursement Letter to Nathaniel Driscoll is **January 4, 2024**. Upon receipt of VHG\'s written authorization to disburse, funds will be wired from the Calderwood & Harkness trust account to VHG\'s designated operating account in accordance with the Client\'s written instructions.

**B. Stipulation of Dismissal**

The draft Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice (the \"Stipulation\") was circulated by the undersigned to defense counsel --- Gregory Stanton at Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP and Patricia Kraus at Delvecchio & Kraus LLP --- on December 22, 2023. Minor comments were received from Mr. Stanton on December 27, 2023, and have been incorporated into the revised draft.

The final agreed-upon version of the Stipulation is expected to be executed by all parties and filed with the Clerk of the Eleventh Judicial Circuit, Miami-Dade County, in Case No. 2022-CA-031547, promptly upon finalization. A Proposed Order of Dismissal with Prejudice will be submitted to the Honorable Catherine Embry contemporaneously with the filing of the Stipulation.

The undersigned will coordinate directly with Gregory Stanton and Patricia Kraus to obtain all necessary signature pages from the defendant parties and their counsel. All signature pages will be collected electronically to facilitate timely filing.

92: **Section 2.1** **Amount.** In consideration of the releases, covenants, and other obligations set forth in this Agreement, NovaSpark shall pay to Lumos a lump-sum settlement payment in the amount of Four Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$4,350,000.00) (the \"Settlement Payment\"). The Settlement Payment shall constitute the total monetary consideration payable by Defendants to Lumos under this Agreement, subject to the separate forensic cost allocation set forth in Section 4.6.
93: **Section 2.2** **Payment Deadline.** The Settlement Payment shall be due and payable in full within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date, that is, no later than October 22, 2023. Time is of the essence with respect to the payment obligation set forth in this Section.
94: **Section 2.3** **Method of Payment.** The Settlement Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States dollars to a bank account designated in writing by Lumos or its counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP. Lumos shall provide complete wire transfer instructions to Defendants\' counsel, Whitfield, Raines & Gerber LLP, within five (5) business days of the Effective Date. Such wire instructions shall be substantially in the form set forth in Exhibit B attached hereto. The Settlement Payment shall be deemed received on the date the funds are credited to the designated account. NovaSpark shall bear all wire transfer fees and bank charges associated with the transmission of the Settlement Payment.
95: **Section 2.4** **Late Payment.** In the event that the Settlement Payment is not received in full by Lumos on or before October 22, 2023, the unpaid amount shall accrue interest at the rate of ten percent (10%) per annum, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower, calculated from the due date until the date of actual receipt by Lumos. In the event that the Settlement Payment, together with any accrued interest, is not received in full within ten (10) business days after the due date of October 22, 2023, Lumos may, at its sole election: (a) enforce the full amount of the Settlement Payment and accrued interest as a judgment in the Court or any court of competent jurisdiction, and Defendants hereby consent to the entry of such judgment; (b) pursue all available legal and equitable remedies for Defendants\' breach, including the reopening of the Action and the pursuit of all claims asserted therein; or (c) exercise any combination of the foregoing remedies. The exercise of any remedy under this Section shall not constitute an election of remedies or waiver of any other right or remedy available to Lumos under this Agreement, at law, or in equity.
96: **Section 2.5** **Joint and Several Liability.** The obligation to make the Settlement Payment, including any interest accruing thereon pursuant to Section 2.4, is a joint and several obligation of NovaSpark Technologies Inc., Rajiv Anand, Serena Mallick, and Derek Yun. Lumos may enforce the Settlement Payment obligation against any one or more Defendants, jointly or severally, without being required to proceed first against any particular Defendant or to exhaust any remedy against any other Defendant.
97: **Section 2.6** **Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of any and all taxes, including federal, state, and local income taxes, self-employment taxes, and any other taxes or assessments, arising from or attributable to the Settlement Payment or any other consideration received by such Party under this Agreement. NovaSpark shall issue such tax reporting documentation (including, if applicable, IRS Form 1099) as may be required by applicable law in connection with the Settlement Payment. No Party makes any representation or warranty to any other Party regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of the Settlement Payment or any other aspect of this Agreement, and each Party acknowledges that it has been advised to consult with its own tax advisors regarding such matters.

**6.1 Confidential Treatment.** The Parties agree that the existence and terms of this Agreement, including without limitation the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule, the nature and scope of the mutual releases, and all related negotiations, mediation proceedings, communications, and documents exchanged in connection therewith, shall be treated as strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party, except as follows:

**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

In addition, in the event of any late payment or failure to pay, CPS shall be entitled to recover from Harlow its reasonable attorneys\' fees, costs, and expenses incurred in collecting the Settlement Payment, including without limitation fees and costs incurred in any enforcement action. The obligations of confidentiality set forth in this Section 7.1 shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement and shall continue in perpetuity.

**Section 7.3 --- Public Disclosure of Existence.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Parties acknowledge and agree that they may publicly disclose the fact that the Action has been settled and that the Action has been or will be dismissed with prejudice, including by means of press releases, public filings, investor communications, or statements to the media. > \(b\) *Authority.* VMS has full power, authority, and legal right to enter into this Agreement and to perform each and every obligation of VMS hereunder, including, without limitation, the payment of the Settlement Amount, the granting of the releases set forth in Article 4, and the dismissal of VMS\'s counterclaims in the Action.
