lines.text: **Section 4.6** **Cost Allocation.** The total fees of Brindoval Digital Forensics LLC for all services rendered in connection with the Action, including the forensic imaging conducted from March 22 through April 14, 2023, the issuance of the Preliminary Forensic Report dated May 1, 2023, and the Forensic Remediation contemplated by this Article IV, are Two Hundred Eighteen Thousand Six Hundred Dollars (\$218,600.00). Defendants shall bear sixty percent (60%) of Brindoval\'s total fees, in the amount of One Hundred Thirty-One Thousand One Hundred Sixty Dollars (\$131,160.00). Lumos shall bear forty percent (40%) of Brindoval\'s total fees, in the amount of Eighty-Seven Thousand Four Hundred Forty Dollars (\$87,440.00). Each Party shall pay its allocated share directly to Brindoval within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of Brindoval\'s final invoice for services rendered. The obligations under this Section 4.6 are independent of the Settlement Payment obligation set forth in Article II.

**Section 6.1** **Release by Lumos.** Effective upon both (a) receipt by Lumos of the Settlement Payment in full in accordance with Article II and (b) issuance by Brindoval of the Final Forensic Remediation Certification in accordance with Section 4.2, Lumos, on behalf of itself and its officers, directors, shareholders, employees, agents, parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, predecessors, successors, and assigns, hereby releases and forever discharges Defendants---NovaSpark Technologies Inc., Rajiv Anand, Serena Mallick, and Derek Yun---and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, personal representatives, successors, assigns, officers, directors, employees, agents, and attorneys (including the law firm of Whitfield, Raines & Gerber LLP and each of its partners, associates, and staff), from any and all claims, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, damages, judgments, executions, demands, and liabilities of any kind or nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, at law or in equity, that Lumos ever had, now has, or may hereafter have against Defendants, arising from, relating to, or in any way connected with the facts, circumstances, transactions, occurrences, claims, and causes of action alleged in or that could have been alleged in the Action.

> \(a\) any obligation of any Defendant under this Agreement, including without limitation the obligation to make the Settlement Payment, to cooperate with the Forensic Remediation, and to comply with the restrictive covenants set forth in Article V;

**Section 7.1** **Stipulation for Dismissal.** Within five (5) business days following the satisfaction of both of the following conditions: (a) receipt by Lumos of the Settlement Payment in full in accordance with Article II, and (b) issuance by Brindoval of the Final Forensic Remediation Certification in accordance with Section 4.2, the Parties, through their respective counsel, shall execute and file with the Court a Stipulation and Proposed Order of Dismissal with Prejudice of the entire Action, including all claims, counterclaims, and cross-claims asserted or that could have been asserted therein, with each side to bear its own costs of suit and attorneys\' fees except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement. In the event that the Court requires a hearing or other proceeding in connection with the dismissal, the Parties and their respective counsel shall appear and cooperate to secure the dismissal.

**Section 9.1** **Confidentiality of Settlement Terms.** The Parties agree that the terms of this Agreement, including without limitation the Settlement Payment amount and all other financial terms, the terms of the Forensic Remediation, and the specific restrictive covenant provisions herein, are confidential and shall not be disclosed by any Party to any third party, except as follows:

**Section 9.2** **Public Statements.** Any public statement by any Party regarding the resolution of the Action, whether made to the press, media, investors, customers, employees, or any other audience, shall be limited to stating that \"the matter has been resolved to the mutual satisfaction of the parties,\" or such other statement as the Parties may mutually agree upon in writing. No Party shall disclose the Settlement Payment amount, the specific terms of the Forensic Remediation, or the specific restrictive covenants set forth herein in any public statement without the prior written consent of all other Parties.

**Section 11.1** **Material Breach.** The following shall each constitute a material breach of this Agreement: (a) any failure by any Defendant to make the Settlement Payment in accordance with Article II; (b) any breach of the restrictive covenants set forth in Article V, including the personal trade secret covenant in Section 5.1 and the independent development obligation in Section 5.2; (c) any violation by any Defendant of the Stipulated Permanent Injunction entered pursuant to Article III; (d) any failure by any Defendant to cooperate fully with the Forensic Remediation as required by Article IV; (e) any breach of the representation and warranty set forth in Section 10.4 regarding undisclosed materials; and (f) any breach of the confidentiality provisions set forth in Article IX or the non-disparagement provisions set forth in Article VIII, provided that a breach of Article VIII or Article IX shall be material only if it causes or is reasonably likely to cause material harm to the non-breaching Party.
> **Reference / Memo:** Settlement Payment --- Lumos Analytics Inc. v. NovaSpark Technologies Inc. et al., Case No. 23-CV-004871

> \(g\) \"**Service Credits**\" or \"**Settlement Credits**\" means the credits in the aggregate amount of Four Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$485,000) to be applied against Pinnacle\'s subscription invoices during the Renewal Term in the manner set forth in Section 2.1 of this Agreement and as detailed in Exhibit B hereto.
**[ARTICLE 2 --- SETTLEMENT CONSIDERATION]{.underline}**

In full and final settlement of all Released Claims, Lumos shall provide Pinnacle with service credits in the aggregate amount of Four Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$485,000) (the \"**Settlement Credits**\"). The Settlement Credits shall be applied as a lump-sum credit against Pinnacle\'s first four (4) monthly subscription invoices issued during the Renewal Term, at One Hundred Twenty-One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$121,250) per invoice (i.e., \$485,000 ÷ 4 = \$121,250 per month). Specifically, the Settlement Credits shall be applied against invoices for the following billing periods: January 2024, February 2024, March 2024, and April 2024.

The monthly subscription fee during the Renewal Term shall be One Hundred Fifteen Thousand Dollars (\$115,000) per month (being \$1,380,000 per annum ÷ 12 months = \$115,000 per month). Accordingly, for each of the first four (4) months of the Renewal Term, the Settlement Credit installment of \$121,250 shall fully offset the \$115,000 monthly subscription invoice, with the remaining Six Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$6,250) per month carried forward as a credit against the next succeeding invoice, until the full \$485,000 in Settlement Credits has been applied and exhausted. The detailed application schedule, including the treatment of carryforward credits, is set forth in Exhibit B attached hereto. The Parties acknowledge that, based on the credit application schedule set forth in Exhibit B, all Settlement Credits shall be fully consumed no later than the May 2024 invoice cycle.

The Parties acknowledge and agree that the settlement consideration consists solely of the Service Credits described in Section 2.1 of this Agreement, and that Lumos shall not be required to make any cash payment, wire transfer, or other monetary disbursement of any kind to Pinnacle in connection with this Agreement or the settlement of the Released Claims contemplated hereby. Pinnacle acknowledges that the Service Credits, together with the MSA renewal and amendment terms described in Article 3, constitute full and adequate consideration for the releases and other commitments made by Pinnacle in this Agreement.

The Parties shall treat the Settlement Credits as a reduction in the purchase price for the Services provided under the MSA for all applicable federal, state, and local tax purposes. Neither Party shall take any position on any tax return or in any tax proceeding that is inconsistent with such treatment unless required to do so by a final determination of a court of competent jurisdiction or a taxing authority. Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations, including the payment of any income taxes, franchise taxes, or other taxes arising from or related to this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby. Neither Party makes any representation or warranty to the other Party regarding the tax consequences of the settlement consideration provided hereunder.

As a material inducement to Lumos\'s agreement to provide the Settlement Credits, and as additional consideration for this Agreement, Pinnacle agrees to renew the MSA for a Renewal Term of two (2) years, commencing on January 15, 2024 and expiring on January 14, 2026, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in MSA Amendment No. 1 executed concurrently herewith. The annual subscription fee during the Renewal Term shall be One Million Three Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars (\$1,380,000), reflecting a reduction of Sixty Thousand Dollars (\$60,000) per annum (approximately 4.17%) from the annual subscription fee of \$1,440,000 applicable during the initial term of the MSA. The total contract value for the Renewal Term shall be Two Million Seven Hundred Sixty Thousand Dollars (\$2,760,000) (\$1,380,000 × 2 years). Payment of the Renewal Term subscription fees shall be made in monthly installments of \$115,000 each, invoiced and payable in accordance with the payment terms set forth in the MSA, as amended by MSA Amendment No. 1.

This Agreement, the settlement contemplated herein, and the provision of the Settlement Credits do not constitute, and shall not be construed or deemed to constitute, an admission of liability, fault, wrongdoing, breach of contract, breach of duty, negligence, or any other form of culpability or responsibility on the part of either Party or any of its Affiliates. Neither this Agreement, nor any of its terms, provisions, recitals, or exhibits, nor the fact of its execution, nor any statements, communications, or conduct occurring during the course of the mediation or any settlement negotiations between the Parties, may be offered, received, or admitted in evidence in any judicial, administrative, arbitral, or other proceeding for any purpose, including without limitation as an admission or concession of liability, fault, wrongdoing, or breach by either Party. Each Party enters into this Agreement solely for the purpose of resolving the disputes described in the Recitals hereof and avoiding the expense, burden, distraction, and uncertainty associated with continued dispute resolution or litigation. The provisions of this Section 5.1 are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any protections afforded by Federal Rule of Evidence 408 or analogous state evidentiary rules or statutes.

The Parties agree that the existence of this Agreement, the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including without limitation the amount of the Settlement Credits, the financial terms of the Renewal Term (including the reduced subscription pricing), any drafts or proposals exchanged during the negotiation of this Agreement, and any negotiations, discussions, communications, or proceedings leading to this Agreement, shall be kept strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed, published, or otherwise communicated to any third party (collectively, the \"**Confidential Settlement Information**\"), except as expressly permitted by Section 6.2 of this Agreement.

The following table sets forth the manner in which the Settlement Credits in the aggregate amount of Four Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$485,000) shall be applied against Pinnacle\'s monthly subscription invoices during the Renewal Term:
> 1\. **Total Settlement Credits:** \$485,000.

> 2\. **Application Method:** The Settlement Credits are applied at \$121,250 per invoice against the first four (4) monthly invoices of the Renewal Term (January 2024 through April 2024). Because each monthly Settlement Credit installment of \$121,250 exceeds the monthly subscription fee of \$115,000 by \$6,250, the excess \$6,250 per month is carried forward as a credit against the next succeeding invoice.

> 4\. **Full Exhaustion:** All Settlement Credits shall be fully applied and exhausted by the May 2024 invoice cycle. Beginning with the June 2024 invoice and continuing through the end of the Renewal Term (January 2026), Pinnacle shall pay the full monthly subscription fee of \$115,000 without offset or credit.

> 6\. **Total Renewal Term Contract Value:** \$2,760,000 (\$1,380,000 × 2 years), before application of the Settlement Credits. After application of the \$485,000 in Settlement Credits, the net contract value payable by Pinnacle during the Renewal Term is \$2,275,000.

**2.4 Claims Administrator.** The Parties agree that Meridian Settlement Services LLC shall be appointed as the Claims Administrator for purposes of this Settlement, subject to Court approval. The Claims Administrator shall perform all settlement administration tasks as set forth in this Agreement, including but not limited to mailing of Notice, processing of Opt-Out requests and Objections, calculating Individual Settlement Payments, establishing and maintaining the Qualified Settlement Fund, issuing settlement checks, performing tax reporting, and maintaining the Settlement Website and toll-free telephone number.
**[SECTION 3 --- SETTLEMENT CONSIDERATION]{.underline}**

**3.1 Gross Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of the Action and all Released Claims, AMA shall cause to be paid, or shall pay, the total, maximum, all-inclusive, and non-reversionary sum of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,750,000.00) (the \"Gross Settlement Amount\" or \"GSA\"). The GSA constitutes the total maximum monetary obligation of AMA under this Settlement and includes all payments described in this Section 3, including without limitation the Net Settlement Fund, Attorneys\' Fees, Litigation Costs, Class Representative Service Awards, Settlement Administration Costs, and the PAGA Payment. AMA shall have no obligation to pay any amount in excess of the GSA, except for the employer\'s share of payroll taxes as set forth in Section 4.4 of this Agreement.

AMA shall deposit the GSA into a Qualified Settlement Fund (\"QSF\") established and maintained by the Claims Administrator within fourteen (14) calendar days of the Effective Date. The QSF shall be established as a qualified settlement fund within the meaning of Section 468B of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, and the Treasury Regulations promulgated thereunder. AMA shall be responsible for coordinating with Pemberton Mutual Assurance Co. regarding the timely transmittal of the carrier\'s contribution to the QSF. In the event that Pemberton\'s funding is delayed beyond the fourteen (14) day funding deadline, AMA shall advance the full GSA to the QSF and shall seek reimbursement from Pemberton directly, such that the funding deadline shall not be extended on account of any delay by Pemberton.

> **(a) Attorneys\' Fees.** Class Counsel shall apply to the Court for an award of attorneys\' fees in the amount of thirty-three and one-third percent (33.33%) of the GSA, which equals Four Million Nine Hundred Sixteen Thousand One Hundred Seventy-Five Dollars (\$4,916,175.00). The attorneys\' fee award shall be paid from the GSA, and AMA shall have no separate or additional obligation to pay attorneys\' fees beyond the amount approved by the Court from the GSA. AMA agrees that it will not oppose an attorneys\' fee request in an amount up to and including thirty-three and one-third percent (33.33%) of the GSA. The Court\'s determination of the appropriate attorneys\' fee award, including any reduction in the requested amount, is not a material term or condition of this Settlement and shall not provide a basis for termination of this Agreement. Any reduction in the attorneys\' fee award by the Court below the requested amount shall be added to the Net Settlement Fund and distributed to Participating Class Members. The attorneys\' fee award shall compensate Class Counsel for all work performed and costs advanced in connection with the prosecution of this Action, the negotiation and administration of this Settlement, and any related proceedings.

> **(b) Litigation Costs.** Class Counsel shall apply to the Court for reimbursement of reasonable litigation costs and expenses actually incurred in the prosecution of this Action, in an amount not to exceed Four Hundred Twelve Thousand Three Hundred Dollars (\$412,300.00). Such costs include, but are not limited to, filing fees, deposition costs, expert witness fees and expenses, document review and production costs, mediation fees, photocopying and printing costs, travel expenses, and other out-of-pocket litigation expenses. Class Counsel shall submit documentation of such costs with their fee petition. AMA agrees that it will not oppose a cost reimbursement request in an amount up to and including Four Hundred Twelve Thousand Three Hundred Dollars (\$412,300.00). The Court\'s determination of the appropriate cost reimbursement, including any reduction in the requested amount, is not a material term or condition of this Settlement and shall not provide a basis for termination of this Agreement. Any reduction in the cost reimbursement by the Court below the requested amount shall be added to the Net Settlement Fund and distributed to Participating Class Members.

> The total Class Representative Service Awards shall not exceed Thirty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$35,000.00). The Service Awards shall be paid from the GSA and are in addition to any Individual Settlement Payment that the Class Representatives may receive as Participating Class Members. AMA agrees that it will not oppose service award requests up to and including the amounts stated above. The Court\'s determination of the appropriate service awards, including any reduction in the requested amounts, is not a material term or condition of this Settlement and shall not provide a basis for termination of this Agreement. Any reduction in the service awards by the Court below the requested amounts shall be added to the Net Settlement Fund and distributed to Participating Class Members.

> **(d) Settlement Administration Costs.** The reasonable costs and expenses incurred by the Claims Administrator in administering the Settlement shall be paid from the GSA in an amount not to exceed Three Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$385,000.00). The Claims Administrator shall submit itemized invoices to Class Counsel and Defense Counsel for review on a monthly basis during the administration period, and neither Class Counsel nor Defense Counsel shall unreasonably withhold approval of such invoices. Any dispute regarding the reasonableness of the Claims Administrator\'s fees and expenses shall be submitted to the Court for resolution. Any unused portion of the Settlement Administration Costs budget shall be added to the Net Settlement Fund and distributed to Participating Class Members.

> **(e) PAGA Payment.** Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$750,000.00) of the GSA shall be allocated to the PAGA Payment, representing the civil penalties component of the Settlement attributable to PAGA claims asserted in this Action. The PAGA Payment shall be distributed as follows: seventy-five percent (75%) of the PAGA Payment, which equals Five Hundred Sixty-Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$562,500.00), shall be paid to the LWDA; and twenty-five percent (25%) of the PAGA Payment, which equals One Hundred Eighty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$187,500.00), shall be distributed to Aggrieved Employees (i.e., all Participating Class Members who do not opt out of the Settlement Class), pro rata based on the same allocation formula set forth in Section 4.1, in addition to their Individual Settlement Payments from the Net Settlement Fund. The Claims Administrator shall remit the LWDA\'s seventy-five percent (75%) share of the PAGA Payment directly to the LWDA at the address specified by the LWDA, within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date.

> **(f) Net Settlement Fund.** The Net Settlement Fund (\"NSF\") shall equal the GSA minus the sum of the Court-approved Attorneys\' Fees, Litigation Costs, Class Representative Service Awards, Settlement Administration Costs, and PAGA Payment. 199: **4.3 Estimated Average Individual Payment.** Based on the estimated NSF of Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty-One Thousand Five Hundred Twenty-Five Dollars (\$8,251,525.00) and an estimated class size of approximately 1,850 Participating Class Members, the estimated average Individual Settlement Payment is approximately Four Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Dollars (\$4,460.00). Actual Individual Settlement Payments will vary based on each Participating Class Member\'s individual workweeks and overtime hours worked during the Class Period, as well as the total number of Opt-Outs and the final Court-approved deductions from the GSA. Some Participating Class Members may receive more or less than the estimated average depending on their individual circumstances.
200: **4.4 Tax Treatment of Individual Settlement Payments.** Each Individual Settlement Payment shall be allocated for tax purposes as follows:
201: > \(a\) **Wage Portion (50%).** Fifty percent (50%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as wages for services rendered, and shall be subject to applicable federal and state income tax withholding and employee-side payroll taxes, including the employee\'s share of FICA (Social Security and Medicare taxes) and applicable state payroll taxes. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form W-2.
202: > \(b\) **Interest and Penalties Portion (33.33%).** Thirty-three and one-third percent (33.33%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as interest and penalties, which are not subject to withholding but are generally taxable as ordinary income to the recipient. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC (or such other form as may be required by applicable tax law at the time of distribution).
203: > \(c\) **Non-Wage Damages Portion (16.67%).** Sixteen and sixty-seven hundredths percent (16.67%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as non-wage damages, which are not subject to withholding. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC (or such other form as may be required by applicable tax law at the time of distribution).
204: AMA shall be responsible for paying the employer\'s share of payroll taxes (including the employer\'s share of FICA and applicable federal and state unemployment taxes) on the wage portion of Individual Settlement Payments. The employer\'s share of payroll taxes shall be paid by AMA separately from the GSA and shall not be deducted from the NSF or from any Participating Class Member\'s Individual Settlement Payment. Neither Class Counsel, Defense Counsel, nor the Claims Administrator makes any representation or warranty regarding the tax treatment of any Individual Settlement Payment, and each Participating Class Member is encouraged to consult with a qualified tax advisor regarding the tax consequences of his or her Individual Settlement Payment.
205: **4.5 Distribution Timeline.** The Claims Administrator shall mail Individual Settlement Payment checks to Participating Class Members within thirty (30) calendar days of the date on which the GSA is fully funded in the QSF. Checks shall be valid for one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from the date of issuance and shall bear a legend indicating the void-after date. Prior to mailing settlement checks, the Claims Administrator shall perform a National Change of Address (\"NCOA\") search for all Settlement Class Members to update mailing addresses. The Claims Administrator shall make reasonable efforts to locate Participating Class Members whose settlement checks are returned as undeliverable by the United States Postal Service, including performing skip-tracing using commercially available databases. If, after such efforts, a Participating Class Member\'s updated address is identified, the Claims Administrator shall re-mail the check to the updated address. If, despite such efforts, a Participating Class Member cannot be located or a check remains undeliverable, the funds represented by that check shall be treated as residual funds and distributed in accordance with Section 4.6 of this Agreement.
206: **4.7 No Claims Filing Required.** Settlement Class Members are not required to submit a claim form or take any affirmative action to receive an Individual Settlement Payment. All Participating Class Members (i.e., Settlement Class Members who do not submit a valid and timely Opt-Out) shall automatically receive an Individual Settlement Payment based on the allocation formula set forth in Section 4.1, calculated using the Workweek Data provided by AMA. Although the submission of a claim form is not required for eligibility to receive a payment, the Claims Administrator shall provide Settlement Class Members with an opportunity to submit an updated address form (via the Settlement Website, by mail, or by telephone) to ensure that settlement checks are mailed to the correct address. The Claims Administrator shall track address updates for purposes of confirming addresses and ensuring accurate and efficient distribution of settlement funds.
207: > \(b\) A summary of the material terms of the Settlement, including the Gross Settlement Amount, the estimated Net Settlement Fund, the estimated average Individual Settlement Payment, the allocation formula used to calculate Individual Settlement Payments, and the tax treatment of Individual Settlement Payments;
208: > \(i\) A statement that Settlement Class Members who do not submit a valid and timely Opt-Out will be bound by the terms of the Settlement, including the release of claims, and will automatically receive an Individual Settlement Payment.
209: **5.3 Summary/Postcard Notice.** In addition to the Long-Form Class Notice, the Claims Administrator shall mail a Summary/Postcard Notice to each Settlement Class Member at his or her last known mailing address. The Summary/Postcard Notice shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit B, and shall include a brief summary of the Settlement, the estimated average Individual Settlement Payment, the Response Deadline, the date of the Final Approval Hearing, and directions to the Settlement Website and the Long-Form Class Notice for additional information. The Summary/Postcard Notice shall be mailed concurrently with or as part of the same mailing as the Long-Form Class Notice.
210: **5.4 Settlement Website.** The Claims Administrator shall establish and maintain a Settlement Website, accessible to the public, that provides comprehensive information about the Settlement. The Settlement Website shall include, at a minimum: (a) the Long-Form Class Notice; (b) this Settlement Agreement; (c) the Preliminary Approval Order; (d) any other Court orders related to the Settlement; (e) a list of frequently asked questions and answers regarding the Settlement; and (f) a mechanism by which Settlement Class Members may update their mailing addresses and submit inquiries to the Claims Administrator. The Settlement Website shall be operational no later than the date on which the Class Notice is first mailed and shall remain active and accessible for a period of no less than one hundred eighty (180) calendar days after the date on which Individual Settlement Payment checks are mailed.
211: **5.5 Toll-Free Number.** The Claims Administrator shall establish and maintain a toll-free telephone number dedicated to providing recorded information about the Settlement, including a summary of the Settlement terms, the Response Deadline, the date of the Final Approval Hearing, and instructions for submitting Opt-Out requests, Objections, and address updates. The toll-free number shall include the ability for callers to leave voicemail messages for the Claims Administrator, and the Claims Administrator shall respond to all such messages within two (2) business days. The toll-free number shall be operational no later than the date on which the Class Notice is first mailed and shall remain active for a period of no less than one hundred eighty (180) calendar days after the date on which Individual Settlement Payment checks are mailed.
212: **7.2 Effect of Opt-Out.** Any Settlement Class Member who submits a valid and timely Opt-Out request shall not be a Participating Class Member, shall not be bound by the terms of this Settlement Agreement (including the release of claims set forth in Section 9), shall not receive an Individual Settlement Payment from the NSF, and shall not share in the PAGA Aggrieved Employee Payment (25% share). Settlement Class Members who submit valid and timely Opt-Out requests retain all legal rights, remedies, and defenses they possessed prior to the execution of this Settlement Agreement, including the right to pursue individual claims against AMA in a separate proceeding, subject to any applicable statutes of limitations or other defenses. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Settlement Class Members who opt out of the Settlement Class remain bound by the PAGA release set forth in Section 9.5 of this Agreement to the extent permitted by law, as PAGA claims are brought on behalf of the State of California and cannot be individually opted out of.
213: **17.9 No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** Except for the Settlement Class Members (who are intended third-party beneficiaries of this Agreement with respect to their rights to receive Individual Settlement Payments and the other benefits of the Settlement as described herein), no person or entity that is not a signatory to this Agreement shall have any right to enforce, or any claim or cause of action under or arising from, any provision of this Agreement. Nothing in this Agreement is intended to confer any rights, benefits, or causes of action upon any third party, except as expressly stated herein.
214: **17.11 Taxes.** The Claims Administrator shall be responsible for all tax reporting obligations associated with the establishment and administration of the QSF and the distribution of Individual Settlement Payments to Participating Class Members, including without limitation the preparation, filing, and issuance of IRS Forms W-2 and 1099-MISC (or such other tax forms as may be required by applicable federal and state tax law). The Claims Administrator shall timely file all required tax returns for the QSF and shall pay any taxes owed by the QSF from the funds held therein. AMA shall be responsible for the timely payment of the employer\'s share of payroll taxes (including FICA, FUTA, and state unemployment taxes) on the wage portion of Individual Settlement Payments, as set forth in Section 4.4 of this Agreement. Each Participating Class Member shall be solely and individually responsible for any federal, state, or local tax liability arising from or attributable to his or her Individual Settlement Payment, including any taxes, penalties, or interest assessed by any taxing authority. Neither the Parties, Class Counsel, Defense Counsel, nor the Claims Administrator make any representations or warranties regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of any payment made under this Agreement, and each Participating Class Member is strongly encouraged to consult with a qualified tax advisor regarding the tax consequences of his or her Individual Settlement Payment.

The Parties agree that VHG will report the Settlement Amount as proceeds from an insurance recovery for business-interruption losses for applicable tax purposes. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed as tax advice, and each Party is encouraged to consult with its own qualified tax advisors regarding the tax treatment of the Settlement Amount.
230: **Section 3.1** *Stipulation of Dismissal.* Within ten (10) business days following receipt by VHG (through the trust account of Calderwood & Harkness LLP) of the full Settlement Amount from all Insurer Parties, the Parties shall jointly execute and file a Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice of all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and affirmative defenses in the Litigation, Case No. 2022-CA-031547, in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida, in and for Miami-Dade County, before the Honorable Catherine Embry, Circuit Judge. 231: **Section 4.1** *Release by VHG.* Effective upon VHG\'s receipt of the full Settlement Amount from all Insurer Parties, VHG, on behalf of itself and all VHG Parties, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges each and every Insurer Party, and each of their respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents (including, without limitation, Arbor Claims Services LLC and its employees, agents, and representatives, including specifically Denise Whitford), underwriters, reinsurers, predecessors, successors, assigns, and legal counsel (including, without limitation, Fendowell Rourke & Stanton LLP and its attorneys Gregory Stanton, Meredith Liang, and Colin Ashford; and Delvecchio & Kraus LLP and its attorneys Patricia Kraus and Raymond Cho), from any and all Claims of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, asserted or unasserted, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies (collectively, the \"Released Claims\"). 232: **Section 4.2** *Release by Insurer Parties.* Effective upon payment of the full Settlement Amount by all Insurer Parties to VHG, each Insurer Party, on behalf of itself and its respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, underwriters, reinsurers, predecessors, successors, and assigns, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges VHG and all VHG Parties, including, without limitation, VHG\'s officers (specifically Marcus Ellsworth, Diane Calder, Nathaniel Driscoll, and Sandra Pellegrini), directors, employees, agents, representatives, and legal counsel (including, without limitation, Calderwood & Harkness LLP and its attorneys Elaine Forsythe, Howard Bellamy, Tiffany Rosenthal, and Andrew Fitzpatrick), from any and all Claims of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, asserted or unasserted, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured, accrued or not yet accrued, arising out of or relating to the Hurricane Callista Losses and/or the Policies. lines.text: **4.3 Estimated Average Individual Payment.** Based on the estimated NSF of Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty-One Thousand Five Hundred Twenty-Five Dollars (\$8,251,525.00) and an estimated class size of approximately 1,850 Participating Class Members, the estimated average Individual Settlement Payment is approximately Four Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Dollars (\$4,460.00). Actual Individual Settlement Payments will vary based on each Participating Class Member\'s individual workweeks and overtime hours worked during the Class Period, as well as the total number of Opt-Outs and the final Court-approved deductions from the GSA. Some Participating Class Members may receive more or less than the estimated average depending on their individual circumstances.
**4.4 Tax Treatment of Individual Settlement Payments.** Each Individual Settlement Payment shall be allocated for tax purposes as follows:

> \(a\) **Wage Portion (50%).** Fifty percent (50%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as wages for services rendered, and shall be subject to applicable federal and state income tax withholding and employee-side payroll taxes, including the employee\'s share of FICA (Social Security and Medicare taxes) and applicable state payroll taxes. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form W-2.

> \(b\) **Interest and Penalties Portion (33.33%).** Thirty-three and one-third percent (33.33%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as interest and penalties, which are not subject to withholding but are generally taxable as ordinary income to the recipient. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC (or such other form as may be required by applicable tax law at the time of distribution).

> \(c\) **Non-Wage Damages Portion (16.67%).** Sixteen and sixty-seven hundredths percent (16.67%) of each Individual Settlement Payment shall be characterized and reported as non-wage damages, which are not subject to withholding. This portion shall be reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC (or such other form as may be required by applicable tax law at the time of distribution).

AMA shall be responsible for paying the employer\'s share of payroll taxes (including the employer\'s share of FICA and applicable federal and state unemployment taxes) on the wage portion of Individual Settlement Payments. The employer\'s share of payroll taxes shall be paid by AMA separately from the GSA and shall not be deducted from the NSF or from any Participating Class Member\'s Individual Settlement Payment. Neither Class Counsel, Defense Counsel, nor the Claims Administrator makes any representation or warranty regarding the tax treatment of any Individual Settlement Payment, and each Participating Class Member is encouraged to consult with a qualified tax advisor regarding the tax consequences of his or her Individual Settlement Payment.

**4.5 Distribution Timeline.** The Claims Administrator shall mail Individual Settlement Payment checks to Participating Class Members within thirty (30) calendar days of the date on which the GSA is fully funded in the QSF. Checks shall be valid for one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from the date of issuance and shall bear a legend indicating the void-after date. Prior to mailing settlement checks, the Claims Administrator shall perform a National Change of Address (\"NCOA\") search for all Settlement Class Members to update mailing addresses. The Claims Administrator shall make reasonable efforts to locate Participating Class Members whose settlement checks are returned as undeliverable by the United States Postal Service, including performing skip-tracing using commercially available databases. If, after such efforts, a Participating Class Member\'s updated address is identified, the Claims Administrator shall re-mail the check to the updated address. If, despite such efforts, a Participating Class Member cannot be located or a check remains undeliverable, the funds represented by that check shall be treated as residual funds and distributed in accordance with Section 4.6 of this Agreement.

**4.7 No Claims Filing Required.** Settlement Class Members are not required to submit a claim form or take any affirmative action to receive an Individual Settlement Payment. All Participating Class Members (i.e., Settlement Class Members who do not submit a valid and timely Opt-Out) shall automatically receive an Individual Settlement Payment based on the allocation formula set forth in Section 4.1, calculated using the Workweek Data provided by AMA. Although the submission of a claim form is not required for eligibility to receive a payment, the Claims Administrator shall provide Settlement Class Members with an opportunity to submit an updated address form (via the Settlement Website, by mail, or by telephone) to ensure that settlement checks are mailed to the correct address. The Claims Administrator shall track address updates for purposes of confirming addresses and ensuring accurate and efficient distribution of settlement funds.

> \(b\) A summary of the material terms of the Settlement, including the Gross Settlement Amount, the estimated Net Settlement Fund, the estimated average Individual Settlement Payment, the allocation formula used to calculate Individual Settlement Payments, and the tax treatment of Individual Settlement Payments;

> \(i\) A statement that Settlement Class Members who do not submit a valid and timely Opt-Out will be bound by the terms of the Settlement, including the release of claims, and will automatically receive an Individual Settlement Payment.

**5.3 Summary/Postcard Notice.** In addition to the Long-Form Class Notice, the Claims Administrator shall mail a Summary/Postcard Notice to each Settlement Class Member at his or her last known mailing address. The Summary/Postcard Notice shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit B, and shall include a brief summary of the Settlement, the estimated average Individual Settlement Payment, the Response Deadline, the date of the Final Approval Hearing, and directions to the Settlement Website and the Long-Form Class Notice for additional information. The Summary/Postcard Notice shall be mailed concurrently with or as part of the same mailing as the Long-Form Class Notice.

**5.4 Settlement Website.** The Claims Administrator shall establish and maintain a Settlement Website, accessible to the public, that provides comprehensive information about the Settlement. The Settlement Website shall include, at a minimum: (a) the Long-Form Class Notice; (b) this Settlement Agreement; (c) the Preliminary Approval Order; (d) any other Court orders related to the Settlement; (e) a list of frequently asked questions and answers regarding the Settlement; and (f) a mechanism by which Settlement Class Members may update their mailing addresses and submit inquiries to the Claims Administrator. The Settlement Website shall be operational no later than the date on which the Class Notice is first mailed and shall remain active and accessible for a period of no less than one hundred eighty (180) calendar days after the date on which Individual Settlement Payment checks are mailed.

**5.5 Toll-Free Number.** The Claims Administrator shall establish and maintain a toll-free telephone number dedicated to providing recorded information about the Settlement, including a summary of the Settlement terms, the Response Deadline, the date of the Final Approval Hearing, and instructions for submitting Opt-Out requests, Objections, and address updates. The toll-free number shall include the ability for callers to leave voicemail messages for the Claims Administrator, and the Claims Administrator shall respond to all such messages within two (2) business days. The toll-free number shall be operational no later than the date on which the Class Notice is first mailed and shall remain active for a period of no less than one hundred eighty (180) calendar days after the date on which Individual Settlement Payment checks are mailed.

**7.2 Effect of Opt-Out.** Any Settlement Class Member who submits a valid and timely Opt-Out request shall not be a Participating Class Member, shall not be bound by the terms of this Settlement Agreement (including the release of claims set forth in Section 9), shall not receive an Individual Settlement Payment from the NSF, and shall not share in the PAGA Aggrieved Employee Payment (25% share). Settlement Class Members who submit valid and timely Opt-Out requests retain all legal rights, remedies, and defenses they possessed prior to the execution of this Settlement Agreement, including the right to pursue individual claims against AMA in a separate proceeding, subject to any applicable statutes of limitations or other defenses. 30489: **A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per property... 30491: **B. The Litigation.** On November 8, 2021, a former Coastal Palms regional controller, Janet Kerrigan, reported to Verimark\'s compliance hotline allegations of systematic revenue underreporting by the Coastal Palms Parties. In response, Verimark retained Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of the Coastal Palms properties. Thornbury\'s preliminary findings, delivered to Verimark on January 18, 2022, indicated that the audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period spanning fiscal years 2019 through 2021. Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms on February 4, 2022, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the identified breaches within thirty (30) days in accordance with FLA § 14.1. Coastal Palms, through its counsel Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, responded by letter dated February 28, 2022, denying any material breach and contesting the methodology and conclusions of the Thornbury audit. No cure was tendered by Coastal Palms within the thirty (30)-day period, which expired on March 6, 2022. On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, bearing Case Number 1021-00006 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for: (i) breach of contract --- royalties; (ii) breach of contract --- marketing fund; (iii) breach of contract --- technology fees; (iv) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (v) fraudulent concealment; (vi) negligent misrepresentation; (vii) unjust enrichment; (viii) declaratory judgment; (ix) accounting; and (x) civil conspiracy. In the Complaint, Verimark claimed damages in the approximate aggregate amount of \$150,000,000, consisting of: (a) \$16,095,000 in direct underpayments of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees; (b) \$28,400,000 in contractual late-payment interest calculated in accordance with FLA § 4.6; a... Calloway, Circuit Judge) entered an Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Count I (Breach of Contract --- Royalties) and Count II (Breach of Contract --- Marketing Fund), finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. from its calculation and reporting of GRR constituted a material breach of FLA §§ 4.1 and 4.2. The Court denied Coastal Palms\' Cross-Motion for Summary Judgment on all counts and deferred the determination of damages to trial.

A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. The amount of interest due with each installment shall be calculated by multiplying the outstanding principal balance as of the first day of the applicable interest period by the annual interest rate of 6.5%, and then multiplying the result by a fraction, the numerator of which is the actual number of days elapsed during such interest period and the denominator of which is 365. No Party shall take any position on any tax return or in any proceeding before any taxing authority that is inconsistent with the treatment described in this Section 2.8, unless required to do so by a final determination (as defined in Section 1313(a) of the Internal Revenue Code) of a court of competent jurisdiction or an applicable taxing authority.

**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**
**(Execution Version)**
*Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.* Case No. 1021-00006 Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida
