**SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE**
This **SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE** (this \"Agreement\") is entered into and made effective as of April 22, 2024 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:

**VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, and whose common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VHMK\" (hereinafter referred to as \"Verimark\" or \"VHG\");
and

**COASTAL PALMS FRANCHISE HOLDINGS LLC**, a Florida limited liability company, with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108 (hereinafter referred to as \"Coastal Palms\" or \"CPFH\");

**RANDALL \"RANDY\" BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who serves as the Managing Member and holds a sixty percent (60%) equity interest in Coastal Palms, and who also serves as the President of Suncoast Room Management Inc. (hereinafter referred to as \"R. Brecker\");
**THERESA BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a fifteen percent (15%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"T. Brecker\");

**NOLAN PRESCOTT**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a twenty-five percent (25%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"Prescott\");
**GULF BREEZE HOSPITALITY LLC**, a Florida limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Gulf Breeze\");
**SAVANNAH LODGING PARTNERS LLC**, a Georgia limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Savannah Lodging\");
**SUNCOAST ROOM MANAGEMENT INC.**, a Florida corporation (hereinafter referred to as \"Suncoast\");

Coastal Palms, R. Brecker, T. Brecker, Prescott, Gulf Breeze, Savannah Lodging, and Suncoast are collectively referred to herein as the \"Coastal Palms Parties.\" Verimark and the Coastal Palms Parties are collectively referred to herein as the \"Parties\" and each individually as a \"Party.\"
**[RECITALS]{.underline}**
**WHEREAS:**

**A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per property... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

**B. The Litigation.** On November 8, 2021, a former Coastal Palms regional controller, Janet Kerrigan, reported to Verimark\'s compliance hotline allegations of systematic revenue underreporting by the Coastal Palms Parties. In response, Verimark retained Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of the Coastal Palms properties. Thornbury\'s preliminary findings, delivered to Verimark on January 18, 2022, indicated that the audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period spanning fiscal years 2019 through 2021. Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms on February 4, 2022, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the identified breaches within thirty (30) days in accordance with FLA § 14.1. Coastal Palms, through its counsel Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, responded by letter dated February 28, 2022, denying any material breach and contesting the methodology and conclusions of the Thornbury audit. No cure was tendered by Coastal Palms within the thirty (30)-day period, which expired on March 6, 2022. On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, bearing Case Number 1021-00006 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for: (i) breach of contract --- royalties; (ii) breach of contract --- marketing fund; (iii) breach of contract --- technology fees; (iv) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (v) fraudulent concealment; (vi) negligent misrepresentation; (vii) unjust enrichment; (viii) declaratory judgment; (ix) accounting; and (x) civil conspiracy. In the Complaint, Verimark claimed damages in the approximate aggregate amount of \$150,000,000, consisting of: (a) \$16,095,000 in direct underpayments of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees; (b) \$28,400,000 in contractual late-payment interest calculated in accordance with FLA § 4.6; a... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

**C. Summary Judgment Ruling.** On February 9, 2024, the Court (the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge) entered an Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Count I (Breach of Contract --- Royalties) and Count II (Breach of Contract --- Marketing Fund), finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. from its calculation and reporting of GRR constituted a material breach of FLA §§ 4.1 and 4.2. The Court denied Coastal Palms\' Cross-Motion for Summary Judgment on all counts and deferred the determination of damages to trial.

**D. Mediation and Settlement.** On February 23, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Retired), of Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC. A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. A tentative settlement was reached on the second day of mediation, March 15, 2024, and the Parties executed a written term sheet memorializing the principal terms of the settlement on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims and counterclaims in the Litigation, and all related disputes among the Parties, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

**E. Desire to Settle.** The Parties acknowledge the uncertainty, risk, and expense inherent in continued litigation and trial, and each Party has made an independent assessment of the merits and risks of its respective claims and defenses. The Parties desire to avoid the further burden and expense of trial and to resolve their disputes amicably and in full. Entry into this Agreement is not, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim or defense by any Party. Each Party has been represented by competent legal counsel of its choosing in the negotiation and execution of this Agreement, and each Party has had a full and fair opportunity to review, analyze, and negotiate the terms set forth herein.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, releases, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**1.1** \"**Agreement**\" means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, together with all Exhibits and Schedules attached hereto, which are incorporated herein by reference and made a part hereof.

**1.2** \"**Closing**\" means the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement on the Closing Date, including the execution and delivery of this Agreement by all Parties, the payment of the Initial Payment, and the execution and delivery of all ancillary documents required to be delivered at or prior to the Closing.
**1.3** \"**Closing Date**\" means April 22, 2024.

**1.4** \"**Collateral Properties**\" means the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 hereto, which serve as collateral for the security interest granted to Verimark pursuant to Article III.

**1.5** \"**Complaint**\" means the ten-count Complaint filed by Verimark on March 7, 2022, in Case No. 1021-00006, in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, together with all amendments thereto.
**1.6** \"**Counterclaim**\" means the \$12,000,000 counterclaim filed by Coastal Palms on April 18, 2022, in the Litigation, asserting claims for alleged brand-standard violations and over-billing.
**1.7** \"**Court**\" means the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida.
**1.8** \"**De-Identification Deadline**\" means August 20, 2024, which is one hundred twenty (120) days from the Closing Date.

**1.9** \"**Enhanced Audit Protocol**\" means the enhanced audit and reporting requirements applicable to the Retained Properties, as set forth in Article VIII of this Agreement and as more fully described in Exhibit D attached hereto.
**1.10** \"**Event of Default**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.7 of this Agreement.

**1.11** \"**Existing FLAs**\" means the twenty-two (22) Franchise License Agreements between Verimark and Coastal Palms and/or its affiliates (including Gulf Breeze and Savannah Lodging), the first of which was executed on June 15, 2007, and the most recent of which was executed on September 3, 2019, governing the operation of the Properties under the Verimark Brands.

**1.12** \"**GRR**\" or \"**Gross Room Revenue**\" has the meaning ascribed to such term in Section 4.1 of each FLA, which generally includes all revenue derived from or attributable to the rental of guest rooms at the applicable Property, regardless of the method of collection, booking channel, or collecting entity.
**1.13** \"**Initial Payment**\" means the cash payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) payable by Coastal Palms to Verimark at Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 of this Agreement.

**1.14** \"**Ironclad**\" means Ironclad National Bank, a national banking association, which holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Properties, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000) as of the date hereof.

**1.15** \"**Litigation**\" means the action styled *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.*, Case No. 1021-00006, pending in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and third-party claims asserted therein.

**1.16** \"**New FLAs**\" means the new ten (10)-year Franchise License Agreements to be executed by Verimark and the applicable Coastal Palms Party for each of the Retained Properties, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit C.
**1.17** \"**Payment Schedule**\" means the schedule of payments set forth in Article II and as more fully described in Exhibit A attached hereto.

**1.18** \"**Personal Guaranties**\" means the individual guaranty agreements to be executed by R. Brecker and Prescott, each substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott jointly and severally guarantee all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement.
**1.19** \"**Properties**\" means the twenty-two (22) hotel properties operated by the Coastal Palms Parties under the Existing FLAs.

**1.20** \"**Retained Properties**\" means the eight (8) Properties identified in Section 7.1 of this Agreement and in Exhibit C that will continue to be franchised under the New FLAs, consisting of four (4) properties in Naples, Florida; two (2) properties on Marco Island, Florida; and two (2) properties in Tampa, Florida.

**1.21** \"**Security Agreement**\" means the security agreement to be executed by Coastal Palms in favor of Verimark, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F, granting Verimark a first-priority security interest in the Collateral Properties to secure the Structured Payments and other obligations under this Agreement.

**1.22** \"**Settlement Amount**\" means the aggregate sum of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable by the Coastal Palms Parties to Verimark in accordance with Article II of this Agreement.

**1.23** \"**Structured Payments**\" means the eight (8) semi-annual payments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in accordance with Section 2.3 of this Agreement, the first such payment being due on October 22, 2024, and the last such payment being due on April 22, 2028, as more fully described in the Payment Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**1.24** \"**Surrendered Properties**\" means the fourteen (14) Properties identified in Section 7.1 and Exhibit B of this Agreement that are subject to franchise surrender, de-identification, and termination of the applicable Existing FLAs.

**1.25** \"**Verimark Brands**\" means \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand,\" together with all associated trademarks, service marks, logos, trade dress, proprietary systems (including reservation systems, property management systems, and revenue management systems), and all other intellectual property owned, licensed, or controlled by Verimark in connection with the branding and operation of its franchised hotel properties.
**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Total Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, and disputes among the Parties, whether asserted or unasserted, known or unknown, arising from or relating to the Existing FLAs, the Litigation, or the subject matter thereof, the Coastal Palms Parties shall pay to Verimark a total Settlement Amount of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable as follows:
> \(a\) The Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), payable at the Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 below; and

> \(b\) The Structured Payments totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in eight (8) semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, in accordance with Section 2.3 below.
The Payment Schedule setting forth the dates, amounts, and interest calculations for all payments under this Article II is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.

**Section 2.2 --- Initial Payment.** On the Closing Date, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) by wire transfer of immediately available funds from the escrow account established at Ironclad National Bank for the purposes of this settlement to Verimark\'s designated account. Verimark shall provide Coastal Palms with complete wire-transfer instructions for the designated receiving account no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment, Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, at 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, shall promptly issue a written confirmation of receipt to counsel for the Coastal Palms Parties. The obligation to make the Initial Payment is unconditional and shall not be subject to any right of setoff, counterclaim, defense, or deduction.

**Section 2.3 --- Structured Payments.** Following the payment of the Initial Payment, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the remaining Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000) in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, on the following schedule:
> \(a\) The first installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2024.
> \(b\) The second installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2025.
> \(c\) The third installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2025.
> \(d\) The fourth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2026.
> \(e\) The fifth installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2026.
> \(f\) The sixth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2027.
> \(g\) The seventh installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2027.
> \(h\) The eighth and final installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2028.

All Structured Payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Verimark in accordance with the wire-transfer instructions provided pursuant to Section 2.2, or to such other account as Verimark may designate in writing from time to time upon not less than ten (10) business days\' prior notice to Coastal Palms.

**Section 2.4 --- Interest on Structured Payments.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall begin to accrue on the Closing Date and shall be calculated on the then-outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments. Interest payments shall be due and payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment payment. The amount of interest due with each installment shall be calculated by multiplying the outstanding principal balance as of the first day of the applicable interest period by the annual interest rate of 6.5%, and then multiplying the result by a fraction, the numerator of which is the actual number of days elapsed during such interest period and the denominator of which is 365. A detailed schedule setting forth the estimated interest amounts due with each installment is set forth in Exhibit A.

**Section 2.5 --- Late Payments.** Any Structured Payment (including any concurrent interest payment) not received by Verimark within ten (10) business days of its scheduled due date shall bear additional default interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month on the overdue amount, calculated from the original due date until the date on which such overdue amount is received by Verimark in full. This default interest shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, the interest otherwise payable under Section 2.4. If Coastal Palms fails to cure a late payment within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the overdue payment and the amount due, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.7 of this Agreement. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed to extend the due date for any Structured Payment or to waive Verimark\'s right to declare an Event of Default following the expiration of the applicable cure period.

**Section 2.6 --- Prepayment.** Coastal Palms may, at its option, prepay all or any portion of the Structured Payments at any time without premium, penalty, or additional charge of any kind. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to any accrued and unpaid interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, and second to the scheduled installments in inverse order of maturity (i.e., applied first to the most distant scheduled installment, then to the next most distant, and so on), thereby reducing the total interest obligation over the remaining term. Coastal Palms shall provide Verimark with not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of any prepayment, specifying the amount and intended date of such prepayment. Verimark shall recalculate the interest amounts due on any remaining installments following any partial prepayment and shall provide an updated Payment Schedule to Coastal Palms within ten (10) business days of receipt of any such prepayment.
**Section 2.7 --- Events of Default and Acceleration.** An \"Event of Default\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the happening of any of the following:

> \(a\) **Payment Default.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to make any payment of the Structured Payments, accrued interest, or any other monetary obligation under this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date on which Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such payment default;

> \(b\) **Covenant Default.** Breach by any Coastal Palms Party of any material covenant, agreement, or obligation under this Agreement (other than a payment obligation, which is governed by clause (a) above) that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such breach in reasonable detail;

> \(c\) **Bankruptcy or Insolvency.** The commencement of any voluntary or involuntary proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code, Title 11, United States Code, or under any state insolvency, receivership, dissolution, or similar statute, by or against any Coastal Palms Party, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee, custodian, or similar official for the business, assets, or property of any Coastal Palms Party, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors by any Coastal Palms Party;

> \(d\) **Breach of Representations and Warranties.** Any representation or warranty made by any Coastal Palms Party in this Agreement or in any ancillary document delivered in connection herewith that is materially inaccurate, false, or misleading as of the date on which it was made, and such inaccuracy, falsity, or misleading character is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the same;

> \(e\) **De-Identification Failure.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to comply with the de-identification requirements set forth in Article VII of this Agreement by the De-Identification Deadline.

Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Verimark may, at its sole election and upon written notice to Coastal Palms, declare the entire outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon and all other amounts owing under this Agreement, immediately due and payable in full, without further notice, demand, presentment, or protest, all of which are hereby waived by the Coastal Palms Parties. Acceleration of the Structured Payments pursuant to this Section 2.7 shall not constitute a waiver of, or limit, any other rights or remedies available to Verimark at law or in equity, including, without limitation, the right to enforce the Security Agreement, to seek collection under the Personal Guaranties, to pursue foreclosure on the Collateral Properties, and to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from the Court.

**Section 2.8 --- Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all federal, state, and local taxes, and for the filing of all tax returns and reports, arising from or attributable to the payments received or made by such Party under this Agreement. The Parties agree that, for federal and state income-tax purposes, the Settlement Amount shall be treated by all Parties as compensatory damages and that no portion of the Settlement Amount shall be characterized as punitive damages, penalties, or interest for tax purposes, except to the extent required by applicable law. The Coastal Palms Parties shall be solely responsible for any and all withholding obligations, including but not limited to any obligation to withhold and remit taxes on behalf of Verimark, if any such obligation exists under applicable law. No Party shall take any position on any tax return or in any proceeding before any taxing authority that is inconsistent with the treatment described in this Section 2.8, unless required to do so by a final determination (as defined in Section 1313(a) of the Internal Revenue Code) of a court of competent jurisdiction or an applicable taxing authority.
**[ARTICLE III --- SECURITY FOR STRUCTURED PAYMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Security Interest.** To secure the prompt and full payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, the payment of all Structured Payments, accrued interest thereon, default interest, and any indemnification obligations arising under Article X, Coastal Palms hereby grants to Verimark a first-priority security interest in the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 attached hereto (the \"Collateral Properties\"), together with all improvements, fixtures, furnishings, equipment, accounts, general intangibles, and proceeds related thereto (collectively, the \"Collateral\"). The aggregate appraised value of the Collateral Properties, as determined by independent appraisals conducted by licensed commercial real-estate appraisers within the ninety (90)-day period preceding the Closing Date, is not less than Seventy-One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$71,200,000). The security interest granted hereunder shall be evidenced by the Security Agreement, which shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F and shall be executed and delivered concurrently with the execution of this Agreement.

**Section 3.2 --- UCC Filings.** To perfect the security interest granted under Section 3.1, Coastal Palms hereby authorizes Verimark, and Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, to prepare, execute, and file on behalf of Coastal Palms UCC-1 Financing Statements with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry and with any other filing office in any jurisdiction where filing may be necessary or advisable to perfect or maintain Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. The UCC-1 Financing Statement shall identify the following:
> **Debtor:** Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108
> **Secured Party:** Verimark Hospitality Group Inc., 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301

Coastal Palms shall execute and deliver all additional documents, instruments, and agreements, including without limitation continuation statements, amendments, and such other filings and recordings, as may be reasonably necessary or requested by Verimark from time to time to perfect, preserve, and maintain the first-priority status of Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. Coastal Palms shall bear all costs and expenses associated with such filings.

**Section 3.3 --- Personal Guaranties.** Concurrently with the execution of this Agreement, R. Brecker and Prescott shall each execute and deliver to Verimark a Personal Guaranty, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott shall jointly and severally, absolutely, unconditionally, and irrevocably guarantee the full and prompt payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest, indemnification obligations, and any and all other amounts that may become due and owing under this Agreement. The Personal Guaranties shall remain in full force and effect until all Structured Payments, accrued interest, and all other obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement have been paid or performed in full to the complete satisfaction of Verimark.

**Section 3.4 --- Relationship with Ironclad National Bank.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that Ironclad National Bank (\"Ironclad\") holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Properties, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000) as of the date hereof. The Parties further acknowledge that the eight (8) Collateral Properties identified in Schedule 3.1, which secure Verimark\'s security interest under this Agreement, are unencumbered by any mortgage, lien, or security interest held by Ironclad. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed or interpreted so as to impair, subordinate, modify, or otherwise affect in any manner whatsoever the existing liens, security interests, or other rights of Ironclad under its mortgage-loan agreements with the Coastal Palms Parties. Coastal Palms represents and warrants that it has provided written notice to Ironclad of the existence and terms of this Agreement and the grant of the security interest to Verimark, and that Ironclad has not objected to the transactions contemplated hereby. Ironclad is an intended third-party beneficiary of this Section 3.4 and of Section 9.5 of this Agreement.

**Section 3.5 --- Release of Security Interest.** Upon the payment in full of all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest (if any), and all other obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, Verimark shall, within thirty (30) days of such payment in full: (a) file UCC-3 Termination Statements with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry and all other applicable filing offices; and (b) execute and deliver to Coastal Palms such releases, satisfactions, and other documents and instruments as may be reasonably necessary to evidence the termination and release of Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. Verimark shall bear its own costs associated with the preparation and filing of such termination statements and releases.

Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC et al.\*, Case No. 1021-00006, Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida; Ironclad National Bank\'s First-Lien Mortgage Loans on Certain Hotel Properties Owned by Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC and Affiliated Entities**
28711: 
28712: Dear Mr. Schultz:
28713: 
28714: **[I. Introduction and Purpose of This Letter]{.underline}**
28715: 
28716: This firm represents Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. (\"Verimark\" or \"VHG\"), a Delaware corporation publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under ticker symbol VHMK, with its principal executive offices located at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301. We write on behalf of Verimark in connection with the above-referenced litigation and Ironclad National Bank\'s (\"Ironclad\" or the \"Bank\") commercial real estate lending relationship with Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC (\"Coastal Palms\") and its affiliated entities.
28717: 
28718: The purpose of this letter is threefold. First, we write to formally notify Ironclad of the settlement of the above-captioned litigation, which was executed on April 22, 2024, and to apprise the Bank of the material terms thereof. Second, we write to inform Ironclad of the manner in which the settlement terms affect and intersect with Ironclad\'s lending relationship with Coastal Palms and its affiliates, including the Bank\'s first-lien mortgage positions on certain hotel properties within the Coastal Palms portfolio. Third, and of particular importance, we write to notify Ironclad of Verimark\'s perfection of a first-priority security interest in certain hotel properties that are not encumbered by Ironclad\'s existing mortgage loans, and to request the Bank\'s written acknowledgment of and consent to such security interest. We respectfully request Ironclad\'s prompt attention to the matters set forth herein.
28719: 
28720: **[II. Background --- The Litigation]{.underline}**
28721: 
28722: On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint against Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, a Florida limited liability company with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108, and certain affiliated parties in the Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, in and for Broward County, Florida, assigned Case No. 1021-00006. The named defendants in the action included Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, Randall Brecker (individually and in his capacity as Managing Member of Coastal Palms), and Suncoast Room Management Inc. (\"Suncoast\"), a Florida corporation controlled by Mr. Brecker that had been established and utilized to collect and divert direct-booking revenues from the franchised hotel properties.
28723: 
28724: The litigation arose from Coastal Palms\' systematic underreporting of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") over a nine-year period spanning from 2013 through 2021 across its portfolio of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties, consisting of eighteen (18) Verimark Suites-branded locations and four (4) Verimark Select-branded locations operating in the states of Florida and Georgia. The affected portfolio comprised approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. Through the use of Suncoast as an intermediary revenue-collection entity, Coastal Palms diverted direct-booking revenues outside the GRR calculations required under the applicable Franchise License Agreements, thereby materially understating the royalties, marketing-fund contributions, technology fees, and other amounts owed to Verimark.
28725: 
28726: Verimark\'s Complaint asserted claims for breach of contract, breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, fraud, fraudulent concealment, unjust enrichment, violations of the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, and related causes of action, seeking approximately \$150 million in damages, including underpaid royalties, marketing-fund contributions, technology fees, contractual late-payment interest at the rates specified in the Franchise License Agreements, and liquidated damages as provided therein.
28727: 
28728: After extensive discovery---including the production of more than 600,000 documents, the depositions of twenty-three fact witnesses and four expert witnesses, and the retention of forensic accounting experts---Verimark moved for partial summary judgment on Counts I (breach of contract) and II (breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing). On February 9, 2024, the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge, granted Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on those counts, finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected through Suncoast Room Management Inc. from the calculation of GRR constituted a material breach of the Franchise License Agreements. Judge Calloway\'s order further concluded that the plain language of the GRR definition in the Franchise License Agreements encompassed all room revenues generated at the franchised hotel properties, irrespective of the booking channel or the entity through which payment was collected.
28729: 
28730: The Court\'s ruling on partial summary judgment left for trial only the issues of the precise amount of damages and Verimark\'s remaining claims, including the fraud-based counts. Following entry of the partial summary judgment order, the parties engaged in court-ordered mediation, which ultimately led to the comprehensive settlement described below.
28731: 
28732: **[III. The Settlement]{.underline}**
28733: 
28734: On April 22, 2024, Verimark and Coastal Palms, together with the following additional parties---Randall Brecker (individually), Theresa Brecker (individually), Nolan Prescott (individually), Gulf Breeze Hospitality LLC, Savannah Lodging Partners LLC, and Suncoast Room Management Inc.---executed a Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (the \"Settlement Agreement\") resolving all claims and counterclaims in the above-captioned litigation.
28735: 
28736: **A. Settlement Consideration**
28737: 
28738: The total settlement amount is Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000.00), structured as follows:
28739: 
28740: > 1\. **Cash Payment at Closing.** A cash payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000.00), which was funded via wire transfer from an Ironclad National Bank escrow account (Account No. ending in 4781) on April 22, 2024, the date of execution of the Settlement Agreement. Verimark acknowledges receipt of this payment in full.
28741: >
28742: > 2\. **Structured Payments.** The remaining balance of Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000.00), payable in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500.00) each, with the first installment due and payable on October 22, 2024, and successive installments due on the twenty-second day of each subsequent April and October, with the final installment due on April 22, 2028.
28743: >
28744: > 3\. **Interest on Deferred Payments.** The outstanding balance of the structured payments shall bear simple interest at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, calculated on the unpaid principal balance from the date of execution of the Settlement Agreement. Interest shall be payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment.
28745: 
28746: **B. Additional Settlement Terms Relevant to Ironclad**
28747: 
28748: The Settlement Agreement contains several additional provisions that are directly relevant to Ironclad\'s lending relationship with Coastal Palms and its affiliated entities:
28749: 
28750: > 1\. **Franchise Surrender --- 14 Properties.** Coastal Palms is required to surrender its franchise rights to fourteen (14) of the twenty-two (22) hotel properties within one hundred twenty (120) days of the date of the Settlement Agreement. The de-identification deadline---by which all Verimark branding, signage, logos, proprietary systems, and reservation-system integrations must be removed from the surrendered properties---is August 20, 2024. The fourteen surrendered properties are located in the following markets: Sarasota, Florida (3 properties); Fort Myers, Florida (4 properties); Jacksonville, Florida (2 properties); Savannah, Georgia (3 properties); and Brunswick, Georgia (2 properties). Upon de-identification, these properties will no longer be authorized to operate under the Verimark Suites or Verimark Select brands, nor will they have access to the Verimark reservation system, loyalty program, or proprietary technology platforms.
28751: >
28752: > 2\. **Retained Properties --- 8 Properties.** Eight (8) hotel properties will be retained under new ten-year Franchise License Agreements executed contemporaneously with the Settlement Agreement. The retained properties are located in Naples, Florida (4 properties); Marco Island, Florida (2 properties); and Tampa, Florida (2 properties). The new Franchise License Agreements incorporate enhanced quarterly audit protocols, including mandatory engagement of an independent third-party auditor approved by Verimark, as well as real-time point-of-sale (\"POS\") integration requirements that provide Verimark with direct, contemporaneous access to transactional revenue data at each retained property.
28753: >
28754: > 3\. **Counterclaim Dismissal.** Coastal Palms\' Twelve Million Dollar (\$12,000,000.00) counterclaim, which alleged wrongful termination threats, tortious interference with business relationships, and unfair franchise practices, has been dismissed with prejudice pursuant to the terms of the Settlement Agreement.
28755: >
28756: > 4\. **Joint Stipulation of Dismissal.** A Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice was filed with the Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida, on April 26, 2024, and the Court is expected to enter an order of dismissal in due course.

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Attorneys at Law* 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800 Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301 Telephone: (954) 761-8200 Facsimile: (954) 761-8201 www.calderwoodharkness.com
April 24, 2024
VIA FEDEX AND ELECTRONIC MAIL
Devon Schultz Senior Vice President, Commercial Real Estate Lending Ironclad National Bank 225 Peachtree Street NE, Suite 2600 Atlanta, GA 30303

> **Re: Notice of Settlement and Lien --- \*Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC et al.\*, Case No. 1021-00006, Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida; Ironclad National Bank\'s First-Lien Mortgage Loans on Certain Hotel Properties Owned by Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC and Affiliated Entities**
Dear Mr. Schultz:
**[I. Introduction and Purpose of This Letter]{.underline}**

This firm represents Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. (\"Verimark\" or \"VHG\"), a Delaware corporation publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under ticker symbol VHMK, with its principal executive offices located at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301. We write on behalf of Verimark in connection with the above-referenced litigation and Ironclad National Bank\'s (\"Ironclad\" or the \"Bank\") commercial real estate lending relationship with Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC (\"Coastal Palms\") and its affiliated entities.

The purpose of this letter is threefold. First, we write to formally notify Ironclad of the settlement of the above-captioned litigation, which was executed on April 22, 2024, and to apprise the Bank of the material terms thereof. Second, we write to inform Ironclad of the manner in which the settlement terms affect and intersect with Ironclad\'s lending relationship with Coastal Palms and its affiliates, including the Bank\'s first-lien mortgage positions on certain hotel properties within the Coastal Palms portfolio. Third, and of particular importance, we write to notify Ironclad of Verimark\'s perfection of a first-priority security interest in certain hotel properties that are not encumbered by Ironclad\'s existing mortgage loans, and to request the Bank\'s written acknowledgment of and consent to such security interest. We respectfully request Ironclad\'s prompt attention to the matters set forth herein.
**[II. Background --- The Litigation]{.underline}**

On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint against Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, a Florida limited liability company with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108, and certain affiliated parties in the Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, in and for Broward County, Florida, assigned Case No. 1021-00006. The named defendants in the action included Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, Randall Brecker (individually and in his capacity as Managing Member of Coastal Palms), and Suncoast Room Management Inc. (\"Suncoast\"), a Florida corporation controlled by Mr. Brecker that had been established and utilized to collect and divert direct-booking revenues from the franchised hotel properties.

The litigation arose from Coastal Palms\' systematic underreporting of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") over a nine-year period spanning from 2013 through 2021 across its portfolio of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties, consisting of eighteen (18) Verimark Suites-branded locations and four (4) Verimark Select-branded locations operating in the states of Florida and Georgia. The affected portfolio comprised approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. Through the use of Suncoast as an intermediary revenue-collection entity, Coastal Palms diverted direct-booking revenues outside the GRR calculations required under the applicable Franchise License Agreements, thereby materially understating the royalties, marketing-fund contributions, technology fees, and other amounts owed to Verimark.

Verimark\'s Complaint asserted claims for breach of contract, breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, fraud, fraudulent concealment, unjust enrichment, violations of the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, and related causes of action, seeking approximately \$150 million in damages, including underpaid royalties, marketing-fund contributions, technology fees, contractual late-payment interest at the rates specified in the Franchise License Agreements, and liquidated damages as provided therein.

After extensive discovery---including the production of more than 600,000 documents, the depositions of twenty-three fact witnesses and four expert witnesses, and the retention of forensic accounting experts---Verimark moved for partial summary judgment on Counts I (breach of contract) and II (breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing). On February 9, 2024, the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge, granted Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on those counts, finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected through Suncoast Room Management Inc. from the calculation of GRR constituted a material breach of the Franchise License Agreements. Judge Calloway\'s order further concluded that the plain language of the GRR definition in the Franchise License Agreements encompassed all room revenues generated at the franchised hotel properties, irrespective of the booking channel or the entity through which payment was collected.

The Court\'s ruling on partial summary judgment left for trial only the issues of the precise amount of damages and Verimark\'s remaining claims, including the fraud-based counts. Following entry of the partial summary judgment order, the parties engaged in court-ordered mediation, which ultimately led to the comprehensive settlement described below.
**[III. The Settlement]{.underline}**

On April 22, 2024, Verimark and Coastal Palms, together with the following additional parties---Randall Brecker (individually), Theresa Brecker (individually), Nolan Prescott (individually), Gulf Breeze Hospitality LLC, Savannah Lodging Partners LLC, and Suncoast Room Management Inc.---executed a Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (the \"Settlement Agreement\") resolving all claims and counterclaims in the above-captioned litigation.
**A. Settlement Consideration**
The total settlement amount is Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000.00), structured as follows:

> 1\. **Cash Payment at Closing.** A cash payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000.00), which was funded via wire transfer from an Ironclad National Bank escrow account (Account No. ending in 4781) on April 22, 2024, the date of execution of the Settlement Agreement. Verimark acknowledges receipt of this payment in full.

> 2\. **Structured Payments.** The remaining balance of Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000.00), payable in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500.00) each, with the first installment due and payable on October 22, 2024, and successive installments due on the twenty-second day of each subsequent April and October, with the final installment due on April 22, 2028.

> 3\. **Interest on Deferred Payments.** The outstanding balance of the structured payments shall bear simple interest at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, calculated on the unpaid principal balance from the date of execution of the Settlement Agreement. Interest shall be payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment.
**B. Additional Settlement Terms Relevant to Ironclad**
The Settlement Agreement contains several additional provisions that are directly relevant to Ironclad\'s lending relationship with Coastal Palms and its affiliated entities:

> 1\. **Franchise Surrender --- 14 Properties.** Coastal Palms is required to surrender its franchise rights to fourteen (14) of the twenty-two (22) hotel properties within one hundred twenty (120) days of the date of the Settlement Agreement. The de-identification deadline---by which all Verimark branding, signage, logos, proprietary systems, and reservation-system integrations must be removed from the surrendered properties---is August 20, 2024. The fourteen surrendered properties are located in the following markets: Sarasota, Florida (3 properties); Fort Myers, Florida (4 properties); Jacksonville, Florida (2 properties); Savannah, Georgia (3 properties); and Brunswick, Georgia (2 properties). Upon de-identification, these properties will no longer be authorized to operate under the Verimark Suites or Verimark Select brands, nor will they have access to the Verimark reservation system, loyalty program, or proprietary technology platforms.

> 2\. **Retained Properties --- 8 Properties.** Eight (8) hotel properties will be retained under new ten-year Franchise License Agreements executed contemporaneously with the Settlement Agreement. The retained properties are located in Naples, Florida (4 properties); Marco Island, Florida (2 properties); and Tampa, Florida (2 properties). The new Franchise License Agreements incorporate enhanced quarterly audit protocols, including mandatory engagement of an independent third-party auditor approved by Verimark, as well as real-time point-of-sale (\"POS\") integration requirements that provide Verimark with direct, contemporaneous access to transactional revenue data at each retained property.

> 3\. **Counterclaim Dismissal.** Coastal Palms\' Twelve Million Dollar (\$12,000,000.00) counterclaim, which alleged wrongful termination threats, tortious interference with business relationships, and unfair franchise practices, has been dismissed with prejudice pursuant to the terms of the Settlement Agreement.

> 4\. **Joint Stipulation of Dismissal.** A Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice was filed with the Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida, on April 26, 2024, and the Court is expected to enter an order of dismissal in due course.

**C. Confidentiality.** We note that the terms of the Settlement Agreement are subject to confidentiality provisions binding on all parties thereto, with limited exceptions. Among those exceptions are disclosures required (a) to Ironclad National Bank in its capacity as lender to Coastal Palms and its affiliated entities, as contemplated by Section 11.3 of the Settlement Agreement, and (b) by Verimark in connection with its disclosure obligations under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and the rules and regulations of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Verimark intends to file a Current Report on Form 8-K with the SEC disclosing the material terms of the settlement, which filing is expected to be made on or about April 26, 2024.
**[IV. Ironclad\'s Existing Loan Position]{.underline}**

We understand, based on publicly available information and representations made by Coastal Palms during the course of the litigation, that Ironclad National Bank holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) hotel properties in the Coastal Palms portfolio, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000.00). We further understand that you, Devon Schultz, serve as the Senior Vice President and Relationship Manager for the Coastal Palms commercial real estate lending relationship at Ironclad, and that you are the appropriate point of contact for communications regarding these loans.

We also understand that eight (8) of the twenty-two (22) properties in the Coastal Palms portfolio are not encumbered by Ironclad\'s existing first-lien mortgage loans. That is, these eight (8) properties are not subject to, and do not serve as collateral under, Ironclad\'s existing first-lien mortgage position. It is these eight (8) unencumbered properties that are the subject of the security interest described in Section V below.

To the extent that Ironclad\'s records reflect a different number of encumbered or unencumbered properties, or a different aggregate outstanding balance, we respectfully request that you notify us promptly so that we may reconcile any discrepancies with the information provided by Coastal Palms.
**[V. Verimark\'s Security Interest --- First-Priority Lien on the 8 Unencumbered Properties]{.underline}**
**A. Grant of Security Interest**

Pursuant to Section 7.1 of the Settlement Agreement, Coastal Palms has granted Verimark a first-priority security interest in the eight (8) hotel properties described above that are not encumbered by Ironclad\'s existing mortgage loans. This security interest was granted as collateral to secure Coastal Palms\' obligation to pay the Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$62,500,000.00) structured-payment balance, together with simple interest at six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum accruing on the outstanding balance, as described in Section III.A above.
**B. Appraised Value**

The aggregate appraised value of the eight (8) unencumbered properties, as determined by independent MAI-certified appraisals conducted within the ninety (90) days preceding the execution of the Settlement Agreement, is Seventy-One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$71,200,000.00). Copies of the appraisals are available upon request, subject to the confidentiality provisions of the Settlement Agreement.
**C. UCC-1 Financing Statement**

Verimark is in the process of perfecting this security interest by filing a UCC-1 Financing Statement with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry. The material particulars of the filing are as follows:
> **Debtor:** Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, FL 34108
> **Secured Party:** Verimark Hospitality Group Inc., 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33301

> **Collateral:** All right, title, and interest of the Debtor in and to the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties more particularly described in the Settlement Agreement, Exhibit F thereto, including without limitation all improvements, fixtures, furniture, furnishings, equipment, accounts, and general intangibles associated therewith.

In addition to the UCC-1 filing, Verimark intends to record mortgage instruments in the applicable county recording offices in the jurisdictions where the eight (8) unencumbered properties are situated, as contemplated by Section 7.2 of the Settlement Agreement.
**D. Personal Guaranties**

As additional security for the structured payments, personal guaranties have been executed by Randall Brecker and Nolan Prescott in favor of Verimark. These guaranties are absolute, unconditional, and irrevocable, and guarantee the full and timely payment of all structured-payment obligations, including accrued interest. The guaranties are governed by Florida law and contain standard provisions regarding waiver of defenses, consent to jurisdiction, and liability for costs and attorneys\' fees in the event of enforcement.
**E. Non-Interference with Ironclad\'s Lien Position**

We wish to make clear that Verimark\'s first-priority security interest pertains exclusively to the eight (8) hotel properties that are not encumbered by Ironclad\'s existing first-lien mortgages. Because these eight (8) properties are not subject to Ironclad\'s mortgage loans, Verimark\'s lien does not in any way affect, impair, subordinate, or interfere with Ironclad\'s security position on any of the eighteen (18) properties that serve as collateral under Ironclad\'s existing mortgage loans. Ironclad\'s first-lien position on those eighteen (18) properties remains unimpaired and unaffected by the Settlement Agreement and the security interest granted thereunder.

Verimark\'s lien is intended to be a first-priority lien with respect to the eight (8) unencumbered properties. To the extent that any other encumbrances, liens, or security interests of record may exist on one or more of those eight (8) properties, Verimark\'s lien would rank in priority in accordance with applicable Florida and Georgia law. Based on the representations and warranties made by Coastal Palms in the Settlement Agreement, Verimark believes that no such prior encumbrances exist.
**[VI. Impact on Coastal Palms\' Operations and Ironclad\'s Collateral]{.underline}**

We believe it is important to bring certain operational implications of the settlement to Ironclad\'s attention, as they may bear upon the Bank\'s assessment of its collateral position and the financial condition of Coastal Palms as borrower.
**A. Franchise Surrender --- Impact on Ironclad\'s Collateral**

As noted in Section III.B above, Coastal Palms is required to surrender franchise rights to fourteen (14) hotel properties and to complete de-identification by August 20, 2024. We understand that some or all of these fourteen surrendered properties may be among the eighteen (18) properties encumbered by Ironclad\'s mortgage loans. The de-identification of Verimark branding---including the removal of all exterior and interior signage, the disconnection from the Verimark central reservation system, the termination of access to the Verimark Rewards loyalty program, and the removal of proprietary technology systems---may have a material impact on the operating revenue and occupancy rates of those properties in the near term. Properties that lose their brand affiliation and access to a national reservation and loyalty platform may experience a meaningful decline in revenue per available room (\"RevPAR\"), which could in turn affect the debt-service coverage ratios and other financial covenants in Ironclad\'s loan documents with Coastal Palms.

We raise this point not to express a view on Ironclad\'s internal credit assessment, but rather to ensure that the Bank is fully informed of the settlement terms as they may relate to the value and income-producing capacity of Ironclad\'s collateral. We encourage Ironclad to consult with Coastal Palms and its counsel, Nathan Whitfield III of Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, regarding the operational transition plan for the surrendered properties.
**B. Retained Properties --- Continuity of Brand Affiliation**

The eight (8) retained properties---located in Naples, Marco Island, and Tampa---will continue operating under the Verimark brand under the terms of the new ten-year Franchise License Agreements. The enhanced audit protocols and real-time POS integration requirements applicable to the retained properties are designed to ensure full transparency and accurate reporting of GRR going forward. For those retained properties that are among the properties encumbered by Ironclad\'s mortgage loans, the continued Verimark brand affiliation should provide stability and continuity of revenue performance.
**C. Settlement Payment Obligations**

As previously noted, the Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000.00) closing payment has already been funded from the Ironclad escrow account. The ongoing structured payments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500.00) per semi-annual installment, together with accrued interest, will constitute ongoing payment obligations of Coastal Palms and the personal guarantors. These obligations should be taken into account in any assessment of Coastal Palms\' overall debt-service capacity and financial condition.
**[VII. Requests for Acknowledgment and Consent]{.underline}**
In light of the foregoing, Verimark respectfully requests that Ironclad National Bank provide written acknowledgment and, to the extent applicable, consent with respect to the following:

> 1\. **Receipt and Review.** Written acknowledgment that Ironclad has received and reviewed this notice regarding the settlement of *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC et al.*, Case No. 1021-00006, and the terms thereof as they affect Ironclad\'s lending relationship with Coastal Palms, including Verimark\'s first-priority security interest in the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties.

> 2\. **Confirmation of Unencumbered Status.** Written confirmation that the eight (8) properties subject to Verimark\'s first-priority lien, as described in Exhibit F to the Settlement Agreement and in Section V of this letter, are not encumbered by Ironclad\'s existing first-lien mortgage loans---that is, that these eight (8) properties do not serve as collateral under any Ironclad loan or credit facility.

> 3\. **Consent to Verimark\'s Lien.** To the extent that any provision in Ironclad\'s loan documents with Coastal Palms---including but not limited to any negative pledge covenant, negative lien covenant, or other restrictive covenant---requires the prior written consent of Ironclad as lender for the granting of additional liens or security interests on assets of the borrower or its affiliates, Verimark requests that Ironclad provide such written consent to Verimark\'s first-priority lien on the eight (8) unencumbered properties. Verimark believes, based on information available to it, that the eight (8) unencumbered properties may not fall within the scope of Ironclad\'s negative-pledge covenants; however, out of an abundance of caution and to avoid any ambiguity, Verimark requests Ironclad\'s affirmative consent.

Verimark is prepared to provide Ironclad with copies of the relevant settlement documents, including the Settlement Agreement (with appropriate redactions consistent with the confidentiality provisions thereof), the form of UCC-1 Financing Statement, the independent appraisals of the eight (8) unencumbered properties, and the personal guaranty agreements, upon Ironclad\'s request. Any such documents will be provided subject to applicable confidentiality protections, and Ironclad will be asked to execute a brief confidentiality acknowledgment prior to receipt of the full Settlement Agreement.
We respectfully request that Ironclad\'s written acknowledgment and consent be directed to the undersigned at the following address:
> Priya Anand, Esq. Calderwood & Harkness LLP 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800 Fort Lauderdale, FL 33301
> Email: panand@calderwoodharkness.com
We would appreciate receiving Ironclad\'s response within fifteen (15) business days of the date of this letter, or by May 15, 2024, whichever is later.
**[VIII. Confidentiality Notice]{.underline}**

As noted above, the settlement terms described in this letter are subject to confidentiality provisions under the Settlement Agreement. While disclosure to Ironclad in its capacity as lender to Coastal Palms is expressly permitted under Section 11.3 of the Settlement Agreement, Ironclad is requested to treat the information contained in this letter, and any settlement documents provided in connection herewith, as confidential. We ask that Ironclad limit the dissemination of this information to those officers, employees, attorneys, and advisors within Ironclad who have a bona fide need to know in connection with Ironclad\'s lending relationship with Coastal Palms and its affiliated entities. Any further disclosure by Ironclad of the settlement terms or related information should be made only as required by applicable law or regulation, or with the prior written consent of Verimark.
**[IX. Contact Information and Closing]{.underline}**

Should you have any questions regarding the matters addressed in this letter, or should you wish to discuss any aspect of the settlement, Verimark\'s security interest, or the operational implications described herein, please do not hesitate to contact me directly at the telephone number and email address listed below. I am available to arrange a call or meeting at your convenience, and I am prepared to facilitate the prompt exchange of any additional information or documentation that Ironclad may require.
> **Primary Contact:** Priya Anand, Partner Calderwood & Harkness LLP 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800 Fort Lauderdale, FL 33301 Telephone: (954) 761-8217
> Email: panand@calderwoodharkness.com
> FL Bar No. 0087451
In addition, should Ironclad prefer to communicate directly with Verimark\'s in-house legal team on any matter arising from this notice, the appropriate contact is:
> Renata Solis-Vega Senior Vice President & General Counsel Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100 Fort Lauderdale, FL 33301 Telephone: (954) 338-6400
> Email: rsolis-vega@verimarkhotels.com

We appreciate Ironclad\'s prompt attention to this matter and look forward to receiving the Bank\'s written acknowledgment and consent at your earliest convenience. Verimark values a constructive and transparent relationship with Ironclad, and we trust that the information provided herein will facilitate Ironclad\'s review of the settlement and its implications for the Bank\'s lending position.
Very truly yours,
CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP
Priya Anand Partner FL Bar No. 0087451 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800 Fort Lauderdale, FL 33301 Telephone: (954) 761-8217
Email: panand@calderwoodharkness.com
**cc:** (via electronic mail)

> Martin Holcomb, EVP & Chief Financial Officer, Verimark Hospitality Group Inc.

**Enclosures:** None enclosed herewith. Copies of the Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, draft UCC-1 Financing Statement, independent property appraisals, personal guaranty agreements, and related documents are available upon request, subject to applicable confidentiality provisions as described herein.

**[MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**
**Date:** April 26, 2024
**FROM:** Yuki Nakamura, Lead Associate, Litigation (General) Calderwood & Harkness LLP (FL Bar No. 0119644)
**TO:** Renata Solis-Vega, SVP & General Counsel, Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. Deidre Langston, SVP, Franchise Operations, Verimark Hospitality Group Inc.
**CC:** Priya Anand, Responsible Partner, Calderwood & Harkness LLP (FL Bar No. 0087451) Douglas Carmichael, Billing Partner, Calderwood & Harkness LLP (FL Bar No. 0093217)

**RE:** Post-Settlement Compliance Monitoring --- Recommended Internal Procedures for Monitoring Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC\'s Compliance with the Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release Dated April 22, 2024
**MATTER:** *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC et al.*, Case No. 1021-00006, Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida
**FILING REFERENCE:** Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice filed April 26, 2024; matter now closed at Calderwood & Harkness LLP
**[I. PURPOSE AND EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

This memorandum provides Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. (\"Verimark\" or \"VHG\") with a comprehensive framework of recommended internal procedures for monitoring Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC (\"Coastal Palms\" or \"CPFH\") and its principals\' compliance with the Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release executed on April 22, 2024 (the \"Settlement Agreement\"). While the litigation is now formally concluded --- the Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice having been filed with the Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida today --- Verimark\'s obligations and rights under the Settlement Agreement will extend for several years and require diligent, systematic monitoring to protect the Company\'s interests.

The Settlement Agreement resolved Verimark\'s approximately \$150 million breach-of-contract action arising from Coastal Palms\' systematic underreporting of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") over a nine-year period spanning from 2013 through 2021. As established through discovery and the Court\'s partial summary judgment ruling, Coastal Palms operated a revenue-diversion structure using its affiliated entity, Suncoast Room Management Inc., to collect direct bookings, retain a 12% management fee, and exclude those revenues from GRR reports submitted to Verimark. This conduct resulted in the underpayment of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees across Coastal Palms\' 22-hotel portfolio of approximately 3,740 total rooms.
The settlement was reached for a total value of **\$87.5 million**, comprised of the following components:
> • **\$25 million in cash at closing**, funded via wire transfer from an Ironclad National Bank escrow account on April 22, 2024 (receipt confirmed); and
> • **\$62.5 million in eight (8) semi-annual structured installments** of \$7,812,500 each, commencing October 22, 2024 and concluding April 22, 2028.
In addition to the monetary terms, the Settlement Agreement contains several critical non-monetary obligations requiring ongoing monitoring:

> • **Franchise Surrender of 14 Properties:** Fourteen of Coastal Palms\' 22 hotel properties will surrender their Verimark franchise, with a 120-day de-identification deadline of August 20, 2024 by which all Verimark branding, proprietary systems, and trademarks must be removed.

> • **Enhanced Audit Protocol for 8 Retained Properties:** The remaining eight properties will continue to operate under new 10-year Franchise License Agreements (\"FLAs\") subject to a significantly enhanced quarterly audit protocol for a minimum of five years.

> • **Personal Guaranties:** Randall Brecker (Managing Member, 60% equity interest in CPFH) and Nolan Prescott (Member, 25% equity interest in CPFH) have executed personal guaranties making them jointly and severally liable for all remaining structured-payment obligations.

> • **First-Priority Security Interest:** Verimark holds a first-priority security interest on eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties with an aggregate appraised value of \$71.2 million, secured by a UCC-1 Financing Statement filed with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry.
This memorandum is organized into five primary compliance-monitoring areas:
1\. **Structured Payment Tracking** (Section III)
2\. **Franchise Surrender and De-Identification Compliance** (Section IV)
3\. **Enhanced Audit Protocol for Retained Properties** (Section V)
4\. **Acceleration-Event Monitoring and Enforcement Triggers** (Section VI)
5\. **Ongoing Coordination with Calderwood & Harkness LLP** (Section VIII)

Additionally, the memorandum addresses Verimark\'s own obligations under the Settlement Agreement, particularly those relating to confidentiality and non-disparagement (Section VII), and provides a consolidated compliance calendar summarizing all key dates and milestones (Section IX).

We recommend designating a single internal compliance coordinator to oversee implementation of the procedures outlined herein and to serve as the central point of contact for all compliance-related matters. Given her role as Senior Vice President, Franchise Operations, and her familiarity with the Coastal Palms portfolio, we suggest that **Deidre Langston** serve as the lead compliance coordinator, with quarterly reporting to Renata Solis-Vega (SVP & General Counsel) and Martin Holcomb (EVP & Chief Financial Officer). This centralized structure will help ensure that no compliance deadlines or monitoring obligations fall through the cracks, and that any potential issues are escalated promptly and appropriately.
**[II. BACKGROUND AND SETTLEMENT OVERVIEW]{.underline}**
**A. Litigation Summary**

On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed its Complaint in the Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida, asserting ten (10) counts against Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, Suncoast Room Management Inc., Randall Brecker, and related entities. The counts included:
> • **Counts I--III:** Breach of Contract for underpayment of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees, respectively, under the Franchise License Agreements (\"FLAs\");
> • **Counts IV--V:** Fraudulent concealment and fraud in the inducement relating to Coastal Palms\' deliberate misrepresentation of GRR in its periodic financial reports to Verimark;
> • **Count VI:** Civil conspiracy involving Randall Brecker, Nolan Prescott, and Suncoast Room Management Inc. in the design and operation of the revenue-diversion scheme;

The total underreported GRR for this period was approximately **\$197.8 million**.

> **Partial pro-rata bonus:** Under Section 4.2 of the Employment Agreement, Aldrich was eligible for an annual discretionary performance bonus of up to 50% of base salary. Aldrich\'s last actual annual bonus was \$225,000 for fiscal year 2021 (paid in Q1 2022). For fiscal year 2022, Aldrich worked approximately 9.5 months (from January 1, 2022, through his October 14, 2022 termination) before being terminated. His pro-rata bonus for FY 2022, based on his FY 2021 bonus, would have been approximately \$225,000 × (9.5/12) = \$178,125, although the parties agreed to use the round figure of approximately \$168,750 as a reasonable estimate given the discretionary nature of the bonus. Of this amount, \$87,500 has been allocated to the wage component; the remainder is subsumed in the non-wage component as general settlement consideration, reflecting the inherent uncertainty as to whether a discretionary bonus would have been awarded at all for FY 2022 and, if so, in what amount.

The non-wage component of \$1,292,500 represents damages and settlement consideration that are not in the nature of compensation for services rendered by Aldrich to AMA. Rather, this component reflects the resolution of tort-based and contract-based claims, emotional distress damages, and general consideration for the broad mutual release of all claims between the parties. The non-wage component corresponds to the following elements:

> **General settlement consideration.** The non-wage component also includes consideration for Aldrich\'s release of all claims against AMA, its parent, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents. This release encompasses Aldrich\'s claims for: (i) wrongful termination in violation of public policy (Labor Code § 1102.5 retaliation theory); (ii) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (iii) declaratory relief regarding the enforceability of the 18-month post-employment restrictive covenant set forth in Section 10.3 of the Employment Agreement; and (iv) a claim for unreimbursed business expenses in the amount of \$28,400 (comprising travel, entertainment, and equipment expenses allegedly incurred by Aldrich during his final months of employment and not reimbursed by AMA). The value of Aldrich\'s release of these disparate claims --- particularly the declaratory relief claim, which, if successful, would have invalidated a restrictive covenant that AMA considers valuable --- is reflected in the non-wage component.

> **Lost future compensation (\$1,200,000 claimed).** Aldrich asserted in mediation that, as a result of AMA\'s wrongful termination and the \"for cause\" designation, he suffered \$1,200,000 in lost future compensation over a two-year horizon, reflecting the diminution in his earning capacity and the difficulty of obtaining comparable employment in the entertainment industry while bearing the stigma of a \"for cause\" termination. While lost future earnings are generally taxable as ordinary income to the recipient (whether or not characterized as wages), the parties have agreed to treat a portion of the lost future compensation claim as non-wage settlement consideration in the overall allocation. This treatment reflects the settlement\'s compromise nature: the \$1,200,000 claimed amount was disputed by AMA, Aldrich\'s mitigation efforts were contested, and the parties agreed to resolve the claim as part of a global settlement rather than separately valuing each component with precision. The characterization of a portion of lost future earnings as non-wage settlement consideration, rather than as wages, is supportable because the amounts are not attributable to services actually performed for AMA and are not severance or back pay in the traditional sense, but rather represent damages for the harm caused by the allegedly wrongful termination.

Because the non-wage component is not in the nature of \"wages\" as defined in IRC § 3401(a), it is **not subject to federal income tax withholding or FICA taxes**. The withholding obligation under IRC § 3402 applies only to \"wages\" --- that is, amounts paid for services rendered in an employer-employee relationship. Settlement payments that are in the nature of damages, general settlement consideration, or non-compensatory payments do not fall within the definition of wages, even if they are taxable income to the recipient. *See* Rev. Rul. 80-364, 1980-2 C.B. 294 (distinguishing between settlement payments that are wages subject to withholding and those that are not).

These are the types of damages that are properly characterized as non-wage settlement consideration.
